examples.english: Don't [assume] it will rain tomorrow before checking the weather.
examples.chinese: 先别[想当然地认为]明天会下雨，看看天气预报再说。

examples.english: She [assumed] he was tired because he kept yawning.
examples.chinese: 她[猜测]他累了，因为他一直打哈欠。

meanings.explanation: If you [assume] a role, position, or attitude, you start to have it or behave in that way.

examples.english: He will [assume] the role of team captain next season.
examples.chinese: 下个赛季他将[担任]队长。

examples.english: She [assumed] a confident smile before walking on stage.
examples.chinese: 上台前，她[露出]自信的微笑。

examples.english: The new teacher will [assume] her duties on Monday.
examples.chinese: 新老师将在周一[开始履行]她的职责。

meanings.explanation: If you [associate] one thing with another, you connect them together in your mind because they often appear together or are related.

examples.english: I always [associate] the smell of cookies with my grandmother's house.
examples.chinese: 我总是把饼干的香味和外婆家[联系]在一起。

examples.english: Many people [associate] blue skies with happy days.
examples.chinese: 很多人把蓝天和开心的日子[联系]起来。

examples.english: Don't [associate] me with him; we are just classmates.
examples.chinese: 别把我和他[联系]在一起，我们只是同学。

meanings.explanation: An [associate] is someone you work with, do business with, or spend time with, but who is not a close friend.

examples.english: My dad went to a meeting with his business [associate].
examples.chinese: 我爸爸和他的业务[伙伴]一起去开会了。

examples.english: She is just a work [associate], not my best friend.
examples.chinese: 她只是我的工作[同事]，不是我最好的朋友。

examples.english: The store owner asked his [associate] to help the customers.
examples.chinese: 店主让他的[助手]去帮助顾客。

meanings.explanation: An [athlete] is someone who is good at sports and physical activities, especially someone who competes in sports events.

examples.english: Sarah is a fast [athlete] who loves to run races at school.
examples.chinese: 萨拉是一名跑得很快的[运动员]，她喜欢在学校参加赛跑。

examples.english: My big brother wants to be a [athlete] when he grows up.
examples.chinese: 我哥哥长大后想成为一名[运动员]。

examples.english: The [athlete] jumped very high and won the gold medal.
examples.chinese: 这位[运动员]跳得很高，赢得了金牌。

meanings.explanation: If you [attend] an event such as a meeting, a class, or a party, you go to it and are present there.

examples.english: I will [attend] the school sports day next Friday.
examples.chinese: 下周五我要[参加]学校的运动会。

examples.english: All students must [attend] the morning assembly.
examples.chinese: 所有学生都必须[参加]早会。

examples.english: My mom didn't [attend] the parent-teacher meeting yesterday.
examples.chinese: 我妈妈昨天没有[出席]家长会。

meanings.explanation: If you [attend] to someone or something, you give them your care and attention, or you deal with what they need.

examples.english: The nurse will [attend] to you in a minute.
examples.chinese: 护士马上就来[照顾]你。

examples.english: Please wait a moment — I need to [attend] to this customer first.
examples.chinese: 请稍等一下——我需要先[接待]这位顾客。

examples.english: Dad is [attending] to a broken pipe in the kitchen.
examples.chinese: 爸爸正在[处理]厨房里一根破裂的水管。

meanings.explanation: If people [assimilate] into a society or group, they gradually become part of that society and stop being noticeably different.

examples.english: The new students tried to [assimilate] into the class quickly.
examples.chinese: 这些新学生努力[融入]班级。

examples.english: Many immigrants want to [assimilate] into their new country.
examples.chinese: 许多移民想要[融入]他们的新国家。

examples.english: It takes time for refugees to [assimilate] into the local community.
examples.chinese: 难民需要时间才能[融入]当地社区。

meanings.explanation: If you [assimilate] information or ideas, you understand and remember it fully.

examples.english: Children can [assimilate] new words very fast.
examples.chinese: 孩子们能很快[吸收掌握]新单词。

examples.english: She read the book twice to [assimilate] all the ideas.
examples.chinese: 她把书看了两遍，以便[融会贯通]所有观点。

examples.english: The teacher helped students [assimilate] the difficult concepts.
examples.chinese: 老师帮助学生[理解吸收]这些难懂的概念。

meanings.explanation: An [assessment] is a process of judging or evaluating the quality, ability, or importance of someone or something.

examples.english: Our teacher gave us a short [assessment] at the end of the week.
examples.chinese: 我们老师在周末给我们做了一次简短[测评]。

examples.english: The coach did an [assessment] of my soccer skills before I joined the team.
examples.chinese: 教练在我入队前对我的足球技术做了一次[评估]。

examples.english: My mom's [assessment] of the new movie was that it's very fun.
examples.chinese: 我妈妈对这部新电影的[评价]是非常好看。

meanings.explanation: An [assessment] is an official calculation of the value of property for tax purposes.

examples.english: The tax worker finished the [assessment] of our new house.
examples.chinese: 税务人员完成了对我们新房子的[估价]。

examples.english: The new [assessment] says we need to pay a little more tax this year.
examples.chinese: 新的[评估]显示我们今年需要多交一点税。

examples.english: Dad went to the office to ask about the property [assessment].
examples.chinese: 爸爸去办公室询问了房产[估价]的事情。

meanings.explanation: If something is done [artificially], it is made or produced by human beings rather than occurring naturally.

examples.english: This candy is [artificially] flavored.
examples.chinese: 这颗糖果是[人工]调味的。

examples.english: Many winter vegetables are [artificially] grown.
examples.chinese: 很多冬季蔬菜都是[人工]种植的。

examples.english: The lake in the park is [artificially] made.
examples.chinese: 公园里的这个湖是[人工]建造的。

meanings.explanation: If a behavior or feeling is [artificially] produced, it is not genuine, natural, or spontaneous.

examples.english: She [artificially] laughed at her boss's boring joke.
examples.chinese: 她对老板无聊的笑话[假惺惺地]笑了。

examples.english: He [artificially] acted happy to see his guest.
examples.chinese: 他[不自然地]对客人表现得很开心。

examples.english: The welcome at the party felt [artificially] warm.
examples.chinese: 聚会上的欢迎显得[刻意地]热情。

meanings.explanation: An [association] is an organized group of people who share the same interest, job, or activity.

examples.english: My sister joined the photography [association] at her school.
examples.chinese: 我姐姐加入了她学校的摄影[协会]。

examples.english: The local bakers formed an [association] to support each other.
examples.chinese: 当地面包师成立了一个[协会]来互相支持。

examples.english: Our city's sports [association] is hosting a basketball game this weekend.
examples.chinese: 我们市的体育[协会]这周末要举办一场篮球比赛。

meanings.explanation: An [association] is a connection, relationship, or mental link between things, people, or ideas.

examples.english: Scientists found a strong [association] between exercise and good health.
examples.chinese: 科学家发现运动和健康之间存在紧密[关联]。

examples.english: I have happy [associations] with my grandma's house.
examples.chinese: 奶奶的房子给我留下很多美好[联想]。

examples.english: She keeps a close [association] with her high school friends.
examples.chinese: 她和高中朋友保持着密切[交往]。

meanings.explanation: If you [assist] someone, you help them do something or make their work easier.

examples.english: Can you [assist] me with my homework?
examples.chinese: 你能[帮]我做作业吗？

examples.english: The kind girl stopped to [assist] the old man cross the street.
examples.chinese: 那个善良的女孩停下来[帮助]老爷爷过马路。

examples.english: Please [assist] your little brother with putting on his shoes.
examples.chinese: 请[帮]弟弟把鞋穿上。

meanings.explanation: In sports such as basketball and soccer, an [assist] is a pass that helps another player on your team score a goal or basket.

examples.english: He got five [assists] in yesterday's basketball game.
examples.chinese: 他在昨天的篮球比赛中送出了五次[助攻]。

examples.english: Good players know how to make great [assists] for their teammates.
examples.chinese: 好的球员知道如何为队友送出漂亮的[助攻]。

examples.english: She had the most [assists] on the team this season.
examples.chinese: 她这个赛季在队里的[助攻]数是最多的。

meanings.explanation: Something or someone that is [attractive] has qualities that make you notice them or want to be near them, especially because they are visually pleasing.

examples.english: She is an [attractive] woman with a warm smile.
examples.chinese: 她是一位笑容亲切的[有魅力]女性。

examples.english: This park has an [attractive] garden full of colorful flowers.
examples.chinese: 这个公园有一个开满五颜六色花朵的[迷人]花园。

examples.english: He found the job [attractive] because of the high salary.
examples.chinese: 他觉得这份工作[吸引人]，因为工资很高。

meanings.explanation: An [attractive] offer or price is very good and worth accepting, often better than usual.

examples.english: The store has an [attractive] discount this week.
examples.chinese: 这家店这周有[很划算的]折扣。

examples.english: They made an [attractive] offer to buy the house.
examples.chinese: 他们提出了一个[诱人]的买房报价。

examples.english: This is an [attractive] deal for both sides.
examples.chinese: 这是一个对双方都[很有吸引力]的交易。

meanings.explanation: If you [avoid] something, you stay away from it or stop yourself from doing it.

examples.english: I always [avoid] the busy road on my way to school.
examples.chinese: 我上学路上总是[避开]那条很挤的路。

examples.english: She tried to [avoid] eating too much candy.
examples.chinese: 她尽量[避免]吃太多糖。

examples.english: He turned around to [avoid] his friend in the hallway.
examples.chinese: 他转过身去，[躲开]走廊里的朋友。

meanings.explanation: If you [avoid] a topic or person, you do not talk about it or keep your distance from them.

examples.english: Mom always [avoids] talking about the messy room.
examples.chinese: 妈妈总是[回避]谈论那个乱糟糟的房间。

examples.english: He [avoids] the neighbor's dog because it barks a lot.
examples.chinese: 他尽量[远离]邻居家的狗，因为它老叫。

examples.english: They [avoid] that restaurant because the food is too spicy.
examples.chinese: 他们尽量[不去]那家餐厅，因为菜太辣了。

meanings.explanation: If something is [available], you are able to get it, buy it, or use it.

examples.english: The new toys will be [available] in the store next week.
examples.chinese: 这些新玩具下周会在商店里[有售]。

examples.english: There are many [available] seats on the bus.
examples.chinese: 公交车上还有很多[空余的]座位。

examples.english: Free water is [available] at the park entrance.
examples.chinese: 公园入口处[提供]免费饮用水。

meanings.explanation: If a person is [available], they have enough time to talk to you or do something.

examples.english: Is your mom [available] to talk on the phone?
examples.chinese: 你妈妈现在[有空]接电话吗？

examples.english: The teacher is [available] after class to help students.
examples.chinese: 这位老师课后[有空]帮助学生。

examples.english: I am not [available] on Saturday because I have a game.
examples.chinese: 我周六没[空]，因为我要参加比赛。

meanings.explanation: Someone who is [assured] is confident and certain about their own abilities or decisions.

examples.english: She gave an [assured] smile when answering the teacher's questions.
examples.chinese: 她回答老师问题时露出了[自信]的微笑。

examples.english: The young man spoke in an [assured] voice during the interview.
examples.chinese: 面试时这个年轻男士说话的语气很[自信]。

examples.english: He walked onto the stage looking calm and [assured].
examples.chinese: 他走上舞台时看起来沉着[自信]。

meanings.explanation: If something is [assured], it is certain to happen; guaranteed.

examples.english: The doctor said her recovery was [assured] with proper rest.
examples.chinese: 医生说好好休息的话，她的康复是[肯定]的。

examples.english: Our team is [assured] of victory after winning the first two games.
examples.chinese: 赢了前两场后，我们队[稳操胜券]。

examples.english: Success in the final exam is [assured] if you study hard every day.
examples.chinese: 如果你每天都努力学习，期末考试[一定]能取得好成绩。

meanings.explanation: [Arithmetic] is the part of mathematics that involves basic operations such as adding, subtracting, multiplying, and dividing numbers.

examples.english: I like [arithmetic] because it is fun.
examples.chinese: 我喜欢[算术]，因为它很有趣。

examples.english: We have an [arithmetic] test tomorrow.
examples.chinese: 我们明天有个[算术]测验。

examples.english: My brother is doing his [arithmetic] homework.
examples.chinese: 我弟弟正在做[算术]作业。

meanings.explanation: An [attack] is an act of using violence to try to hurt, damage, or kill someone or something.

examples.english: The soldiers fought off the enemy's [attack].
examples.chinese: 士兵们击退了敌人的[进攻]。

examples.english: My grandpa was sent to hospital after a heart [attack].
examples.chinese: 我爷爷心脏病[发作]后被送去了医院。

examples.english: A sudden [attack] by the wolf scared all the sheep.
examples.chinese: 狼的突然[袭击]吓坏了所有的羊。

meanings.explanation: If you [attack] someone or something, you use violence to try to hurt, damage, or defeat them.

examples.english: The wolf will [attack] sheep when it's hungry.
examples.chinese: 狼饿的时候会[袭击]羊群。

examples.english: The enemy will [attack] our town early tomorrow morning.
examples.chinese: 敌人明天一大早会[进攻]我们的城镇。

examples.english: Never [attack] a dog when it is sleeping.
examples.chinese: 永远不要在狗睡觉的时候[攻击]它。

meanings.explanation: If something will [assuredly] happen, it will definitely happen.

examples.english: The sun will [assuredly] rise tomorrow morning.
examples.chinese: 太阳明天早上[肯定]会升起。

examples.english: If you practice every day, you will [assuredly] get better at playing the piano.
examples.chinese: 如果你每天练习，你弹钢琴的水平[肯定]会提高。

examples.english: The little dog [assuredly] knows the way back home.
examples.chinese: 那只小狗[肯定]认识回家的路。

meanings.explanation: If you do something [assuredly], you do it in a confident way.

examples.english: She answered the teacher's question [assuredly] in front of the whole class.
examples.chinese: 她在全班同学面前[自信地]回答了老师的问题。

examples.english: The captain walked [assuredly] onto the big ship.
examples.chinese: 船长[自信地]走上那艘大船。

examples.english: He [assuredly] climbed to the top of the tall tree.
examples.chinese: 他[自信地]爬到了那棵大树的顶端。

meanings.explanation: A [battle] is a fight between armies or between groups of people, or it can also mean a long struggle to achieve something or deal with a problem.

examples.english: The two armies had a big [battle] near the river.
examples.chinese: 两支军队在河边打了一场大[仗]。

examples.english: She is fighting a [battle] against illness.
examples.chinese: 她正在和疾病进行一场[斗争]。

examples.english: The kids had a [battle] over who got the last piece of cake.
examples.chinese: 孩子们为了最后一块蛋糕[争抢]了一番。

meanings.explanation: If you [battle] with someone or something, you fight against them, or you try hard to deal with a difficult situation.

examples.english: The doctor [battled] to save the sick child.
examples.chinese: 医生全力[抢救]那个生病的孩子。

examples.english: He has [battled] this cold for a whole week.
examples.chinese: 他和这场感冒[抗争]了整整一个星期。

examples.english: The team [battled] hard and finally won the game.
examples.chinese: 全队奋力[拼搏]，最终赢得了比赛。

meanings.explanation: An [award] is a prize or reward that someone gets for doing something very well.

examples.english: She won the first [award] in the painting competition.
examples.chinese: 她在绘画比赛中获得了第一名[奖项]。

examples.english: The movie won an [award] for best music.
examples.chinese: 这部电影获得了最佳音乐[奖]。

examples.english: My teacher got a special [award] for her hard work.
examples.chinese: 我的老师因为工作努力得了一个特别[奖]。

meanings.explanation: If you [award] something to someone, you officially give it to them as a prize or payment.

examples.english: The judges will [award] a prize to the best singer.
examples.chinese: 评委们会把奖品[颁发]给最棒的歌手。

examples.english: The school [awarded] him a medal for his bravery.
examples.chinese: 学校因他的勇敢[授予]了他一枚奖章。

examples.english: They [awarded] her the trophy for first place.
examples.chinese: 他们[颁给]她第一名的奖杯。

meanings.explanation: A [barrier] is a physical fence, wall, or gate that stops people or things from moving freely from one place to another.

examples.english: There is a [barrier] between the road and the playground to keep children safe.
examples.chinese: 马路和操场之间有一道[护栏]，用来保护孩子们的安全。

examples.english: We put a [barrier] around the garden to keep the rabbits out.
examples.chinese: 我们在花园周围设了[围栏]来挡住兔子。

examples.english: The police set up [barriers] to control the crowd at the concert.
examples.chinese: 警察在音乐会现场设置了[路障]来控制人群。

meanings.explanation: A [barrier] is also a problem or situation that stops progress, communication, or understanding between people.

examples.english: Learning a new language can be a [barrier] at first, but practice helps.
examples.chinese: 刚开始学新语言可能会是一道[难关]，但练习会有帮助。

examples.english: We need to break down the [barriers] between us and talk more often.
examples.chinese: 我们需要打破彼此之间的[隔阂]，多交流交流。

examples.english: Money should not be a [barrier] to getting a good education.
examples.chinese: 金钱不应该是获得良好教育的[障碍]。

meanings.explanation: If you are [aware] of something, you know about it or realize that it is present or happening.

examples.english: I wasn't [aware] of the time when I was reading my book.
examples.chinese: 我看书的时候没[注意到]时间。

examples.english: Are you [aware] that tomorrow is a holiday?
examples.chinese: 你[知道]明天是假日吗？

examples.english: My cat is always [aware] of every little sound in the house.
examples.chinese: 我的猫咪对家里的每一点声响都很[敏感]。

meanings.explanation: If you are [aware], you are concerned about and well-informed about important issues and developments in the world around you.

examples.english: My teacher is very [aware] of environmental problems.
examples.chinese: 我的老师非常[关注]环境问题。

examples.english: We should all be more [aware] of keeping our neighborhood clean.
examples.chinese: 我们都应该更[有意识到]保持社区清洁的重要性。

examples.english: Many young people today are politically [aware].
examples.chinese: 如今许多年轻人对政治[很关注]。

meanings.explanation: A [band] is a group of people, especially musicians, who play music together.

examples.english: My brother plays guitar in a [band].
examples.chinese: 我哥哥在一个[乐队]里弹吉他。

examples.english: She wants to start a [band] with her friends.
examples.chinese: 她想和朋友们一起组建一支[乐队]。

examples.english: The [band] played great music at the school party.
examples.chinese: [乐队]在学校晚会上演奏了很棒的音乐。

meanings.explanation: A [band] is a flat strip or loop of material that is used for fastening, holding, or decorating things.

examples.english: She always wears a [band] in her hair.
examples.chinese: 她总是在头发上戴一个[带子]。

examples.english: I use a [band] to hold my cards together.
examples.chinese: 我用一个[带子]把卡片绑在一起。

examples.english: He wears a [band] on his wrist when running.
examples.chinese: 他跑步时手腕上戴着一条[带子]。

derived_forms: battlefield (adjective, used in compounds like battlefield conditions)

meanings.explanation: A [battlefield] is an area of land where a battle is fought, especially in the past.

examples.english: Many soldiers died on this [battlefield].
examples.chinese: 很多士兵在这个[战场]上牺牲了。

examples.english: We visited the historic [battlefield] last weekend.
examples.chinese: 上周末我们参观了这个历史[战场]。

examples.english: The [battlefield] is now a peaceful museum.
examples.chinese: 这个[战场]现在是一个和平博物馆。

meanings.explanation: You can describe any place where people compete or fight very hard as a [battlefield].

examples.english: The office can feel like a [battlefield] sometimes.
examples.chinese: 办公室有时候会像[战场]一样。

examples.english: The soccer field was a [battlefield] after the match.
examples.chinese: 足球赛结束后，球场简直成了[战场]。

examples.english: Love is a [battlefield], you need to be strong.
examples.chinese: 爱情就像一个[战场]，你需要变得坚强。

meanings.explanation: If someone or something is [average], they are ordinary, neither very good nor very bad, and not particularly special.

examples.english: He's just an [average] kid who loves playing soccer after school.
examples.chinese: 他只是个喜欢放学后踢足球的[普通]孩子。

examples.english: The cake tastes [average]—it's not super delicious but it's okay.
examples.chinese: 这个蛋糕味道[一般]，不算特别好吃但也不难吃。

examples.english: My running speed is pretty [average] at school.
examples.chinese: 我在学校的跑步速度相当[一般]。

meanings.explanation: The [average] of a set of numbers is the result you get when you add all the numbers together and divide by the number of numbers.

examples.english: The [average] of 2, 4 and 6 is 4.
examples.chinese: 2、4和6的[平均值]是4。

examples.english: We worked out the [average] of all our test scores.
examples.chinese: 我们算出了所有测试分数的[平均值]。

examples.english: The [average] of daily temperatures last July was 28 degrees.
examples.chinese: 去年七月每日气温的[平均值]是28度。

meanings.explanation: A [basic] fact, idea, or skill is the most essential one that everything else depends on.

examples.english: We need to learn [basic] math first before solving hard problems.
examples.chinese: 在解难题之前，我们需要先学习[基础的]数学。

examples.english: Food and water are [basic] needs for all people.
examples.chinese: 食物和水是所有人[基本的]需求。

examples.english: My mom taught me some [basic] cooking skills.
examples.chinese: 我妈妈教了我一些[基础的]烹饪技巧。

meanings.explanation: A [basic] thing is simple and does not have any extra features or detailed changes.

examples.english: This cheap phone only has [basic] functions.
examples.chinese: 这款便宜的手机只有[基本的]功能。

examples.english: We stayed at a [basic] cabin in the mountain.
examples.chinese: 我们住在山上一间[简易的]小木屋里。

examples.english: She has a [basic] understanding of this question.
examples.chinese: 她对这个问题有[初步的]了解。

meanings.explanation: If you [believe] something, you think it is true, even though you cannot be completely certain.

examples.english: I [believe] that the sun will rise tomorrow.
examples.chinese: 我[相信]太阳明天会升起。

examples.english: She [believes] his story is true.
examples.chinese: 她[相信]他讲的事情是真的。

examples.english: Do you [believe] in ghosts?
examples.chinese: 你[相信]有鬼吗？

meanings.explanation: If you [believe] in a religion or God, you are sure that God or the religion is real.

examples.english: My grandmother [believes] in God.
examples.chinese: 我奶奶[信奉]上帝。

examples.english: He [believes] in Buddhism.
examples.chinese: 他[信仰]佛教。

examples.english: She goes to church because she [believes].
examples.chinese: 她去做礼拜因为她[有信仰]。

meanings.explanation: If someone is [assaulting] another person, they are physically attacking them in a violent way.

examples.english: The video shows two men [assaulting] a store owner during the robbery.
examples.chinese: 视频显示两名男子在抢劫过程中[袭击]店主。

examples.english: He was sent to prison for [assaulting] a security guard.
examples.chinese: 他因为[攻击]保安而被送进监狱。

examples.english: The bully was caught on camera [assaulting] another student.
examples.chinese: 那个恶霸被摄像头拍到正在[殴打]另一名学生。

meanings.explanation: If a loud noise, strong smell, or a lot of questions are [assaulting] you, they are affecting you in a very strong and unpleasant way.

examples.english: The loud music from the party was [assaulting] our ears all night.
examples.chinese: 派对上传来的巨大音乐声整晚都在[刺激]我们的耳朵。

examples.english: The reporters kept [assaulting] the famous singer with questions.
examples.chinese: 记者们不停地用问题[轰炸]那位著名歌手。

examples.english: When we walked into the kitchen, the strong smell was [assaulting] my nose.
examples.chinese: 我们走进厨房时，浓烈的气味直[冲]我的鼻子。

meanings.explanation: A [belief] is an idea that you think is true, especially about life, religion, or the world.

examples.english: Her [belief] in fairies makes her bedtime stories very fun.
examples.chinese: 她对仙女的[信念]让她的睡前故事特别有趣。

examples.english: My grandpa has a strong [belief] that fresh air is good for health.
examples.chinese: 我爷爷坚信新鲜空气对身体好，这个[信念]特别强。

examples.english: People in that village share the [belief] that helping others brings good luck.
examples.chinese: 那个村子里的人们都有一个共同的[信念]：帮助别人会带来好运。

meanings.explanation: A [belief] is also a feeling that something is true or that someone is trustworthy, without needing proof.

examples.english: I have a [belief] that my best friend will always help me.
examples.chinese: 我[相信]我最好的朋友永远都会帮我的。

examples.english: His [belief] in his team helped them win the game.
examples.chinese: 他对团队的[信任]帮助他们赢得了比赛。

examples.english: Mom's [belief] in me gives me courage to try new things.
examples.chinese: 妈妈对我的[信任]给了我尝试新事物的勇气。

meanings.explanation: Something that is [arguable] can be discussed and debated because it is not obviously true or certain.

examples.english: It is [arguable] that there is life on other planets.
examples.chinese: [可以论证]其他星球上存在生命。

examples.english: His guilt is [arguable] because the evidence is weak.
examples.chinese: 他的罪行[有争议]，因为证据不足。

examples.english: Whether the weather is good today is [arguable].
examples.chinese: 今天的天气好不好[有待商榷]。

meanings.explanation: If something is [arguable], it seems reasonable or likely to be true, though not proven for certain.

examples.english: Your idea sounds [arguable] and makes sense.
examples.chinese: 你的想法听起来[有道理]，符合逻辑。

examples.english: It seems [arguable] that she finished the work by herself.
examples.chinese: [看起来可信]她是独自完成工作的。

examples.english: His excuse was [arguable] but still hard to believe.
examples.chinese: 他的借口[勉强说得过去]，但仍然让人难以相信。

meanings.explanation: If you [bite] something, you use your teeth to cut into it or grip it.

examples.english: The puppy likes to [bite] his toy bone.
examples.chinese: 小狗喜欢[咬]他的玩具骨头。

examples.english: Be careful not to [bite] your tongue when eating.
examples.chinese: 吃东西时要小心别[咬]到舌头。

examples.english: The hungry boy took a big [bite] of his sandwich.
examples.chinese: 那个饿坏了的男孩[咬]了一大口三明治。

meanings.explanation: A [bite] is a small amount of food that you put in your mouth at one time, or an injury caused by an animal or insect using its teeth or mouth.

examples.english: May I have a [bite] of your apple?
examples.chinese: 我能[尝]一口你的苹果吗？

examples.english: The doctor looked at the mosquito [bite] on my arm.
examples.chinese: 医生看了看我手臂上的蚊子[包]。

examples.english: She took another small [bite] of cake.
examples.chinese: 她又[咬]了一小口蛋糕。

meanings.explanation: A [bargain] is something that you buy at a lower price than its normal value, so you feel you have made a good deal.

examples.english: I found a real [bargain] at the second-hand shop yesterday.
examples.chinese: 我昨天在二手店淘到了一个[便宜货]。

examples.english: This dress was such a [bargain] — it only cost five dollars.
examples.chinese: 这条裙子真是个[便宜货]——才五美元。

examples.english: She knows how to find [bargains] at the weekend market.
examples.chinese: 她知道怎么在周末市场淘到[便宜货]。

meanings.explanation: If you [bargain], you discuss the price of something with someone in order to get a lower price.

examples.english: My mother likes to [bargain] at the vegetable market.
examples.chinese: 我妈妈喜欢在菜市场[讨价还价]。

examples.english: He [bargained] with the seller and got ten dollars off.
examples.chinese: 他和卖家[讲价]，少了十美元。

examples.english: You should [bargain] for souvenirs when you visit the night market.
examples.chinese: 你去夜市买纪念品时应该[讲价]。

meanings.explanation: A [bombardment] is a continued attack by dropping many bombs or firing many shells, often used during wars.

examples.english: The city was under [bombardment] for several days.
examples.chinese: 这座城市连续几天遭到[轰炸]。

examples.english: The newspaper reported on the recent [bombardment] in the area.
examples.chinese: 报纸报道了该地区最近的[轰炸]情况。

examples.english: The [bombardment] destroyed many buildings near the coast.
examples.chinese: [轰炸]摧毁了海岸附近的许多建筑。

meanings.explanation: If you [break] something, you damage it so that it is in pieces or no longer works properly.

examples.english: Be careful not to [break] the glass.
examples.chinese: 小心别把玻璃杯[打碎]了。

examples.english: She dropped her phone and [broke] the screen.
examples.chinese: 她把手机摔了，[摔坏]了屏幕。

examples.english: Don't [break] the toy — it's my favorite!
examples.chinese: 别把玩具[弄坏]了——那是我最喜欢的！

meanings.explanation: A [break] is a short period of time when you stop what you are doing to rest or eat.

examples.english: Let's take a short [break] and eat some snacks.
examples.chinese: 我们[休息]一小会儿，吃点零食吧。

examples.english: We had a lunch [break] at twelve o'clock.
examples.chinese: 我们十二点钟有一个午[休]时间。

examples.english: After a long [break], he went back to studying.
examples.chinese: 经过长[假]之后，他又回去学习了。

meanings.explanation: An [authoritative] person or thing gives an impression of power and importance and is likely to be obeyed.

examples.english: The captain's [authoritative] voice made everyone feel safe.
examples.chinese: 船长[威严]的声音让每个人都感到安心。

examples.english: My dad can be very [authoritative] when he tells me to clean my room.
examples.chinese: 我爸叫我打扫房间的时候，口气特别[威严]。

examples.english: The judge spoke in an [authoritative] tone during the trial.
examples.chinese: 法官在庭审中用[威严]的语气说话。

meanings.explanation: Information or a source that is [authoritative] is trusted because it comes from an expert and is considered to be true and reliable.

examples.english: This book is an [authoritative] guide to dinosaurs.
examples.chinese: 这本书是恐龙方面的[权威]指南。

examples.english: Always get information from [authoritative] sources.
examples.chinese: 获取信息要认准[权威]来源。

examples.english: Our teacher gave us an [authoritative] answer to the science question.
examples.chinese: 老师给了我们一个[权威]的科学解答。

meanings.explanation: Something that is [boundless] has no limits or boundaries; it seems to go on forever.

examples.english: The little girl has [boundless] energy and loves to run and play all day.
examples.chinese: 这个小女孩有[无穷的]精力，喜欢整天跑啊玩啊。

examples.english: The desert looked [boundless], with sand stretching as far as we could see.
examples.chinese: 这片沙漠看起来[无边无际]，沙子一直延伸到我们视线所及的地方。

examples.english: My grandmother shows [boundless] kindness to everyone she meets.
examples.chinese: 我奶奶对她遇到的每个人都表现出[无限的]善意。

meanings.explanation: If something is [bound] to happen, it is certain or very likely to happen.

examples.english: You are [bound] to feel a little nervous on your first day of school.
examples.chinese: 你上学第一天[肯定会]有点紧张。

examples.english: It is [bound] to rain later, so bring your umbrella.
examples.chinese: 一会儿[肯定]会下雨，带上伞吧。

examples.english: If you practice every day, you are [bound] to get better at playing the piano.
examples.chinese: 如果你每天都练习，你弹钢琴[肯定会]越来越好的。

meanings.explanation: A [bound] is a limit or edge of something that should not be crossed.

examples.english: Please keep your ball inside the [bounds] of the playground.
examples.chinese: 请让你的球保持在操场的[范围]内。

examples.english: His curiosity knows no [bounds]; he asks questions about everything.
examples.chinese: 他的好奇心永无止[境]，什么事他都要问。

examples.english: You must stay within the [bounds] of good manners at the dinner table.
examples.chinese: 吃饭时你必须遵守礼貌的[界限]。

meanings.explanation: Something that is [breakable] can be easily broken or damaged.

examples.english: This glass cup is [breakable], so be careful.
examples.chinese: 这个玻璃杯[易碎的]，小心点。

examples.english: Please put all [breakable] items in the safe.
examples.chinese: 请把所有[易碎的]物品放到安全的地方。

examples.english: The kids should not touch those [breakable] decorations.
examples.chinese: 孩子们不应该碰那些[易碎的]装饰品。

meanings.explanation: A [bruise] is a dark mark on your skin that appears after you have been hit or bumped, because blood has leaked under the skin.

examples.english: She fell off her bike and got a big [bruise] on her knee.
examples.chinese: 她从自行车上摔下来，膝盖上磕了一大块[淤青]。

examples.english: My little brother has a [bruise] on his arm from playing football.
examples.chinese: 我弟弟踢足球时胳膊上弄了一块[淤青]。

examples.english: Mom put some ice on the [bruise] to make it feel better.
examples.chinese: 妈妈在[淤青]上敷了点冰，让它好受一些。

meanings.explanation: If you [bruise] a part of your body, or if something bruises you, you get a dark mark on your skin because of a bump or hit.

examples.english: Be careful with that door — it almost [bruised] my toe!
examples.chinese: 小心那扇门——差点把我的脚趾磕[青]了！

examples.english: He [bruised] his hand when he punched the wall.
examples.chinese: 他打墙的时候把手给[磕青]了。

examples.english: I [bruise] easily, so I always wear knee pads when I skate.
examples.chinese: 我皮肤很容易[淤青]，所以滑冰时总会戴上护膝。

meanings.explanation: If you [beat] something, you hit it repeatedly with force, often in order to do something such as prepare food or make a sound.

examples.english: My mom needs to [beat] the eggs before making the cake.
examples.chinese: 妈妈做蛋糕前需要[打]鸡蛋。

examples.english: The drummer will [beat] the drum loudly in the parade.
examples.chinese: 鼓手会在游行中用力[打]鼓。

examples.english: The heavy rain [beat] against our window this morning.
examples.chinese: 今天早上大雨[打]在我们的窗户上。

meanings.explanation: If you [beat] someone in a game, race, or competition, you defeat them and finish ahead of them.

examples.english: Our team [beat] their team in the basketball game last week.
examples.chinese: 我们队在上周的篮球比赛中[打败]了他们队。

examples.english: I [beat] my big brother at hide-and-seek yesterday.
examples.chinese: 我昨天捉迷藏[赢]了我哥哥。

examples.english: She [beat] all the other runners in the race.
examples.chinese: 她在赛跑中[打败]了所有其他选手。

meanings.explanation: To [build] means to construct something by putting parts together, especially to make a house, structure, or something physical.

examples.english: My dad helped me [build] a tree house in the backyard.
examples.chinese: 我爸爸帮我[搭建]了一个树屋。

examples.english: The children love to [build] sandcastles on the beach.
examples.chinese: 孩子们喜欢在海滩上[堆]沙堡。

examples.english: They are going to [build] a new library in our town.
examples.chinese: 他们要在我们镇上[建造]一个新图书馆。

meanings.explanation: To [build] also means to develop or increase something gradually, such as strength, skills, or confidence.

examples.english: Running every day helped me [build] up my stamina.
examples.chinese: 每天跑步帮我[增强]了耐力。

examples.english: She worked hard to [build] a successful career.
examples.chinese: 她努力[建立]了一番成功的事业。

examples.english: We need to [build] more trust between us.
examples.chinese: 我们需要[建立]更多的信任。

meanings.explanation: To [bury] something means to put it into a hole in the ground and cover it with earth.

examples.english: The dog likes to [bury] his bone in the garden.
examples.chinese: 这只狗喜欢在花园里[埋]他的骨头。

examples.english: People often [bury] dead pets in the backyard.
examples.chinese: 人们经常在后院[埋葬]死去的宠物。

examples.english: They will [bury] the time capsule near the school next week.
examples.chinese: 他们下周会在学校附近[埋]这个时间胶囊。

meanings.explanation: If you [bury] your face or head in something, you press it firmly against or into that thing.

examples.english: The shy girl will [bury] her face in her hands when she is nervous.
examples.chinese: 这个害羞的女孩紧张时会用手[捂住]脸。

examples.english: He likes to [bury] his face in a soft pillow when he sleeps.
examples.chinese: 他睡觉时喜欢把脸[埋进]软软的枕头里。

examples.english: The cat will [bury] her head under the blanket when it is cold.
examples.chinese: 天冷时，这只猫会把头[藏到]毯子下面。

meanings.explanation: A [block] is a solid piece of material such as wood or cheese that usually has flat, straight sides.

examples.english: My mom bought a [block] of cheese from the supermarket.
examples.chinese: 我妈妈从超市买了一[块]奶酪。

examples.english: My little brother likes to build cars with toy [block]s.
examples.chinese: 我弟弟喜欢用玩具[积木]拼小汽车。

examples.english: This table is made from a large [block] of wood.
examples.chinese: 这张桌子是由一大[块]木头做成的。

meanings.explanation: If you [block] a path, opening, or movement, you get in the way of it so that nothing can pass through.

examples.english: A big truck [block]ed the gate and we couldn't get out.
examples.chinese: 一辆大卡车[堵住]了大门，我们出不去了。

examples.english: Please don't [block] the doorway—people need to walk through.
examples.chinese: 请不要[堵住]门口，大家需要走过这里。

examples.english: He [block]ed the ball with his hands during the game.
examples.chinese: 他在比赛中用手[挡]住了球。

meanings.explanation: Something that is [brief] lasts for only a short time or uses only a few words.

examples.english: We had a [brief] meeting before lunch.
examples.chinese: 午饭前我们开了一个[简短的]会。

examples.english: Please keep your story [brief] so we have time to play.
examples.chinese: 请把故事讲得[简短]一点，这样我们才有时间玩。

examples.english: The rain was [brief], and the sun came out soon.
examples.chinese: 这场雨很[短暂]，太阳很快就出来了。

meanings.explanation: A [brief] is a short spoken or written statement that gives the main points of something.

examples.english: The teacher gave us a [brief] about tomorrow's trip.
examples.chinese: 老师给我们[简单介绍]了明天的旅行安排。

examples.english: Here is a news [brief] from this morning.
examples.chinese: 这是今早的一则新闻[简报]。

examples.english: Can you write a [brief] about what we learned today?
examples.chinese: 你能写个[简要总结]我们今天学了什么吗？

meanings.explanation: If you [calculate] a number or amount, you use mathematics to find out what it is.

examples.english: Let me [calculate] how much money we need for the trip.
examples.chinese: 让我[算算]这趟旅行需要多少钱。

examples.english: Can you help me [calculate] the total score?
examples.chinese: 你能帮我[算一下]总分吗？

examples.english: She used a calculator to [calculate] the answer.
examples.chinese: 她用计算器[算出了]答案。

meanings.explanation: If you [calculate] the effects or result of a possible action, you think about them carefully and plan what to do.

examples.english: He [calculated] that it would take about two hours to get there.
examples.chinese: 他[估算]到那里大概需要两个小时。

examples.english: We need to [calculate] the risk before making a decision.
examples.chinese: 做决定之前，我们需要[估量一下]风险。

examples.english: She [calculated] that she had enough time to finish her homework.
examples.chinese: 她[估计]自己有足够的时间完成作业。

meanings.explanation: A [boxer] is a person who competes in the sport of boxing.

examples.english: My favorite [boxer] won the game last night.
examples.chinese: 我最喜欢的[拳击手]昨晚赢了比赛。

examples.english: That young [boxer] trains for two hours every day.
examples.chinese: 那位年轻的[拳击手]每天训练两小时。

examples.english: He became a professional [boxer] when he was 18.
examples.chinese: 他18岁时成为了一名职业[拳击手]。

meanings.explanation: A [boxer] is a sturdy, short-haired breed of dog that is often kept as a pet.

examples.english: Our family has a cute brown [boxer] named Max.
examples.chinese: 我们家有一只可爱的棕色[拳师犬]叫马克斯。

examples.english: That [boxer] is very friendly to little kids.
examples.chinese: 那只[拳师犬]对小孩子很友好。

examples.english: A [boxer] needs lots of exercise every day.
examples.chinese: 一只[拳师犬]每天需要大量运动。

meanings.explanation: A [carnival] is a public festival with music, dancing, games, and colourful parades, usually held once a year in a town or city.

examples.english: Our school holds a [carnival] every summer with lots of fun games.
examples.chinese: 我们学校每年夏天都会举办一场[狂欢节]，有很多好玩的游戏。

examples.english: We wore funny costumes and danced at the street [carnival].
examples.chinese: 我们穿着搞笑的服装，在街头[狂欢节]上跳舞。

examples.english: The whole town comes out to enjoy the food and music at the [carnival].
examples.chinese: 全镇的人都出来享受[狂欢节]上的美食和音乐。

meanings.explanation: A [carnival] is also a travelling show with rides, games, and food stalls that moves from place to place.

examples.english: The [carnival] came to our town last weekend, and I rode the Ferris wheel for the first time.
examples.chinese: 上周末[游乐场]来到了我们镇上，我第一次坐了摩天轮。

examples.english: I won a big teddy bear at the [carnival] game!
examples.chinese: 我在[游乐会]的游戏中赢了一只大泰迪熊！

examples.english: My favourite part of the [carnival] is eating cotton candy.
examples.chinese: 我最喜欢[游乐会]的部分就是吃棉花糖。

meanings.explanation: [Calculation] is the process of using mathematics to find a number or amount.

examples.english: The [calculation] took her several hours to complete.
examples.chinese: [计算]花了她好几个小时才完成。

examples.english: Can you help me with this [calculation]?
examples.chinese: 你能帮我做这个[计算]吗？

examples.english: By my [calculation], we have enough money for the trip.
examples.chinese: 根据我的[计算]，我们有足够的钱去旅行。

meanings.explanation: A [calculation] is an estimate or prediction of something, often based on available information.

examples.english: His [calculation] of the project cost was very accurate.
examples.chinese: 他对项目成本的[估算]非常准确。

examples.english: After careful [calculation], they decided to move forward.
examples.chinese: 经过仔细[盘算]，他们决定继续推进。

examples.english: Her [calculation] about the future turned out to be wrong.
examples.chinese: 她对未来的[预测]最后证明是错的。

meanings.explanation: The [briefness] of an event or period of time is the quality of it lasting only a short time.

examples.english: We all felt unhappy about the [briefness] of summer vacation.
examples.chinese: 我们都为暑假的[短暂]感到不开心。

examples.english: The [briefness] of the show made the audience want more.
examples.chinese: 演出的[短暂]让观众还没看够。

examples.english: No one noticed the [briefness] of his morning visit.
examples.chinese: 没人察觉到他上午来访的[短暂]。

meanings.explanation: The [briefness] of written or spoken words is the quality of using only a few words.

examples.english: The teacher praised the [briefness] of my written answer.
examples.chinese: 老师表扬了我书面回答的[简洁]。

examples.english: I like the [briefness] of his speech because I get bored easily.
examples.chinese: 我喜欢他发言的[简洁]，因为我很容易感到无聊。

examples.english: The [briefness] of this note makes it easy to remember.
examples.chinese: 这张便条的[简洁]让人好记。

meanings.explanation: A [carnivore] is an animal that eats meat. Its body is designed to hunt and digest other animals.

examples.english: Lions are [carnivores] that hunt other animals for food.
examples.chinese: 狮子是[肉食动物]，靠捕猎其他动物为食。

examples.english: My pet cat is a [carnivore] and loves eating fish.
examples.chinese: 我的宠物猫是[肉食动物]，特别爱吃鱼。

examples.english: A [carnivore] has sharp teeth to tear meat.
examples.chinese: [肉食动物]有尖牙用来撕咬肉。

meanings.explanation: If you [catch] something that is moving through the air, you stop it and hold it with your hands.

examples.english: Can you [catch] the ball I throw to you?
examples.chinese: 你能[接住]我扔给你的球吗？

examples.english: The cat jumped up to [catch] a butterfly.
examples.chinese: 猫跳起来去[抓]一只蝴蝶。

examples.english: Quick! [Catch] the apple before it falls!
examples.chinese: 快！在苹果掉下来之前[接住]它！

meanings.explanation: If you [catch] a bus, train, or plane, you get on it in time before it leaves.

examples.english: We need to run fast to [catch] the school bus.
examples.chinese: 我们需要跑快点才能[赶上]校车。

examples.english: She got up late and couldn't [catch] the morning train.
examples.chinese: 她起晚了，没能[赶上]早班火车。

examples.english: Let's hurry or we won't [catch] the last bus home.
examples.chinese: 我们快点吧，不然就[赶不上]末班车回家了。

meanings.explanation: If you [catch] an illness, you get that illness from someone or something.

examples.english: He didn't wear a jacket and [caught] a bad cold.
examples.chinese: 他没穿外套，[染上]了重感冒。

examples.english: I stayed home because I didn't want to [catch] the flu.
examples.chinese: 我待在家里，因为我不想被[传染上]流感。

examples.english: Wash your hands so you don't [catch] a cold.
examples.chinese: 洗手吧，这样你就不会[得]感冒了。

meanings.explanation: A [category] is a group of things that share the same characteristics or belong to the same type.

examples.english: Which [category] does this book belong to?
examples.chinese: 这本书属于哪个[类别]？

examples.english: We need to sort these items into different [categories].
examples.chinese: 我们要把这些东西分成不同的[类别]。

examples.english: This song won an award in the pop music [category].
examples.chinese: 这首歌获得了流行音乐[类别]的奖项。

meanings.explanation: A [business] is an organization or activity that involves making, buying, selling, or exchanging goods or services for money.

examples.english: My uncle started his own [business] selling coffee.
examples.chinese: 我叔叔做起了自己卖咖啡的[生意]。

examples.english: The whole town depends on this fishing [business].
examples.chinese: 全镇人都靠这个捕鱼[生意]生活。

examples.english: This local [business] has been on Main Street for 20 years.
examples.chinese: 这家本地[商户]在主街上已经开了20年了。

meanings.explanation: Your [business] is matters that concern you personally or that you are responsible for dealing with, especially private matters that other people do not need to get involved in.

examples.english: What I do with my pocket money is my own [business].
examples.chinese: 我怎么花零用钱是我自己的[事]。

examples.english: It is none of your [business] which toy I choose.
examples.chinese: 我选哪个玩具不关你的[事]。

examples.english: She always wants to know other people's [business].
examples.chinese: 她总是想知道别人的[私事]。

meanings.explanation: A [case] is a particular situation, example, or instance of something.

examples.english: In [this case], we should ask our teacher for help.
examples.chinese: 在这种[情况]下，我们应该向老师寻求帮助。

examples.english: The doctor said it was a bad [case] of cold.
examples.chinese: 医生说这是感冒很严重的[病例]。

examples.english: Let me give you a [case] from my school.
examples.chinese: 让我给你讲一个我们学校的[例子]。

meanings.explanation: A [case] is a container or box that is used for holding or protecting something.

examples.english: My phone is in a protective [case].
examples.chinese: 我的手机在一个保护[壳]里。

examples.english: Please put the glasses back in their [case].
examples.chinese: 请把眼镜放回[盒子]里。

examples.english: She carries her violin in a hard [case].
examples.chinese: 她把小提琴放在一个硬[琴盒]里。

meanings.explanation: A [bullet] is a small metal object that is fired from a gun.

examples.english: The toy gun shoots plastic [bullets].
examples.chinese: 这把玩具枪发射的是塑料[子弹]。

examples.english: Police officers carry guns loaded with real [bullets].
examples.chinese: 警察的枪里装的是真[子弹]。

examples.english: A [bullet] left a tiny hole in the wall.
examples.chinese: 一颗[子弹]在墙上留下了一个小洞。

meanings.explanation: A [bullet] is a small round symbol (•) used to mark each item in a list.

examples.english: Put a [bullet] before each item on your shopping list.
examples.chinese: 在购物清单的每项前面加上[圆点]。

examples.english: Use [bullets] to make your notes look neat and tidy.
examples.chinese: 用[圆点]让你的笔记看起来整洁清楚。

examples.english: Each [bullet] in the list shows one key idea.
examples.chinese: 列表中的每个[圆点]代表一个关键想法。

meanings.explanation: If you [capture] a person or animal, you catch them and hold them under your control.

examples.english: The police worked together to [capture] the bank robber.
examples.chinese: 警察联手[抓获]了银行劫匪。

examples.english: The zookeepers will [capture] the escaped lion this afternoon.
examples.chinese: 动物园管理员今天下午会[捕获]逃跑的狮子。

examples.english: My cat helped me [capture] the mouse in the kitchen.
examples.chinese: 我的猫帮我[抓住]了厨房里的老鼠。

meanings.explanation: If you [capture] an image, sound, or moment, you record it using a camera or other device; it can also mean to attract and hold someone's attention.

examples.english: She used her phone to [capture] the beautiful sunset.
examples.chinese: 她用手机[拍下]了美丽的日落。

examples.english: This funny video never fails to [capture] my attention.
examples.chinese: 这个有趣的视频总能[吸引]我的注意力。

examples.english: The photographer went to [capture] photos of the cute pandas.
examples.chinese: 摄影师去[拍摄]可爱熊猫的照片了。

meanings.explanation: If something is [centrifugal], it means it moves or tends to move away from the center, especially in a spinning motion.

examples.english: When you spin a ball on a string, its [centrifugal] pull makes it want to fly away from you.
examples.chinese: 当你用绳子旋转一个球时，[离心的]拉力会让它想从你手中飞出去。

examples.english: A washing machine uses [centrifugal] force to spin water out of wet clothes.
examples.chinese: 洗衣机利用[离心]力把湿衣服里的水甩出来。

examples.english: The fair ride pushed riders outward with [centrifugal] motion.
examples.chinese: 游乐场的设施用[离心]运动把乘客向外推。

meanings.explanation: [Breakage] is when something gets broken, or the act of breaking something.

examples.english: Brushing wet hair can cause [breakage].
examples.chinese: 梳理湿头发可能会导致[断裂]。

examples.english: We wrapped the glasses in cloth to prevent [breakage].
examples.chinese: 我们用布把玻璃杯包起来防止[破损]。

examples.english: The delivery driver handles boxes gently to avoid [breakage].
examples.chinese: 送货司机轻拿轻放箱子以避免[损坏]。

meanings.explanation: A [breakage] is an item that has been broken, usually by accident.

examples.english: There were two [breakages] in the box of dishes.
examples.chinese: 那箱盘子里有两件[破损品]。

examples.english: Mom asked us to pay for any [breakages] we cause.
examples.chinese: 妈妈让我们赔偿我们弄[碎]的东西。

examples.english: The store has a sign about paying for [breakages].
examples.chinese: 店里有个关于赔偿[破损物品]的告示。

meanings.explanation: A [carnivorous] animal is one that eats the flesh of other animals.

examples.english: Lions are [carnivorous] animals that hunt for food.
examples.chinese: 狮子是[食肉]动物，它们靠捕猎获得食物。

examples.english: My cat is [carnivorous] and only eats meat.
examples.chinese: 我的猫是[食肉]的，只吃肉。

examples.english: [Carnivorous] dinosaurs like the T-Rex were very scary hunters.
examples.chinese: 像霸王龙这样的[食肉]恐龙是非常可怕的猎手。

meanings.explanation: A [carnivorous] plant is one that traps and digests insects or other small creatures for food.

examples.english: The Venus flytrap is a [carnivorous] plant that eats bugs.
examples.chinese: 捕蝇草是一种[食虫]植物，会吃虫子。

examples.english: Some [carnivorous] plants grow in poor soil and get food from insects.
examples.chinese: 有些[食虫]植物长在贫瘠的土壤里，靠昆虫获取养分。

examples.english: We saw many [carnivorous] plants at the botanical garden.
examples.chinese: 我们在植物园看到了很多[食虫]植物。

meanings.explanation: A [catastrophe] is an unexpected event that causes great suffering and damage.

examples.english: The big flood was a terrible [catastrophe] for the small town.
examples.chinese: 这场大洪水对这个小镇来说是一场可怕的[灾难]。

examples.english: The hurricane brought a terrible [catastrophe] to the island.
examples.chinese: 飓风给这座小岛带来了一场可怕的[灾难]。

examples.english: We need to work together to stop a climate [catastrophe] from happening.
examples.chinese: 我们需要共同努力，阻止一场气候[灾难]发生。

meanings.explanation: You can refer to any very bad situation as a [catastrophe], often when you are exaggerating how bad it is.

examples.english: Forgetting my birthday cake was a total [catastrophe] for my party.
examples.chinese: 忘了买生日蛋糕对我的派对来说完全是一场[灾难]。

examples.english: Spilling ice cream on my new shirt felt like a [catastrophe] to me.
examples.chinese: 把冰淇淋洒在我的新衬衫上，我觉得这简直是一场[灾难]。

examples.english: When our picnic got rained out, it felt like a [catastrophe] to the kids.
examples.chinese: 我们的野餐被下雨搅黄了，孩子们觉得这简直是一场[灾难]。

meanings.explanation: A [benefit] is something that helps you or gives you an advantage.

examples.english: Eating fruits and vegetables has many health [benefits].
examples.chinese: 吃水果和蔬菜对健康有很多[好处]。

examples.english: One [benefit] of brushing your teeth every day is that you won't get cavities.
examples.chinese: 每天刷牙的一个[好处]是你不会长蛀牙。

examples.english: The new playground is a great [benefit] for children in our town.
examples.chinese: 新游乐场对我们镇上的孩子来说是一个很大的[好处]。

meanings.explanation: If you [benefit] from something, it helps you or gives you an advantage.

examples.english: Everyone can [benefit] from drinking enough water every day.
examples.chinese: 每个人都能从每天喝足够的水中[受益]。

examples.english: Students [benefit] a lot from reading different kinds of books.
examples.chinese: 学生从阅读不同类型的书中[受益]很多。

examples.english: Children [benefit] from playing outside with their friends.
examples.chinese: 孩子们从和朋友在外面玩耍中[受益]。

meanings.explanation: [Captivity] is the state of being kept in a confined place, such as a prison or cage, and being unable to be free.

examples.english: The tiger was born in [captivity] at the zoo.
examples.chinese: 这只老虎是在动物园[圈养]的环境中出生的。

examples.english: The bird escaped from [captivity] and flew into the forest.
examples.chinese: 那只鸟从[囚禁]中逃脱，飞进了森林。

examples.english: The soldier was held in [captivity] for many years.
examples.chinese: 那名士兵被[囚禁]了很多年。

meanings.explanation: A [certification] is an official document or statement that proves that something is true, genuine, or of a particular quality, or that someone has achieved a particular standard or qualification.

examples.english: My sister got a [certification] after finishing her swimming lessons.
examples.chinese: 我姐姐上完游泳课后拿到了[证书]。

examples.english: This toy has a safety [certification] on the box.
examples.chinese: 这个玩具的包装盒上有安全[认证]。

examples.english: He needs a [certification] to work as a lifeguard.
examples.chinese: 他需要[资格证]才能当救生员。

meanings.explanation: If you [characterize] someone or something, you describe their main qualities or features in a particular way.

examples.english: She would [characterize] her dad as a kind and funny person.
examples.chinese: 她会把爸爸[形容]成一个善良又幽默的人。

examples.english: The teacher [characterized] the new student as very hardworking.
examples.chinese: 老师把这个新同学[描述]为非常勤奋。

examples.english: How would you [characterize] your best friend?
examples.chinese: 你会怎么[形容]你最好的朋友？

meanings.explanation: If a feature or quality [characterizes] something, it is a typical and important part of it.

examples.english: Sunny weather [characterizes] the summer in this city.
examples.chinese: 晴朗的天气是这座城市夏天的[典型特征]。

examples.english: A love for music [characterizes] their whole family.
examples.chinese: 对音乐的热爱[是]他们全家的[典型特征]。

examples.english: Hard work and honesty [characterize] this small village.
examples.chinese: 勤劳和诚实[是]这个小村庄的[典型特征]。

meanings.explanation: If you are [certain] about something, you are sure of it and have no doubt about it.

examples.english: I'm [certain] that I locked the door before leaving.
examples.chinese: 我[确定]出门前锁了门。

examples.english: She didn't seem [certain] about the answer.
examples.chinese: 她对答案似乎不太[确定]。

examples.english: You can be [certain] of my support.
examples.chinese: 你可以[确信]我会支持你。

meanings.explanation: A [certain] thing or person is one that is not named or described in detail but that exists or will come.

examples.english: A [certain] teacher gave us lots of homework.
examples.chinese: 有位[特定的]老师给我们留了很多作业。

examples.english: She has a [certain] charm that everyone loves.
examples.chinese: 她有一种[特有的]魅力，大家都很喜欢。

examples.english: On a [certain] day, everything changed.
examples.chinese: 在[某一天]，一切都变了。

meanings.explanation: You use [certainly] to emphasize that something is definitely true or correct.

examples.english: She [certainly] knows how to bake delicious cookies.
examples.chinese: 她[肯定]知道怎么烤出好吃的饼干。

examples.english: He will [certainly] win the race because he runs very fast.
examples.chinese: 他跑得很快，[肯定]能赢这场比赛。

examples.english: This is [certainly] the best book I have ever read.
examples.chinese: 这[绝对]是我读过的最棒的一本书。

meanings.explanation: You use [certainly] to say "yes" in a polite and friendly way when someone asks you something or asks for permission.

examples.english: "May I borrow your pen?" "[Certainly]! Here you go."
examples.chinese: “我能借一下你的笔吗？”“[当然可以]！给你。”

examples.english: "Could you help me carry this box?" "[Certainly], I'd be happy to."
examples.chinese: “你能帮我搬一下这个箱子吗？”“[没问题]，我很乐意。”

examples.english: "Can I sit here?" "[Certainly], please do."
examples.chinese: “我可以坐这里吗？”“[当然]，请坐。”

meanings.explanation: Someone or something that is [charming] is very pleasant and attractive, making you like them very much.

examples.english: The little girl gave us a [charming] smile.
examples.chinese: 那个小女孩给了我们一个[迷人的]微笑。

examples.english: We stayed in a [charming] small house by the beach.
examples.chinese: 我们住在一座[迷人的]海边小屋里。

examples.english: My grandma tells the most [charming] stories before bedtime.
examples.chinese: 我奶奶睡前会讲最[动听的]故事。

meanings.explanation: When you [cheer], you shout loudly to show support or encouragement for someone, especially at a sports game or event.

examples.english: We all [cheered] when our team scored a goal.
examples.chinese: 我们队进球的时候，大家都[欢呼]起来。

examples.english: The whole class [cheered] for the runners at the school sports day.
examples.chinese: 运动会上，全班同学都在为跑步的同学们[加油]。

examples.english: My parents [cheered] me on when I sang on stage.
examples.chinese: 我在台上唱歌时，爸爸妈妈一直在为我[加油打气]。

meanings.explanation: If you [cheer] someone up, or something [cheers] you up, you make that person feel happier or less sad.

examples.english: Mom gave me a big hug to [cheer] me up after I lost the game.
examples.chinese: 比赛输了之后，妈妈给了我一个大大的拥抱来[安慰]我。

examples.english: A funny cartoon can always [cheer] my little sister up.
examples.chinese: 一部搞笑的动画片总能让我妹妹[开心起来]。

examples.english: My best friend came to [cheer] me up when I was sick.
examples.chinese: 我生病的时候，我最好的朋友来看我，让我[振作起来]。

meanings.explanation: A [circus] is a show that includes performances by acrobats, clowns, and trained animals, usually performed in a large tent.

examples.english: We went to the [circus] last weekend and saw some amazing shows.
examples.chinese: 上周末我们去看了一场[马戏]，表演特别精彩。

examples.english: The [circus] has a big red and white tent in the park.
examples.chinese: [马戏团]在公园里搭了一顶红白相间的大帐篷。

examples.english: My little sister loves the clowns at the [circus].
examples.chinese: 我妹妹特别[马戏团里]的小丑。

meanings.explanation: A [circus] can also describe a situation or place that is very noisy, busy, and seems a bit out of control.

examples.english: The kitchen was a [circus] when all the kids tried to cook at the same time.
examples.chinese: 所有孩子同时想做饭，厨房简直成了[马戏团]，一片混乱。

examples.english: After the game, the school hall was like a [circus].
examples.chinese: 比赛结束后，学校大厅热闹得[像马戏团]一样。

examples.english: It was a total [circus] with dogs running everywhere in the house.
examples.chinese: 狗在家里到处乱跑，简直是[一场闹剧]。

meanings.explanation: A [beam] is a line of light that shines from a source such as the sun, a flashlight, or a lamp.

examples.english: A warm [beam] of sunlight came through the window.
examples.chinese: 一缕温暖的[光线]透过窗户照了进来。

examples.english: The cat chased the red [beam] from the toy.
examples.chinese: 小猫追着玩具射出的红色[光束]。

examples.english: The flashlight made a bright [beam] in the dark room.
examples.chinese: 手电筒在黑暗的房间里照出一道明亮的[光柱]。

meanings.explanation: If you [beam], you smile in a very happy and bright way, usually because you are proud or pleased.

examples.english: She [beamed] when she opened her birthday presents.
examples.chinese: 她拆开生日礼物时，[笑容满面]。

examples.english: Dad [beamed] with pride at my good grades.
examples.chinese: 爸爸看到我的好成绩，[自豪地笑了]。

examples.english: The teacher [beamed] at the students after the wonderful show.
examples.chinese: 精彩的表演结束后，老师对着同学们[开心地笑了]。

meanings.explanation: A [circuit] is a complete, closed path around which an electric current can flow, or the electrical equipment that is connected to this path.

examples.english: When you flip the switch, electricity flows through the [circuit] to turn on the light.
examples.chinese: 当你按下开关，电流通过[电路]让灯亮起来。

examples.english: The [circuit] in my bedroom broke, so I had to call an electrician to fix it.
examples.chinese: 我卧室的[电路]坏了，所以我得叫电工来修理。

examples.english: The teacher taught us how to build a simple [circuit] using wires and a battery.
examples.chinese: 老师教我们如何用导线和电池搭建一个简单的[电路]。

meanings.explanation: A [circuit] is a route or course that is shaped like a circle, often used for races or regular journeys.

examples.english: The race cars drove around the [circuit] five times before finishing the race.
examples.chinese: 赛车在[赛道]上跑了五圈才完成比赛。

examples.english: I like to run the same [circuit] through the park every morning.
examples.chinese: 我喜欢每天早上在公园里跑同样的[一圈]。

examples.english: The circus traveled the [circuit], visiting ten different towns this summer.
examples.chinese: 马戏团沿着[巡回路线]，今年夏天去了十个不同的城镇。

meanings.explanation: If you [cherish] someone or something, you love them very much and want to protect them or keep them safe.

examples.english: I [cherish] the time I spend with my grandmother.
examples.chinese: 我[珍惜]和奶奶在一起的时光。

examples.english: They [cherish] their friendship more than anything.
examples.chinese: 他们[珍视]彼此的友谊胜过一切。

examples.english: She [cherish]es the old photos from her childhood.
examples.chinese: 她[珍爱]童年的老照片。

meanings.explanation: To [classify] things means to divide them into groups or types according to what they are like.

examples.english: Please [classify] these toys into big and small ones.
examples.chinese: 请把这些玩具按大小[分类]。

examples.english: We [classify] animals into mammals, birds, and fish.
examples.chinese: 我们把动物[分成]哺乳动物、鸟类和鱼类。

examples.english: The teacher asked us to [classify] these words by their first letter.
examples.chinese: 老师让我们按首字母把这些单词[分类]。

meanings.explanation: A [ceremony] is a formal event that is held on a special occasion, such as a wedding or a graduation.

examples.english: My sister got married at a beautiful [ceremony] last spring.
examples.chinese: 我姐姐去年春天在一个漂亮的[仪式]上结了婚。

examples.english: We had a small [ceremony] for my grandfather's birthday.
examples.chinese: 我们为爷爷的生日办了一个小小的[仪式]。

examples.english: All the students wore nice clothes for the graduation [ceremony].
examples.chinese: 所有学生都穿了漂亮的衣服去参加毕业[典礼]。

meanings.explanation: If something is done with [ceremony], it is done in a very formal and special way.

examples.english: The old man always pours tea with great [ceremony].
examples.chinese: 这位老人倒茶时总是非常[讲究礼节]。

examples.english: They signed the agreement without much [ceremony].
examples.chinese: 他们没有太多[礼节]就签了协议。

examples.english: The principal gave out the medals with a lot of [ceremony].
examples.chinese: 校长以非常[隆重的礼节]颁发了奖牌。

meanings.explanation: If someone [charge]s an amount of money for something, they ask for that amount of money in payment for it.

examples.english: How much do you [charge] for a cup of lemonade?
examples.chinese: 一杯柠檬水你[要价]多少？

examples.english: The store [charge]s five dollars for a notebook.
examples.chinese: 那家商店一个笔记本[收费]五美元。

examples.english: They don't [charge] for water here.
examples.chinese: 这里水不[收钱]。

meanings.explanation: If you [charge] a battery, you put energy into it so it can work. Also means to fill something with a feeling or quality.

examples.english: I need to [charge] my phone before we leave.
examples.chinese: 我们出发前我得给手机[充电]。

examples.english: Dad is [charge]ing his electric car at home.
examples.chinese: 爸爸在家给电动车[充电]。

examples.english: The air was [charge]d with excitement.
examples.chinese: 空气中[充满]了兴奋的气氛。

meanings.explanation: A [cliff] is a high, steep area of rock or earth on the side of a mountain, coast, or valley.

examples.english: We stood at the edge of the [cliff] and looked down at the sea.
examples.chinese: 我们站在[悬崖]边上，往下看着大海。

examples.english: There is a tall [cliff] near our village.
examples.chinese: 我们村子附近有一座很高的[悬崖]。

examples.english: The bird built its nest on the side of a [cliff].
examples.chinese: 那只鸟在[悬崖]峭壁上筑了巢。

meanings.explanation: If you [change] something, you make it different or replace it with another thing.

examples.english: I [change] my socks every day after school.
examples.chinese: 我每天放学之后都会[换]袜子。

examples.english: We need to [change] our old bed for a new one.
examples.chinese: 我们需要把旧床[换成]新的。

examples.english: The colours of the leaves [change] in autumn.
examples.chinese: 树叶的颜色在秋天会[变化]。

meanings.explanation: A [change] is the act or result of becoming different or of replacing one thing with another.

examples.english: There is a big [change] in my hometown this year.
examples.chinese: 我的家乡今年有很大的[变化]。

examples.english: Mum made a small [change] to our weekend plan.
examples.chinese: 妈妈对我们的周末计划做了一点小小的[改动]。

examples.english: The [change] of weather made our picnic end early.
examples.chinese: 天气的[变化]让我们的野餐提前结束了。

meanings.explanation: A [circumstance] is a fact or condition that affects a particular situation or event.

examples.english: We need to change our plan because of unexpected [circumstances].
examples.chinese: 因为意外[情况]，我们需要改变计划。

examples.english: She stayed calm even in this unexpected [circumstance].
examples.chinese: 即使在这个意外[情况]中，她也保持冷静。

examples.english: Under no [circumstances] can you touch that dangerous button.
examples.chinese: 在任何[情况]下你都不能碰那个危险的按钮。

meanings.explanation: A person's [circumstances] are the conditions in which they live, especially relating to their money and personal life.

examples.english: His family's poor [circumstances] meant he couldn't go to college.
examples.chinese: 他家贫困的[境况]意味着他没法上大学。

examples.english: She always helps children from difficult [circumstances].
examples.chinese: 她总是帮助来自困难[境况]的孩子。

examples.english: My aunt's [circumstances] got much better after she started her own business.
examples.chinese: 我阿姨创业后，她的[境况]好了很多。

meanings.explanation: If you are [cognizant] of something, you are aware of it or know about it.

examples.english: The driver was [cognizant] of the children playing nearby.
examples.chinese: 司机[意识到]附近有孩子在玩耍。

examples.english: We need to be [cognizant] of the time so we are not late.
examples.chinese: 我们要[留意]时间，这样才不会迟到。

examples.english: She was fully [cognizant] of the risks before making her choice.
examples.chinese: 在做选择之前，她已经完全[清楚]其中的风险。

meanings.explanation: A [clinician] is a medical professional, such as a doctor or therapist, who works directly with patients to diagnose and treat health problems.

examples.english: The [clinician] checked my heart rate and blood pressure.
examples.chinese: 这位[临床医生]检查了我的心率和血压。

examples.english: My mom took me to see a [clinician] when I had a fever.
examples.chinese: 我发烧时，妈妈带我去看[临床医生]。

examples.english: The [clinician] told me to drink more water and rest.
examples.chinese: [临床医生]让我多喝水，多休息。

meanings.explanation: Something that is [collectable] is worth collecting because it is interesting, rare, or valuable.

examples.english: These old stamps are very [collectable] now.
examples.chinese: 这些旧邮票现在很[值得收藏]。

examples.english: She bought a [collectable] toy from the store.
examples.chinese: 她从商店买了一个[可收藏的]玩具。

examples.english: My grandpa says these coins are [collectable].
examples.chinese: 我爷爷说这些硬币很有[收藏价值]。

meanings.explanation: A [collectable] is an item that people like to collect, such as old toys, stamps, or coins.

examples.english: He has a big box of [collectables] in his room.
examples.chinese: 他房间里有一大箱[收藏品]。

examples.english: This shop sells many fun [collectables].
examples.chinese: 这家店卖很多有趣的[收藏品]。

examples.english: My dad gave me his old [collectables] from when he was young.
examples.chinese: 我爸爸把他年轻时攒下的旧[收藏品]给了我。

meanings.explanation: A [civilian] is a person who is not a member of the military, police, or other armed forces.

examples.english: The army told all [civilian]s to stay indoors.
examples.chinese: 军队要求所有[平民]待在室内。

examples.english: Many [civilian]s lost their homes in the earthquake.
examples.chinese: 许多[平民]在地震中失去了家园。

examples.english: No [civilian]s were hurt in the military operation.
examples.chinese: 这次军事行动没有伤及[平民]。

meanings.explanation: [Civilian] means relating to ordinary people who are not in the military or police, or relating to normal life outside the armed forces.

examples.english: After the war, he went back to [civilian] life.
examples.chinese: 战争结束后，他回归了[平民]生活。

examples.english: The city has a [civilian] government, not a military one.
examples.chinese: 这座城市由[平民]政府管理，不是军政府。

examples.english: He wore [civilian] clothes instead of his uniform.
examples.chinese: 他穿着[便装]，没穿制服。

meanings.explanation: A [chimpanzee] is a kind of small African ape that is very intelligent and lives in forests.

examples.english: Look at that funny [chimpanzee] eating a banana!
examples.chinese: 快看那只搞笑的[黑猩猩]在吃香蕉！

examples.english: We saw a mother [chimpanzee] holding her baby at the zoo.
examples.chinese: 我们在动物园看到一只[黑猩猩]妈妈抱着她的宝宝。

examples.english: My sister loves watching [chimpanzees] climb trees on TV.
examples.chinese: 我姐姐喜欢在电视上看[黑猩猩]爬树。

meanings.explanation: If you [chase] someone or something, you run after them in order to catch or reach them.

examples.english: My dog loves to [chase] butterflies in the garden.
examples.chinese: 我的狗喜欢在花园里[追逐]蝴蝶。

examples.english: If our ball rolls into the street, we have to [chase] it.
examples.chinese: 如果我们的球滚到街上，我们得去[追]它。

examples.english: Cats always [chase] small moving things.
examples.chinese: 猫总是[追逐]会移动的小东西。

meanings.explanation: A [chase] is an act of running after someone or something in order to catch or stop them.

examples.english: After a short [chase], the police caught the thief.
examples.chinese: 经过短暂的[追捕]，警察抓住了小偷。

examples.english: The cat gave up the [chase] when the mouse ran into a hole.
examples.chinese: 老鼠钻进洞后，猫放弃了[追逐]。

examples.english: We saw an exciting car [chase] in the cartoon.
examples.chinese: 我们在动画片里看到了一场刺激的汽车[追逐]。

meanings.explanation: A [college] is a place where you can study after high school, often part of a university or a school that provides higher education.

examples.english: I want to go to [college] after I finish high school.
examples.chinese: 我高中毕业后想上[大学]。

examples.english: My cousin is a [college] student now.
examples.chinese: 我表姐现在是[大学生]了。

examples.english: That [college] has a big sports field.
examples.chinese: 那所[学院]有一个很大的运动场。

meanings.explanation: When you [come] to a place, you move toward it and reach it.

examples.english: Please [come] to my birthday party next week.
examples.chinese: 下周请[来]参加我的生日派对。

examples.english: My dog always [comes] when I call his name.
examples.chinese: 我一叫名字，我的狗就[过来]。

examples.english: Will you [come] to school with me tomorrow?
examples.chinese: 你明天会[来]学校找我吗？

meanings.explanation: If something [comes] from a particular place or person, it originates from there or is sent by them.

examples.english: This gift [comes] from my grandmother.
examples.chinese: 这份礼物是我奶奶[送来]的。

examples.english: The river [comes] from the mountains far away.
examples.chinese: 这条河从遥远的山上[流来]。

examples.english: These apples [come] from a farm nearby.
examples.chinese: 这些苹果是从附近的农场[来]的。

meanings.explanation: [Clay] is a sticky type of earth that becomes hard when baked or dried, and is used to make things such as pots, bricks, and modeling materials for children.

examples.english: My little sister makes cute animals with colored [clay].
examples.chinese: 我妹妹用彩色[黏土]做可爱的小动物。

examples.english: The potter shaped wet [clay] into a beautiful bowl.
examples.chinese: 陶工把湿[黏土]塑造成了一个漂亮的碗。

examples.english: After the rain, the [clay] in the yard got very sticky.
examples.chinese: 下雨后，院子里的[黏土]变得非常黏。

meanings.explanation: A [comedy] is a type of movie, play, or TV show that is intended to make people laugh.

examples.english: We watched a funny [comedy] last night and laughed a lot.
examples.chinese: 我们昨晚看了一部搞笑的[喜剧]，笑得停不下来。

examples.english: My favorite kind of movie is [comedy] because it always makes me happy.
examples.chinese: 我最喜欢的电影类型是[喜剧]，因为它总能让我开心。

examples.english: The school play this year is a [comedy] about a talking cat.
examples.chinese: 今年的校园话剧是一部关于一只会说话的猫的[喜剧]。

meanings.explanation: [Comedy] is a style of entertainment that uses humor, jokes, and funny situations to amuse people.

examples.english: He loves watching [comedy] videos online before going to bed.
examples.chinese: 他喜欢睡前在网上看[搞笑]视频。

examples.english: Her talent for [comedy] makes her the funniest person in our class.
examples.chinese: 她的[搞笑]天赋让她成为我们班最有趣的人。

examples.english: The clown used [comedy] to make the little kids laugh.
examples.chinese: 小丑用[滑稽表演]逗得小朋友们哈哈大笑。

meanings.explanation: If something is [common], it happens often, exists in large numbers, or is found in many places.

examples.english: Colds are very [common] in winter.
examples.chinese: 感冒在冬天非常[常见]。

examples.english: This kind of bird is [common] in our city.
examples.chinese: 这种鸟在我们城市很[常见]。

examples.english: It is a [common] mistake to forget your homework.
examples.chinese: 忘带作业是一个很[常见]的错误。

meanings.explanation: If something is [common], it is shared by or belongs to two or more people.

examples.english: We share a [common] goal to win the game.
examples.chinese: 我们有一个[共同的]目标——赢得比赛。

examples.english: English is a [common] language in many countries.
examples.chinese: 英语在许多国家是一种[通用的]语言。

examples.english: These two students have a [common] interest in drawing.
examples.chinese: 这两个学生有一个[共同的]爱好——画画。

meanings.explanation: A [coastal] place is located on or near the coast, which is the land next to the sea or ocean.

examples.english: We took a walk along the [coastal] path.
examples.chinese: 我们沿着[沿海]小路散步。

examples.english: Many people visit the [coastal] city during summer vacation.
examples.chinese: 暑假时，很多人去那座[沿海]城市玩。

examples.english: The [coastal] village is famous for its fresh seafood.
examples.chinese: 那个[沿海]村子以新鲜海鲜出名。

meanings.explanation: If something [commences], or if you commence it, it begins.

examples.english: The movie will [commence] at 7 PM tonight.
examples.chinese: 电影今晚7点[开始]。

examples.english: Please [commence] your work when the bell rings.
examples.chinese: 铃声一响就请[开始]做作业。

examples.english: The party will [commence] after dinner.
examples.chinese: 派对将在晚餐后[开始]。

meanings.explanation: [Comfort] is a pleasant state of being relaxed, warm, and free from pain.

examples.english: The soft blanket gave her great [comfort] on the cold night.
examples.chinese: 那条柔软的毯子在寒冷的夜晚给了她很大的[舒适]感。

examples.english: He lives in [comfort] now that he has a good job.
examples.chinese: 他现在有了好工作，生活过得很[舒适]。

examples.english: The hotel room was small but had every [comfort].
examples.chinese: 酒店房间虽小，但各种[舒适]设施一应俱全。

meanings.explanation: If you [comfort] someone, you make them feel calmer, happier, and less worried.

examples.english: She held the crying baby to [comfort] him.
examples.chinese: 她抱着哭泣的宝宝来[安慰]他。

examples.english: A cup of hot tea can [comfort] you after a hard day.
examples.chinese: 辛苦一天后，一杯热茶可以[慰藉]你。

examples.english: His words [comforted] her when she felt sad.
examples.chinese: 她难过的时候，他的话[安慰]了她。

meanings.explanation: If you [compensate] for something bad or for a mistake, you do something good to make the situation better.

examples.english: Nothing can [compensate] for losing a good friend.
examples.chinese: 失去一位好朋友，什么都[弥补]不了。

examples.english: She bought him a big cake to [compensate] for forgetting his birthday.
examples.chinese: 她买了一个大蛋糕送他，来[弥补]忘记他生日的过失。

examples.english: He studied harder to [compensate] for the classes he missed.
examples.chinese: 他更加努力学习，来[弥补]缺课落下的进度。

meanings.explanation: If you [compensate] someone, you pay them money because something bad has happened to them, or because they have done work for you.

examples.english: The company will [compensate] the workers for their extra hours.
examples.chinese: 公司会给工人们[付报酬]，补偿他们的加班时间。

examples.english: The restaurant [compensated] us for the long wait with a free meal.
examples.chinese: 餐厅用一顿免费的饭菜来[补偿]我们长时间的等待。

examples.english: The insurance company will [compensate] him for his broken bike.
examples.chinese: 保险公司会为他的破损自行车给他[赔偿]。

meanings.explanation: Two things or people are [compatible] if they can exist or work well together without causing problems or conflicts.

examples.english: This game app is [compatible] with all kinds of phones.
examples.chinese: 这款游戏应用程序与各种手机都[兼容]。

examples.english: My new printer is not [compatible] with my old computer.
examples.chinese: 我的新打印机与旧电脑不[兼容]。

examples.english: These two apps are [compatible] and can work together smoothly.
examples.chinese: 这两个应用程序互相[兼容]，可以顺畅地协同工作。

meanings.explanation: Someone who is [compatible] with another person has similar opinions, interests, or personalities, and can have a good relationship with them.

examples.english: Tom and Lucy are very [compatible] because they both love reading books.
examples.chinese: 汤姆和露西很[合得来]，因为两人都热爱阅读。

examples.english: The two friends are very [compatible] and never argue about anything.
examples.chinese: 这两个朋友非常[投缘]，从不为任何事情争吵。

examples.english: If you are [compatible] with someone, you enjoy spending time together.
examples.chinese: 如果你和某人很[合拍]，你们会喜欢一起度过时光。

meanings.explanation: If you [command] someone to do something, you tell them to do it in a firm and official way.

examples.english: The king [commanded] his guards to open the castle gate.
examples.chinese: 国王[命令]卫兵打开城堡大门。

examples.english: Our teacher [commanded] us to line up quietly.
examples.chinese: 老师[命令]我们安静地排队。

examples.english: The general [commanded] his army to march forward.
examples.chinese: 将军[命令]军队向前行进。

meanings.explanation: A [command] is an order that someone gives to another person, especially in a formal situation.

examples.english: The brave dog obeyed its master's [command].
examples.chinese: 勇敢的小狗听从了主人的[命令]。

examples.english: Soldiers must follow the captain's [command].
examples.chinese: 士兵必须听从队长的[命令]。

examples.english: Give the [command] and we will start.
examples.chinese: 下达[命令]，我们就开始。

meanings.explanation: If you [collect] things, you gather them together and keep them as a hobby or for a particular purpose.

examples.english: I [collect] colorful sea shells when I go to the beach.
examples.chinese: 我去海滩的时候会[收集]彩色贝壳。

examples.english: My brother [collects] toy cars from all over the world.
examples.chinese: 我弟弟[收集]来自世界各地的玩具汽车。

examples.english: We [collect] old books to give to poor children.
examples.chinese: 我们[收集]旧书送给贫困儿童。

meanings.explanation: If you [collect] someone or something, you go to a place to get them and bring them back with you.

examples.english: Mom will [collect] me from school after class.
examples.chinese: 妈妈下课后来学校[接]我。

examples.english: Can you help me [collect] the package from the post office?
examples.chinese: 你能帮我去邮局[取]包裹吗？

examples.english: The school bus comes to [collect] us at 7 every morning.
examples.chinese: 校车每天早上7点来[接]我们。

meanings.explanation: If you [compete] with someone, you try to beat them in a game, race, or other contest.

examples.english: The two teams [compete] against each other every year.
examples.chinese: 这两支球队每年都要[较量]一番。

examples.english: Many kids [compete] to get into the best schools.
examples.chinese: 很多孩子为了进入最好的学校而互相[竞争]。

examples.english: She wants to [compete] in the swimming race next month.
examples.chinese: 她想参加下个月的游泳[比赛]。

meanings.explanation: A [charity] is an organization that raises money or provides help for people who are sick, poor, or in need.

examples.english: We raised money for [charity] at the school fair.
examples.chinese: 我们在学校义卖上为[慈善机构]筹款。

examples.english: The [charity] gives hot meals to homeless people.
examples.chinese: 这家[慈善机构]为无家可归的人提供热饭。

examples.english: My dad donates money to a children's [charity] every month.
examples.chinese: 我爸爸每个月都向一家儿童[慈善机构]捐款。

meanings.explanation: [Charity] is kindness and understanding towards other people, especially when you are judging them.

examples.english: Please show a little [charity] to your younger brother.
examples.chinese: 请对你的弟弟[宽容]一点。

examples.english: We should treat everyone with [charity] and respect.
examples.chinese: 我们应该以[善意]和尊重的态度对待每一个人。

examples.english: [Charity] means forgiving someone when they make a mistake.
examples.chinese: [宽容]意味着原谅别人犯的错。

meanings.explanation: If you [communicate] with someone, you share or exchange information, news, or ideas with them.

examples.english: I need to [communicate] with my teacher about my project.
examples.chinese: 我需要和老师[沟通]一下我的项目。

examples.english: It is hard to [communicate] with people who speak different languages.
examples.chinese: 和说不同语言的人[交流]很难。

examples.english: She learns to [communicate] her feelings through drawing.
examples.chinese: 她学会通过画画来[表达]自己的感受。

meanings.explanation: A [competition] is an event in which people try to win something by being better, faster, or more skilled than others.

examples.english: My sister won first prize in the art [competition].
examples.chinese: 我姐姐在美术[比赛]中获得了一等奖。

examples.english: We are training hard for the school sports [competition].
examples.chinese: 我们正在为学校的体育[比赛]刻苦训练。

examples.english: There is a spelling [competition] for the third-grade students.
examples.chinese: 有一场面向三年级学生的拼写[比赛]。

meanings.explanation: [Competition] is the activity of trying to win or be more successful than other people.

examples.english: There is a lot of [competition] to get into the best schools.
examples.chinese: 要进最好的学校[竞争]非常激烈。

examples.english: Healthy [competition] can help us work harder.
examples.chinese: 良性的[竞争]可以帮助我们更加努力。

examples.english: The two teams are in strong [competition] with each other.
examples.chinese: 两支队伍之间[竞争]非常激烈。

meanings.explanation: A [complaint] is a statement in which you express your dissatisfaction with or annoyance about something.

examples.english: She made a [complaint] about the loud noise next door.
examples.chinese: 她对隔壁的吵闹声提出了[投诉]。

examples.english: The restaurant received a [complaint] about the cold food.
examples.chinese: 这家餐厅收到了关于食物太凉的[投诉]。

examples.english: If you have a [complaint], please tell the teacher.
examples.chinese: 如果你有什么[意见]，请告诉老师。

meanings.explanation: A [complaint] is a physical or medical condition, especially one that causes pain or discomfort, that a patient reports to a doctor.

examples.english: His main [complaint] is a bad headache.
examples.chinese: 他主要的[不适]是剧烈的头痛。

examples.english: The patient's most common [complaint] is feeling tired all the time.
examples.chinese: 这位病人最常见的[主诉]是整天都觉得累。

examples.english: She went to the doctor because of a stomach [complaint].
