examples.english: She [decline]d the invitation to the birthday party.
examples.chinese: 她[婉拒]了生日聚会的邀请。

examples.english: He [decline]d the offer of a second cake.
examples.chinese: 他[拒绝]了再来一块蛋糕的提议。

examples.english: The little boy [decline]d to answer the question.
examples.chinese: 小男孩[拒绝]回答这个问题。

meanings.explanation: A [decline] is a gradual decrease in the amount, number, or quality of something.

examples.english: There has been a big [decline] in the price of apples.
examples.chinese: 苹果的价格大幅[下跌]。

examples.english: The old man is in a state of [decline].
examples.chinese: 这位老人正处于[衰落]状态。

examples.english: Sales showed a slight [decline] this month.
examples.chinese: 这个月销售额略有[下滑]。

meanings.explanation: [Credit] is praise or approval that you get for doing something good.

examples.english: She got all the [credit] for the beautiful painting.
examples.chinese: 她那幅漂亮的画赢得了大家的[称赞]。

examples.english: You should share the [credit] with your classmates.
examples.chinese: 你应该和同学们分享这个[功劳]。

examples.english: The [credit] for the idea goes to my sister.
examples.chinese: 这个主意的[功劳]归我姐姐。

meanings.explanation: If you [credit] money to an account, you add money to it.

examples.english: Mom will [credit] five dollars to my bank account this week.
examples.chinese: 妈妈这周会往我的银行账户里[存]五美元。

examples.english: Please [credit] this gift money to your savings account.
examples.chinese: 请把这笔礼金[存入]你的储蓄账户。

examples.english: The bank will [credit] your account with ten dollars.
examples.chinese: 银行会把十美元[存入]你的账户。

meanings.explanation: If something [decreases], it becomes less in amount, size, or degree.

examples.english: The wind will [decrease] by this evening.
examples.chinese: 到今天晚上，风会[减弱]。

examples.english: We need to [decrease] the noise in the library.
examples.chinese: 我们需要[降低]图书馆里的噪音。

examples.english: Her fever started to [decrease] after taking medicine.
examples.chinese: 吃药后，她的发烧开始[减退]。

meanings.explanation: A [decrease] is a reduction in the amount, size, or degree of something.

examples.english: There was a [decrease] in the number of students this year.
examples.chinese: 今年的学生人数有所[减少]。

examples.english: We saw a big [decrease] in prices after the sale.
examples.chinese: 促销后我们看到价格大幅[下降]。

examples.english: The [decrease] in temperature made it feel like winter.
examples.chinese: 气温的[下降]让人感觉像是冬天。

meanings.explanation: [Degeneration] is the process of becoming worse or weaker in quality, condition, or strength.

examples.english: The [degeneration] of the old building worried everyone in the town.
examples.chinese: 那座老建筑的[衰败]让镇上的每个人都很担心。

examples.english: Without exercise, there will be a slow [degeneration] of your muscles.
examples.chinese: 如果不锻炼，你的肌肉会慢慢[退化]。

examples.english: The [degeneration] of the forest happened because of pollution.
examples.chinese: 由于污染，这片森林出现了[退化]。

meanings.explanation: [Degeneration] is also a medical condition in which tissue or parts of the body become damaged or stop working properly.

examples.english: The doctor explained that [degeneration] in his knees made walking painful.
examples.chinese: 医生解释说，他膝盖的[退化]让走路很疼。

examples.english: Eating carrots can help prevent eye [degeneration].
examples.chinese: 吃胡萝卜有助于预防眼睛[退化]。

examples.english: Scientists are studying nerve [degeneration] to find new treatments.
examples.chinese: 科学家们正在研究神经[退化]以寻找新的治疗方法。

meanings.explanation: If you do something [deliberately], you do it on purpose, meaning you intended to do it and planned it ahead of time.

examples.english: He [deliberately] broke his little brother's toy because he was angry.
examples.chinese: 他[故意]弄坏了弟弟的玩具，因为他很生气。

examples.english: She [deliberately] did not answer the phone because she didn't want to talk.
examples.chinese: 她[故意]不接电话，因为她不想说话。

examples.english: Tom [deliberately] wore mismatched socks to make his friends laugh.
examples.chinese: 汤姆[故意]穿了不配对的袜子来逗朋友们笑。

meanings.explanation: If you act [deliberately], you do things in a slow, careful, and thoughtful way, thinking carefully before making a decision.

examples.english: She spoke [deliberately] so everyone could hear her clearly.
examples.chinese: 她[不紧不慢地]说话，好让每个人都听清楚。

examples.english: The teacher [deliberately] read each question twice to help the students.
examples.chinese: 老师[刻意地]把每道题读了两次来帮助学生。

examples.english: He moved [deliberately] through the dark room so he wouldn't trip.
examples.chinese: 他[小心翼翼地]穿过黑漆漆的房间，免得绊倒。

meanings.explanation: A [decision] is a choice that you make after thinking carefully about several possibilities.

examples.english: My mom made a [decision] to buy me a new bike.
examples.chinese: 我妈妈做出了给我买一辆新自行车的[决定]。

examples.english: It was hard to make a [decision] about where to go on holiday.
examples.chinese: 很难做出去哪里度假的[决定]。

examples.english: My teacher said the final [decision] would be announced tomorrow.
examples.chinese: 老师说最终[决定]会在明天公布。

meanings.explanation: [Decision] is the ability to decide quickly and firmly what to do in a difficult situation.

examples.english: The captain showed great [decision] during the storm.
examples.chinese: 船长在暴风雨中展现出极强的[决断力]。

examples.english: When the fire started, he acted with [decision].
examples.chinese: 火灾发生时，他行动充满[决断力]。

examples.english: A good leader needs [decision] in hard times.
examples.chinese: 好领导在困难时期需要有[决断力]。

meanings.explanation: To [defend] means to protect someone or something from attack, harm, or danger.

examples.english: The police are here to [defend] us.
examples.chinese: 警察在这里[保护]我们。

examples.english: My dad will [defend] our home.
examples.chinese: 我爸爸会[保护]我们的家。

examples.english: Soldiers [defend] their country.
examples.chinese: 士兵们[保卫]他们的国家。

meanings.explanation: To [defend] also means to argue in support of someone or something when they are being criticized.

examples.english: I will [defend] my best friend.
examples.chinese: 我会为我的好朋友[辩护]。

examples.english: Please [defend] your idea.
examples.chinese: 请为你的想法[辩护]。

examples.english: She always [defends] the truth.
examples.chinese: 她总是维护[真理]。

meanings.explanation: If something is done [delightfully], it is done in a way that gives great pleasure or happiness.

examples.english: The little puppy played [delightfully] in the park.
examples.chinese: 小狗在公园里玩得[很开心]。

examples.english: She sang a song [delightfully] at the birthday party.
examples.chinese: 她在生日派对上[甜美地]唱了一首歌。

examples.english: The story ends [delightfully] with everyone laughing.
examples.chinese: 故事以大家都笑的[欢乐]方式结尾。

meanings.explanation: If you [demand] something, you ask for it very firmly and you do not accept a negative answer.

examples.english: The little boy likes to [demand] candy before dinner.
examples.chinese: 这个小男孩喜欢在晚饭前[吵着要]糖果。

examples.english: My sister will [demand] a new toy when we go to the store.
examples.chinese: 我妹妹去商店的时候会[吵着要]一个新玩具。

examples.english: The angry customer began to [demand] his money back.
examples.chinese: 那个愤怒的顾客开始[要求]退款。

meanings.explanation: A [demand] for something is a strong need or desire for it by a lot of people.

examples.english: There is high [demand] for new video games during the holidays.
examples.chinese: 节日期间人们对新电子游戏的[需求]很高。

examples.english: The hot weather created a big [demand] for ice cream.
examples.chinese: 炎热的天气让人们对冰淇淋的[需求]大增。

examples.english: The bakery cannot keep up with the [demand] for birthday cakes.
examples.chinese: 这家面包店无法满足人们对生日蛋糕的[需求]。

meanings.explanation: If you are [dependent] on someone or something, you need them in order to live or succeed.

examples.english: The baby bird is [dependent] on its mother for food.
examples.chinese: 这只雏鸟[依赖]鸟妈妈喂食。

examples.english: My little sister is still [dependent] on our parents.
examples.chinese: 我的小妹妹仍然[依赖]父母。

examples.english: Plants are [dependent] on sunlight to grow.
examples.chinese: 植物[依靠]阳光生长。

meanings.explanation: A [dependent] is a person such as a child who depends on someone else for money, food, and shelter.

examples.english: Each worker can bring one [dependent] to the company picnic.
examples.chinese: 每位员工可以带一名[家属]参加公司野餐。

examples.english: The insurance covers the worker and all his [dependents].
examples.chinese: 这份保险涵盖了这名工人及其所有[家属]。

examples.english: As a [dependent], the child receives health benefits.
examples.chinese: 作为[受抚养人]，这个孩子享有医疗保险。

meanings.explanation: If something is [debatable], it is not certain and people may have different opinions about it.

examples.english: It is [debatable] whether we will go to the beach tomorrow because the weather is not good.
examples.chinese: 明天能不能去海边还[说不准]，因为天气不太好。

examples.english: Whether dogs are better than cats is [debatable] — everyone has their own favorite.
examples.chinese: 狗和猫哪个更好[不好说]——每个人都有自己的最爱。

examples.english: The answer to this question is [debatable], so different students gave different answers.
examples.chinese: 这道题的答案[说不准]，所以不同的学生给出了不同的答案。

meanings.explanation: If a statement, idea, or topic is [debatable], it can be argued about from different sides and has no simple answer.

examples.english: Our teacher said this is a [debatable] question, so everyone can share their own ideas.
examples.chinese: 我们老师说这个问题[可以讨论]，所以每个人都可以说说自己的想法。

examples.english: The best way to spend summer vacation is a [debatable] topic among my classmates.
examples.chinese: 暑假怎么过最好，在我同学之间是一个[有争议的]话题。

examples.english: His opinion about the movie was [debatable], so we had a friendly talk about it.
examples.chinese: 他对这部电影的看法[有争议]，于是我们友好地聊了聊。

meanings.explanation: A [delay] is a situation in which something happens later than it was expected or planned.

examples.english: There was a long [delay] at the traffic light.
examples.chinese: 红绿灯那里出现了长时间的[延误]。

examples.english: The bad weather caused a [delay] to our flight.
examples.chinese: 坏天气导致我们的航班[延误]。

examples.english: We need to leave now to avoid any [delay].
examples.chinese: 我们得现在出发，避免任何[延误]。

meanings.explanation: If you [delay] something, you make it happen later than it was planned or expected.

examples.english: Please don't [delay] your homework until the last minute.
examples.chinese: 请不要把作业[拖延]到最后一分钟。

examples.english: The airline [delayed] our flight because of the storm.
examples.chinese: 因为暴风雨，航空公司[延误]了我们的航班。

examples.english: We have to [delay] our picnic until next week.
examples.chinese: 我们不得不把野餐[推迟]到下周。

meanings.explanation: A [defeater] is a person or team that beats an opponent in a competition, game, or battle.

examples.english: The [defeater] of the last tournament won the prize again this year.
examples.chinese: 上届锦标赛的[击败者]今年再次赢得了奖项。

examples.english: After a long fight, he became the [defeater] of his opponent.
examples.chinese: 经过长时间的搏斗，他成了对手的[击败者]。

examples.english: The crowd cheered for the [defeater] at the end of the match.
examples.chinese: 比赛结束时，人群为[击败者]欢呼。

meanings.explanation: A [defeater] is a fact, belief, or piece of evidence that undermines or weakens another belief or theory.

examples.english: Finding a green apple is a [defeater] for the belief that all apples are red.
examples.chinese: 发现一颗青苹果就是「所有苹果都是红色」这一观点的[反证]。

examples.english: If you think it's sunny but see rain outside, that observation is a [defeater] for your belief.
examples.chinese: 如果你以为天气晴朗，却看到外面在下雨，这个观察就是你原有想法的[反证]。

examples.english: This new evidence became a [defeater] of the old scientific theory.
examples.chinese: 这个新证据成了旧科学理论的[反证]。

meanings.explanation: When you [count], you say numbers in order to find out how many things there are.

examples.english: Let's [count] the red cars on the street.
examples.chinese: 我们来[数一数]街上的红色汽车。

examples.english: Please [count] how many apples are in the basket.
examples.chinese: 请[数一数]篮子里有多少苹果。

examples.english: I will [count] the money in my piggy bank.
examples.chinese: 我来[数一数]我的存钱罐里有多少钱。

meanings.explanation: A [count] is the total number that you get when you count things.

examples.english: The final [count] was twenty students.
examples.chinese: 最后的[数目]是二十名学生。

examples.english: What is the [count] today?
examples.chinese: 今天的[数目]是多少？

examples.english: I lost [count].
examples.chinese: 我记不清[数目]了。

meanings.explanation: A [deposit] is a sum of money you put into a bank account, or a partial payment you make first when buying something.

examples.english: My mom made a [deposit] at the bank today.
examples.chinese: 我妈妈今天在银行存了一笔[存款]。

examples.english: We paid a [deposit] for the new bike.
examples.chinese: 我们为买新自行车付了一笔[定金]。

examples.english: The bank gives you interest on your [deposit].
examples.chinese: 银行会给你的[存款]付利息。

meanings.explanation: If you [deposit] money, you put it into a bank account to keep it safe.

examples.english: I want to [deposit] my lucky money in the bank.
examples.chinese: 我想把压岁钱[存入]银行。

examples.english: She [deposits] some money every week.
examples.chinese: 她每周都[存入]一些钱。

examples.english: Can you help me [deposit] this cash?
examples.chinese: 你能帮我把这些现金[存入]银行吗？

meanings.explanation: A [democratic] country, system, or organization is governed by its people through elected representatives.

examples.english: My country has a [democratic] government.
examples.chinese: 我的国家有一个[民主的]政府。

examples.english: We held a [democratic] vote to choose our class monitor.
examples.chinese: 我们进行了一次[民主的]投票来选班长。

examples.english: Many countries around the world use [democratic] systems.
examples.chinese: 世界上很多国家都采用[民主的]制度。

meanings.explanation: If a group or activity is [democratic], it involves all members equally in making decisions.

examples.english: Our class has a [democratic] way of choosing activities.
examples.chinese: 我们班有一种[民主的]方式来选择活动。

examples.english: The teacher encourages a [democratic] discussion in class.
examples.chinese: 老师鼓励课堂上开展[民主的]讨论。

examples.english: Our family makes decisions in a [democratic] way.
examples.chinese: 我们家以[民主的]方式做决定。

meanings.explanation: If you [depressed], you feel sad and have no energy or enthusiasm.

examples.english: She was [depressed] after hearing the bad news.
examples.chinese: 听到坏消息后，她很[沮丧]。

examples.english: I sometimes feel [depressed] in winter when it's cold all the time.
examples.chinese: 冬天天气一直很冷的时候，我有时会感到[抑郁]。

examples.english: He looked [depressed] and didn't want to talk to anyone.
examples.chinese: 他看起来[郁郁寡欢]，不想和任何人说话。

meanings.explanation: To [depress] something means to press it down or flatten it.

examples.english: The button will [depress] when you push it.
examples.chinese: 你按下去的时候，按钮会[被按下]。

examples.english: Stamp your feet to [depress] the pedal.
examples.chinese: 踩你的脚来[按下]踏板。

meanings.explanation: To [depict] something is to show it in a picture or painting.

examples.english: This picture [depicts] a little girl playing with a dog.
examples.chinese: 这张画[描绘]了一个小女孩和狗狗玩耍。

examples.english: The mural [depicts] our city's beautiful park.
examples.chinese: 这幅壁画[描绘]了我们城市美丽的公园。

examples.english: The artist [depicts] the sunset in warm colors.
examples.chinese: 画家用温暖的颜色[描绘]了日落。

meanings.explanation: To [depict] something is to describe it in words or writing.

examples.english: The book [depicts] a child's first day at school.
examples.chinese: 这本书[描绘]了一个孩子上学的第一天。

examples.english: The story [depicts] how people lived 100 years ago.
examples.chinese: 这个故事[描绘]了100年前人们的生活。

examples.english: Her letter [depicts] the fun trip she had.
examples.chinese: 她的信[描绘]了她那次愉快的旅行。

meanings.explanation: [Dense] describes something that has a lot of things packed tightly together in a small area, or something that is thick and difficult to see through.

examples.english: The [dense] forest is full of tall trees and bushes.
examples.chinese: 这片[茂密]的森林长满了高大的树木和灌木。

examples.english: Be careful when driving because there is [dense] fog on the road.
examples.chinese: 开车要小心，因为路上有很大的[浓雾]。

examples.english: The city has [dense] traffic during rush hour.
examples.chinese: 高峰时段，城市里的交通很[拥堵]。

meanings.explanation: If someone is [dense], they are not able to understand things quickly; it takes them a long time to learn something. This is an informal use.

examples.english: He is not [dense]; he just needs more time to practice.
examples.chinese: 他不[笨]，只是需要更多时间来练习。

examples.english: Sorry, I am a bit [dense] today. Can you explain again?
examples.chinese: 抱歉，我今天有点[迟钝]。你能再解释一下吗？

examples.english: She is not [dense] at all — she just thinks differently.
examples.chinese: 她一点都不[傻]，只是思维方式不同。

meanings.explanation: A [curve] is a line that bends smoothly, without sharp angles.

examples.english: The road has a sharp [curve] ahead.
examples.chinese: 前面这条路有个急[弯]。

examples.english: Can you draw a beautiful [curve] on your paper?
examples.chinese: 你能在纸上画一条漂亮的[曲线]吗？

examples.english: The river makes a big [curve] around the mountain.
examples.chinese: 小河绕着山拐了一个大[弯]。

meanings.explanation: If something [curves], it bends or moves in a line that is not straight.

examples.english: The road [curves] to the left near our house.
examples.chinese: 我们家附近的路向左边[拐弯]。

examples.english: The path [curves] through the tall grass.
examples.chinese: 小路[弯弯曲曲地]穿过高高的草丛。

examples.english: A line of ants [curves] across the path.
examples.chinese: 一队蚂蚁[弯弯曲曲地]爬过小路。

meanings.explanation: If you [descend], you go down to a lower place or level.

examples.english: We watched the plane [descend] from the sky.
examples.chinese: 我们看着飞机从天空中[降落]。

examples.english: She had to [descend] the stairs carefully.
examples.chinese: 她必须小心地[走下]楼梯。

examples.english: The path [descends] into the valley.
examples.chinese: 这条小路[向下延伸]到山谷里。

meanings.explanation: If a government or authority [decontrols] something, it removes official rules or limits on it, allowing people more freedom to make their own choices.

examples.english: The government decided to [decontrol] the price of bread so stores could sell it for less.
examples.chinese: 政府决定[解除对]面包价格的管控，这样商店可以卖得更便宜。

examples.english: Last year, they [decontrolled] the rules about street food, so my mom started selling her dumplings.
examples.chinese: 去年他们[解除了]对街头小吃的限制，所以我妈妈开始卖她的饺子了。

examples.english: When the city [decontrolled] shop hours, the bookstore near my school stayed open later.
examples.chinese: 当城市[解除]商店营业时间限制后，学校附近的书店开门更晚了。

meanings.explanation: [Decontrol] is the act of removing official rules or limits from something, giving people more freedom.

examples.english: The [decontrol] of fruit prices made apples and oranges cheaper for everyone.
examples.chinese: 水果价格[放开]后，苹果和橙子对大家来说都更便宜了。

examples.english: People were happy about the [decontrol] of the old market rules.
examples.chinese: 人们为旧市场规则的[解除]感到高兴。

examples.english: After the [decontrol] of ticket prices, more families could go to the zoo.
examples.chinese: 门票价格[放开]后，更多家庭可以去动物园了。

meanings.explanation: [Destruction] is the act of damaging something so badly that it no longer exists or can no longer be used.

examples.english: The fire caused terrible [destruction] to the old house.
examples.chinese: 大火让这座老房子遭到了严重的[破坏]。

examples.english: People were sad about the [destruction] of the beautiful park.
examples.chinese: 人们对这座美丽公园的[毁坏]感到难过。

examples.english: A big storm brought [destruction] to many small towns.
examples.chinese: 一场大风暴给许多小镇带来了[毁灭]。

meanings.explanation: [Destruction] is the process of putting an end to something or making it stop existing completely.

examples.english: The [destruction] of the old bridge made people build a new one.
examples.chinese: 旧桥的[拆除]让人们建了一座新桥。

examples.english: The factory's [destruction] gave the city more open space.
examples.chinese: 工厂的[拆毁]为城市腾出了更多的空地。

examples.english: Cutting down all the trees led to the [destruction] of the forest.
examples.chinese: 把所有树都砍掉导致了这片森林的[毁灭]。

meanings.explanation: [Desire] is a strong feeling of wanting something, especially something that would give you pleasure or satisfaction.

examples.english: She has a [desire] to travel around the world.
examples.chinese: 她有一个[愿望]周游世界。

examples.english: His [desire] for knowledge never stops.
examples.chinese: 他对知识的[渴望]永不停止。

examples.english: The little girl shows a [desire] for the red balloon.
examples.chinese: 小女孩[想要]那个红色的气球。

meanings.explanation: If you [desire] something, you want it very much.

examples.english: I [desire] a cup of hot chocolate on a cold day.
examples.chinese: 冷天的时候我[想要]一杯热巧克力。

examples.english: She [desires] to become a doctor when she grows up.
examples.chinese: 她[渴望]长大后成为一名医生。

examples.english: He [desires] nothing more than a quiet life.
examples.chinese: 他[只想要]安静的生活。

meanings.explanation: [Despair] is a feeling of having lost all hope that a situation will improve.

examples.english: The little girl was filled with [despair] when she could not find her lost puppy.
examples.chinese: 小女孩找不到丢失的小狗，心里充满了[绝望]。

examples.english: After many failures, he fell into deep [despair].
examples.chinese: 多次失败后，他陷入了深深的[绝望]。

examples.english: There was a look of [despair] on her face when she missed the bus.
examples.chinese: 错过公交车时，她脸上露出了[绝望]的表情。

meanings.explanation: If you [despair] (of something), you feel that there is no hope that a situation will improve.

examples.english: I sometimes [despair] of ever learning to swim well!
examples.chinese: 我有时[绝望地觉得]自己永远都学不会游泳了！

examples.english: Do not [despair] — there is still time to finish your homework.
examples.chinese: 别[绝望]，还有时间完成作业。

examples.english: She began to [despair] when the rain would not stop.
examples.chinese: 雨下个不停，她开始[感到绝望]。

meanings.explanation: A [dentist] is a person whose job is to examine and treat people's teeth and gums.

examples.english: I go to the [dentist] twice a year to check my teeth.
examples.chinese: 我每年去[牙医]那里检查两次牙齿。

examples.english: The [dentist] told me to brush my teeth every morning and night.
examples.chinese: [牙医]告诉我每天早晚都要刷牙。

examples.english: My little sister was brave when the [dentist] pulled out her loose tooth.
examples.chinese: 我妹妹在[牙医]拔掉她松动的牙齿时很勇敢。

meanings.explanation: If you [deliver] something somewhere, you take it to the place where it is supposed to go.

examples.english: The mail carrier [delivers] letters every morning.
examples.chinese: 邮递员每天早上[送]信。

examples.english: Can you [deliver] this cake to grandma's house?
examples.chinese: 你能把这个蛋糕[送]到奶奶家吗？

examples.english: The pizza shop [delivers] food to our door in thirty minutes.
examples.chinese: 披萨店三十分钟内就把食物[送]到我们家门口。

meanings.explanation: If you [deliver] something that you have promised to do or make, you successfully do it or make it happen.

examples.english: Our team worked hard to [deliver] good results.
examples.chinese: 我们团队努力[交出]了好的成果。

examples.english: She always [delivers] what she promises.
examples.chinese: 她总是[兑现]自己的承诺。

examples.english: The company [delivers] high-quality products.
examples.chinese: 这家公司[提供]高质量的产品。

meanings.explanation: [Detailed] information or work contains a large number of facts and cares about every small part of something.

examples.english: The teacher gave us a [detailed] map of the school.
examples.chinese: 老师给了我们一张学校[详细的]地图。

examples.english: She wrote a [detailed] report about her summer holiday.
examples.chinese: 她写了一份暑假[详细的]报告。

examples.english: I need a [detailed] explanation of how to play this game.
examples.chinese: 我需要这个游戏怎么玩的[详细]解释。

meanings.explanation: A [desert] is a large area of dry land with very little water and few plants, where it is usually very hot.

examples.english: Many camels live in the hot [desert].
examples.chinese: 许多骆驼生活在炎热的[沙漠]里。

examples.english: Cacti can grow well in the [desert].
examples.chinese: 仙人掌能在[沙漠]里很好地生长。

examples.english: My dad saw a snake when he visited the [desert].
examples.chinese: 我爸爸去[沙漠]游玩的时候看到了一条蛇。

meanings.explanation: If you [desert] a person or place, you leave them and do not intend to return.

examples.english: A good friend will never [desert] you when you are in trouble.
examples.chinese: 好朋友永远不会在你有困难的时候[抛弃]你。

examples.english: The family [deserted] their old house and moved to the city.
examples.chinese: 这家人[丢下]了老房子，搬到了城里住。

examples.english: The young soldier [deserted] the army because he missed his family.
examples.chinese: 那个年轻士兵因为想家[逃离]了部队。

meanings.explanation: [Deterioration] is the process of becoming worse in quality, condition, or strength over time.

examples.english: The old house showed signs of [deterioration] after years of rain and wind.
examples.chinese: 经过多年的风吹雨打，这栋老房子出现了[老化]的迹象。

examples.english: The doctor was worried about the [deterioration] of the old man's health.
examples.chinese: 医生很担心这位老人健康状况的[恶化]。

examples.english: The road surface has suffered serious [deterioration] this winter.
examples.chinese: 这个冬天路面出现了严重的[破损]。

meanings.explanation: [Deterioration] can also refer to the gradual worsening of a situation, relationship, or standard.

examples.english: There has been a steady [deterioration] in air quality in the city.
examples.chinese: 这座城市空气质量一直在不断[下降]。

examples.english: The [deterioration] of their friendship made both of them sad.
examples.chinese: 他们友谊的[疏远]让两个人都很难过。

examples.english: The teacher noticed a [deterioration] in his grades this term.
examples.chinese: 老师注意到他这学期的成绩出现了[下滑]。

meanings.explanation: In tennis, [deuce] is the score when the players have won three points each, which is 40-40. The player who wins the next two points wins the game.

examples.english: The score is [deuce], so I need to get the next point.
examples.chinese: 比分[平分]了，所以我得拿下下一分。

examples.english: We were at [deuce] three times before I won the game.
examples.chinese: 我们[平分]了三次，最后我才赢了这一局。

examples.english: The game went to [deuce] after she saved match point.
examples.chinese: 在她挽救赛点后比赛进入了[平分]。

meanings.explanation: A [deuce] is a playing card or the side of a dice that has two spots or marks on it.

examples.english: I need to roll a [deuce] to win this game.
examples.chinese: 我需要掷出一个[二点]才能赢。

examples.english: He played the [deuce] of hearts and won the trick.
examples.chinese: 他打出了红桃[二]，赢下了这一轮。

examples.english: The [deuce] is the lowest card in this game.
examples.chinese: [二点牌]是这副牌里最小的牌。

meanings.explanation: Something that is [desirable] is worth having or wanting because it is useful, pleasant, or of good quality.

examples.english: A big house with a garden is very [desirable].
examples.chinese: 带花园的大房子非常[令人向往]。

examples.english: Sunny weather is [desirable] for our school trip.
examples.chinese: 学校出游的话，晴天是[理想的]。

examples.english: Good health is a [desirable] thing for everyone.
examples.chinese: 身体健康对每个人来说都是[值得追求的]。

meanings.explanation: [Development] is the process of growing, changing, or making something bigger or more advanced over time.

examples.english: The baby's [development] is very fast in the first year.
examples.chinese: 宝宝在第一年的[发育]非常快。

examples.english: We are happy to see the [development] of our town.
examples.chinese: 看到我们镇上的[发展]，我们很高兴。

examples.english: Reading books helps with children's brain [development].
examples.chinese: 读书有助于儿童大脑的[发育]。

meanings.explanation: [Development] is the process of designing, building, or creating something new, such as a product, an app, or a piece of land.

examples.english: My dad works in software [development].
examples.chinese: 我爸爸从事软件[开发]工作。

examples.english: The new [development] near our school has many shops and parks.
examples.chinese: 我们学校附近的新[楼盘]有很多商店和公园。

examples.english: The [development] of this app took two years.
examples.chinese: 这个应用的[开发]花了两年时间。

meanings.explanation: Something that is [destructive] causes or is capable of causing great damage or harm to something.

examples.english: The hurricane was very [destructive] and destroyed many homes.
examples.chinese: 飓风非常具有[破坏性]，摧毁了许多房屋。

examples.english: Smoking is [destructive] to your health.
examples.chinese: 吸烟对你的健康很有[害]。

examples.english: The little boy made a [destructive] mess in the living room.
examples.chinese: 那个小男孩把客厅弄得一塌糊涂，真[有破坏力]。

meanings.explanation: If you [detest] someone or something, you hate them very much.

examples.english: I [detest] waking up early on Mondays.
examples.chinese: 我[讨厌]星期一早早起床。

examples.english: She [detests] the smell of cigarettes.
examples.chinese: 她[讨厌]烟的味道。

examples.english: Many people [detest] political corruption.
examples.chinese: 很多人[憎恨]政治腐败。

meanings.explanation: Something that is [defensive] is used or intended for protection against attack, harm, or danger.

examples.english: The castle had strong [defensive] walls to keep enemies out.
examples.chinese: 城堡有坚固的[防御]城墙，用来阻挡敌人。

examples.english: My dad taught me [defensive] driving to stay safe on the road.
examples.chinese: 爸爸教我[防御性]驾驶，这样在路上才安全。

examples.english: The team's [defensive] players stopped the other side from scoring.
examples.chinese: 球队的[防守]队员阻止了对方得分。

meanings.explanation: If someone is [defensive], they behave as if they are being criticized or attacked, even when this is not true.

examples.english: Don't be so [defensive] — I just asked a simple question.
examples.chinese: 别这么[戒备]——我只是问了个简单的问题。

examples.english: He got [defensive] when his teacher asked about his homework.
examples.chinese: 老师问起他的作业时，他变得很[戒备]。

examples.english: She became [defensive] whenever people talked about her grades.
examples.chinese: 每当别人谈起她的成绩时，她就变得很[戒备]。

meanings.explanation: If something [destroys] a physical object or place, it damages it so completely that the thing no longer exists or cannot be repaired or used.

examples.english: The big fire [destroyed] the old wooden house.
examples.chinese: 大火[烧毁]了那栋老旧的木屋。

examples.english: The heavy storm [destroyed] many small boats.
examples.chinese: 强暴风雨[摧毁]了很多小船。

examples.english: The earthquake [destroyed] hundreds of buildings.
examples.chinese: 地震[摧毁]了数百栋建筑。

meanings.explanation: If something [destroys] an abstract thing like a plan, mood, or opportunity, it completely ruins it so it can no longer exist or work as intended.

examples.english: The bad rumor [destroyed] his good name at school.
examples.chinese: 那个坏谣言[毁掉]了他在学校的好名声。

examples.english: Failing the test [destroyed] her happy mood.
examples.chinese: 考试不及格[破坏]了她的好心情。

examples.english: This mistake [destroyed] our chance to go camping.
examples.chinese: 这个错误[毁掉]了我们去露营的机会。

meanings.explanation: A [detail] is a single piece of information or a small part of something that helps you understand the whole thing.

examples.english: My mother told me every [detail] about her trip.
examples.chinese: 妈妈告诉了我她旅行的每个[细节]。

examples.english: Please write down all the [details] of your science experiment.
examples.chinese: 请写下你科学实验的所有[细节]。

examples.english: I want to hear every [detail] of your birthday party.
examples.chinese: 我想听听你生日派对的每个[细节]。

meanings.explanation: If you [detail] something, you explain it fully by giving all the facts or information about it.

examples.english: He [detailed] his plan for the school project to the class.
examples.chinese: 他向全班[详细说明]了学校项目的计划。

examples.english: Can you [detail] what happened at the party?
examples.chinese: 你能[详细说说]派对上发生了什么吗？

examples.english: The email [details] the time and place of the meeting.
examples.chinese: 这封邮件[详细说明了]会议的时间和地点。

meanings.explanation: To [deter] someone from doing something means to make them unwilling to do it by making them afraid of the bad results that could happen.

examples.english: The locked gate [deters] strangers from entering our neighborhood.
examples.chinese: 锁着的大门[阻止]陌生人进入我们小区。

examples.english: My mom's warning didn't [deter] me from trying the spicy candy.
examples.chinese: 妈妈的警告并没有[阻止]我尝试那颗辣糖果。

examples.english: The big dog [deters] bad people from coming near our house.
examples.chinese: 这条大狗[阻止]坏人靠近我们家。

meanings.explanation: If you say that someone or something is [detestable], you mean that you dislike them very much and think they are extremely unpleasant or morally bad.

examples.english: The smell of rotten eggs is absolutely [detestable].
examples.chinese: 臭鸡蛋的味道简直[让人恶心]。

examples.english: He was punished for his [detestable] rudeness to the elderly.
examples.chinese: 他因为对老人[可恶的]无礼行为而受到了惩罚。

examples.english: Stepping on a snail by accident is a [detestable] feeling.
examples.chinese: 不小心踩到蜗牛的感觉[糟透了]。

meanings.explanation: If you [develop] something such as a habit, skill, or plan, you gradually work on it to make it bigger, better, or more complete.

examples.english: I want to [develop] a good reading habit.
examples.chinese: 我想[养成]一个好的阅读习惯。

examples.english: My music teacher helped me [develop] my piano skills.
examples.chinese: 我的音乐老师帮我[培养]钢琴技巧。

examples.english: We plan to [develop] a small vegetable garden in our yard.
examples.chinese: 我们打算在院子里[开辟]一个小菜园。

meanings.explanation: When a child, plant, or animal [develops], it gradually grows and becomes more mature or advanced over time.

examples.english: The tiny seed [developed] into a big apple tree.
examples.chinese: 这颗小种子[长成]了一棵大苹果树。

examples.english: Children [develop] their speaking skills very quickly when they are little.
examples.chinese: 小孩子的说话能力[发展]得非常快。

examples.english: My cute kitten [developed] into a large, healthy cat.
examples.chinese: 我可爱的小猫[成长]为一只健壮的大猫。

meanings.explanation: If you [devote] time, money, energy, etc. to something, you give it all of your time, money, energy, etc. in order to achieve something or help someone.

examples.english: My mother [devotes] every weekend to cooking for the family.
examples.chinese: 我妈妈每个周末都[把时间花在]为家人做饭上。

examples.english: He [devotes] himself to teaching children in the village.
examples.chinese: 他[致力于]在村里教孩子们。

examples.english: We should [devote] more time to exercise every day.
examples.chinese: 我们每天应该[花更多时间]锻炼身体。

meanings.explanation: A [dial] is the circular face of a clock, watch, or meter that shows numbers or information, or a round control on a machine that you turn to make a selection.

examples.english: The [dial] on the old phone had numbers from zero to nine.
examples.chinese: 这个旧电话的[转盘]上有从0到9的数字。

examples.english: I looked at the [dial] on my watch to check the time.
examples.chinese: 我看了看手表的[表盘]来确认时间。

examples.english: Turn the [dial] on the radio to find a good station.
examples.chinese: 转动收音机的[旋钮]来找一个好听的台。

meanings.explanation: If you [dial] a phone number, you press the buttons or turn the dial on a telephone in order to make a call to someone.

examples.english: I need to [dial] my mom's number to tell her I'm home.
examples.chinese: 我需要[拨打]妈妈的电话告诉她我到家了。

examples.english: Please [dial] 911 if there is an emergency.
examples.chinese: 如果有紧急情况请[拨打]911。

examples.english: He picks up the phone and [dial]s his best friend.
examples.chinese: 他拿起电话[拨打]了最好的朋友的号码。

meanings.explanation: When you [digest] food, your body breaks it down so that it can be absorbed and used. You can also [digest] information, which means to think about it and understand it.

examples.english: It takes a few hours for your stomach to [digest] food.
examples.chinese: 胃[消化]食物需要几个小时。

examples.english: Bananas are very easy to [digest].
examples.chinese: 香蕉非常容易[消化]。

examples.english: I need some time to [digest] what the teacher just said.
examples.chinese: 我需要一点时间来[消化]老师刚才说的话。

meanings.explanation: A [digest] is a short piece of writing that contains the most important facts from a longer piece of writing, making it quicker and easier to read.

examples.english: I read a [digest] of the long report instead of the whole thing.
examples.chinese: 我没有读整份报告，而是读了一份[摘要]。

examples.english: My grandpa gets a monthly [digest] of world news.
examples.chinese: 我爷爷订了一份每月世界新闻[文摘]。

examples.english: The teacher gave us a [digest] of the long story.
examples.chinese: 老师给我们发了一份长篇故事的[摘要]。

meanings.explanation: A [dim] light is not bright. If a place is [dim], it is rather dark because there is not much light.

examples.english: The room was [dim] because the lamp was too small.
examples.chinese: 房间里很[暗]，因为台灯太小了。

examples.english: It is hard to read in such [dim] light.
examples.chinese: 在这么[昏暗]的光线下看书很困难。

examples.english: The old house had [dim] hallways with no windows.
examples.chinese: 那座老房子的走廊没有窗户，很[阴暗]。

meanings.explanation: If you [dim] a light, or if it [dim]s, it becomes less bright.

examples.english: Please [dim] the lights before the movie starts.
examples.chinese: 电影开始前请把灯光[调暗]。

examples.english: The stars began to [dim] as the sun came up.
examples.chinese: 太阳升起时，星星渐渐[变暗]了。

examples.english: She turned a knob to [dim] the bedroom lamp.
examples.chinese: 她转动旋钮把床头灯[调暗]。

meanings.explanation: [Digestion] is the process by which your body breaks down food into substances that can be used for energy and growth.

examples.english: Good [digestion] helps you stay healthy and full of energy.
examples.chinese: 良好的[消化]能让你保持健康、精力充沛。

examples.english: After eating an apple, your body starts the process of [digestion].
examples.chinese: 吃完一个苹果后，你的身体开始[消化]。

examples.english: Some foods like yogurt are easy for [digestion].
examples.chinese: 有些食物比如酸奶很容易[消化]。

meanings.explanation: If something happens [directly], it happens without anything or anyone in between, in a straight line or with no delay.

examples.english: You can go [directly] home after school.
examples.chinese: 放学后你可以[直接]回家。

examples.english: The airport bus goes [directly] to the hotel.
examples.chinese: 机场大巴[径直]开到酒店。

examples.english: Please walk [directly] to the teacher's office.
examples.chinese: 请[直接]去老师办公室。

meanings.explanation: If you do something [directly], you do it in a frank and honest way, without hiding anything.

examples.english: If you have a problem, you should talk to your mom [directly].
examples.chinese: 如果你有问题，应该[直接]跟你妈妈说。

examples.english: He [directly] told me that he didn't like the food.
examples.chinese: 他[直截了当地]告诉我他不喜欢这食物。

examples.english: She [directly] asked the teacher for help.
examples.chinese: 她[直接]向老师求助了。

meanings.explanation: If something is [diminishing], it is becoming smaller, weaker, or less in amount over time.

examples.english: Her [diminishing] eyesight made it hard for her to read small letters.
examples.chinese: 她[日益衰退的]视力让她很难看清小字。

examples.english: The school is facing [diminishing] numbers of new students this year.
examples.chinese: 这所学校今年面临新入学人数[不断减少]的情况。

examples.english: His [diminishing] energy after a long day worried his mom.
examples.chinese: 他一整天后[越来越少的]精力让妈妈很担心。

meanings.explanation: [Diminishing] returns means that after a certain point, putting in more effort or money gives you less and less benefit.

examples.english: Studying for five more hours had [diminishing] returns because she was too tired.
examples.chinese: 再学五个小时的效果[越来越差]，因为她已经太累了。

examples.english: Adding more sugar to the tea gave [diminishing] returns — it just got too sweet.
examples.chinese: 往茶里加更多糖的[效果越来越小]——茶已经太甜了。

examples.english: The farmer learned that using too much fertilizer had [diminishing] returns on his crops.
examples.chinese: 农民发现使用过多肥料对庄稼的[增产效果越来越小]。

meanings.explanation: If something is [direct], it goes straight from one place to another without any stop or change in direction.

examples.english: This [direct] bus takes us straight home.
examples.chinese: 这班[直达]公交车直接送我们回家。

examples.english: The [direct] path from school to my house is very short.
examples.chinese: 从学校到我家[直接的]路很短。

examples.english: We had no [direct] light in the room, so it was dark.
examples.chinese: 房间里没有[直射]的光线，所以很暗。

meanings.explanation: If you [direct] someone somewhere, you tell or show them the way to a place.

examples.english: Can you [direct] me to the bathroom?
examples.chinese: 你能给我[指引]去洗手间的路吗？

examples.english: The teacher will [direct] you to the art room.
examples.chinese: 老师会[指引]你去美术教室。

examples.english: Let me [direct] you to the park entrance.
examples.chinese: 让我给你[指]去公园入口的路。

meanings.explanation: To [direct] a film or play means to be in charge of it and tell the actors what to do.

examples.english: He will [direct] the school play this year.
examples.chinese: 他今年将[导演]学校的话剧。

examples.english: She wants to [direct] movies when she grows up.
examples.chinese: 她长大了想[导演]电影。

examples.english: The famous person will [direct] our next show.
examples.chinese: 这位知名人物将[执导]我们的下一场演出。

meanings.explanation: A [diagnosis] is the identification of an illness or disease that is made by a doctor after examining a patient and looking at their symptoms.

examples.english: The doctor's [diagnosis] was that I just had a common cold.
examples.chinese: 医生的[诊断]是我只是得了普通感冒。

examples.english: After some tests, the [diagnosis] showed that my leg was not broken.
examples.chinese: 经过一些检查，[诊断]结果显示我的腿没有骨折。

examples.english: My mom felt relieved when the [diagnosis] said I was healthy.
examples.chinese: 当[诊断]说我身体健康时，妈妈松了一口气。

meanings.explanation: A [diagnosis] is a judgment about what the cause of a problem is, after looking at all the information carefully.

examples.english: The mechanic's [diagnosis] was that the car needed more oil.
examples.chinese: 修理工的[诊断]是汽车需要加油了。

examples.english: After careful [diagnosis], they found the computer virus.
examples.chinese: 经过仔细的[诊断]，他们找到了电脑病毒。

examples.english: A correct [diagnosis] of the problem saved us a lot of time.
examples.chinese: 对这个问题的正确[诊断]为我们省了很多时间。

meanings.explanation: If something is [difficult], it needs a lot of effort, skill, or patience to do, deal with, or understand.

examples.english: This math problem is really [difficult] for me.
examples.chinese: 这道数学题对我来说真的[难]。

examples.english: It's [difficult] to find a parking spot near the park.
examples.chinese: 在公园附近找停车位很[困难]。

examples.english: My little brother finds it [difficult] to tie his shoes alone.
examples.chinese: 我弟弟觉得自己系鞋带很[难]。

meanings.explanation: If someone is [difficult], they are not easy to please, work with, or deal with.

examples.english: My classmate is sometimes [difficult] to get along with.
examples.chinese: 我的同学有时候很[难相处]。

examples.english: The [difficult] customer complained about everything in the shop.
examples.chinese: 这个[难应付]的顾客抱怨了店里所有的东西。

examples.english: Don't be so [difficult]—let's go play outside!
examples.chinese: 别这么[别扭]了—我们出去玩吧!

meanings.explanation: A [disadvantage] is a condition or situation that makes someone less likely to succeed or happy compared to others.

examples.english: Not being able to speak English is a big [disadvantage] in today's job market.
examples.chinese: 不会说英语在当今就业市场上是一个很大的[劣势]。

examples.english: The [disadvantage] of living in a big city is the high cost of rent.
examples.chinese: 住在大城市的[不利之处]是房租太贵。

examples.english: She was at a [disadvantage] because she didn't know anyone at the party.
examples.chinese: 她在派对上处于[不利地位]，因为她不认识任何人。

meanings.explanation: If someone or something [disappears], they go somewhere where they cannot be seen or found.

examples.english: The rabbit will [disappear] when you open the magic box.
examples.chinese: 当你打开魔术盒时，兔子会[消失]。

examples.english: My pencil [disappeared] from my desk.
examples.chinese: 我的铅笔从书桌上[消失]了。

examples.english: The rainbow will [disappear] when the rain stops.
examples.chinese: 雨停后，彩虹会[消失]。

meanings.explanation: If something [disappears], it stops existing or being available.

examples.english: The snow will [disappear] when spring comes.
examples.chinese: 春天来临时，雪会[消融]。

examples.english: My headache [disappeared] after I drank some water.
examples.chinese: 喝了些水后，我的头疼[消失]了。

examples.english: The problem did not [disappear] by itself.
examples.chinese: 这个问题没有自己[消失]。

meanings.explanation: A [dimension] is a measurement of the size of something in a particular direction, such as length, width, or height.

examples.english: We measured the [dimension]s of our new sofa to see if it fits through the door.
examples.chinese: 我们量了新沙发的[尺寸]，看看能不能从门口搬进去。

examples.english: A rectangle has two [dimension]s: length and width.
examples.chinese: 长方形有两个[维度]：长和宽。

examples.english: We live in a world with three spatial [dimension]s.
examples.chinese: 我们生活在一个拥有三个空间[维度]的世界里。

meanings.explanation: A [dimension] is a particular aspect or feature of something such as a situation or a person's character.

examples.english: Travel adds a new [dimension] to my dad's life.
examples.chinese: 旅行给爸爸的生活增添了新的[层面]。

examples.english: We need to consider every [dimension] of this problem before we decide.
examples.chinese: 我们做决定前需要考虑这个问题的每个[方面]。

examples.english: Her social media posts show a fun [dimension] of her personality I didn't know before.
examples.chinese: 她的社交媒体帖子展现了她性格中有趣的[一面]，我之前并不了解。

meanings.explanation: If you are [desirous] of something or [desirous] to do something, you want it very much.

examples.english: The children are [desirous] to visit the zoo this weekend.
examples.chinese: 孩子们[渴望]这个周末去动物园。

examples.english: She is [desirous] to learn how to ride a bicycle.
examples.chinese: 她[渴望]学会骑自行车。

examples.english: He is [desirous] to make new friends at summer camp.
examples.chinese: 他[渴望]在夏令营交到新朋友。

meanings.explanation: [Disapproval] is a feeling that you do not like or agree with something or someone, or the act of showing that you feel this way.

examples.english: Mom shook her head in [disapproval] when I dropped the cake.
examples.chinese: 我把蛋糕掉在地上时，妈妈[不赞同]地摇了摇头。

examples.english: The teacher looked at the noisy students with [disapproval].
examples.chinese: 老师带着[不满]的目光看着那些吵闹的学生。

examples.english: My dad's face showed clear [disapproval] when I said I wanted a pet snake.
examples.chinese: 当我说想要一条宠物蛇时，爸爸脸上明显露出了[不赞成]。

meanings.explanation: If a group or organization [disbands], or if someone [disbands] it, it stops operating as a single unit and its members go their separate ways.

examples.english: The school club decided to [disband] after the graduation ceremony.
examples.chinese: 学校社团决定在毕业典礼后[解散]。

examples.english: The music band will [disband] when the summer tour ends.
examples.chinese: 夏季巡演结束时，这支乐队将会[解散]。

examples.english: The old organization was [disbanded] due to lack of members.
examples.chinese: 由于成员不足，这个老组织被[解散了]。

meanings.explanation: If someone is [discharged] from a hospital, the army, or a job, they are officially allowed to leave.

examples.english: Grandma was [discharged] from the hospital this morning.
examples.chinese: 奶奶今天早上[出院]了。

examples.english: The doctor said he could be [discharged] tomorrow.
examples.chinese: 医生说他明天就可以[出院]了。

examples.english: My brother was [discharged] from the army last year.
examples.chinese: 我哥哥去年从部队[退伍]了。

meanings.explanation: When something such as a liquid, gas, or electricity is [discharged], it flows or is sent out.

examples.english: The factory [discharges] dirty water into the river.
examples.chinese: 那家工厂把脏水[排放]到河里。

examples.english: The pipe [discharges] water into the garden.
examples.chinese: 这根管子把水[排出]到花园里。

examples.english: Don't forget to [discharge] your phone battery before charging it again.
examples.chinese: 重新充电之前，别忘了先把手机电池[放电]。

meanings.explanation: A [direction] is the general path or way that someone or something moves, faces, or points towards.

examples.english: We walked in the same [direction] to the park.
examples.chinese: 我们朝着同一个[方向]走向公园。

examples.english: Can you tell me which [direction] the zoo is in?
examples.chinese: 你能告诉我动物园在哪个[方向]吗？

examples.english: The wind changed its [direction] this morning.
examples.chinese: 今天早上风改变了[方向]。

meanings.explanation: [Direction]s are instructions that tell you how to get to a place or how to do something correctly.

examples.english: I followed the [direction]s on the cookie box.
examples.chinese: 我按照饼干盒上的[说明]操作。

examples.english: Can you give me [direction]s to the nearest playground?
examples.chinese: 你能告诉我去最近游乐场的[路线]吗？

examples.english: Always read the [direction]s before using a new toy.
examples.chinese: 使用新玩具前一定要阅读[说明]。

meanings.explanation: If you [discover] something, you find it or learn about it for the first time, especially something that was hidden or not known before.

examples.english: I [discovered] a cute little cat hiding under the sofa.
examples.chinese: 我[发现]沙发底下藏着一只可爱的小猫。

examples.english: Scientists [discovered] a new kind of flower in the forest.
examples.chinese: 科学家们在森林里[发现]了一种新花。

examples.english: She [discovered] she was good at drawing when she was five.
examples.chinese: 她五岁时就[发现]自己很擅长画画。

meanings.explanation: If you [discover] a fact or the truth about something, you learn it or realize it after thinking, studying, or checking carefully.

examples.english: I [discovered] that my best friend also loves reading comics.
examples.chinese: 我[发现]我最好的朋友也爱看漫画。

examples.english: We [discovered] the answer after looking at the map for a long time.
examples.chinese: 我们看了很久地图后才[发现]答案。

examples.english: He [discovered] that eating too much candy is bad for his teeth.
examples.chinese: 他[发现]吃太多糖对牙齿不好。

meanings.explanation: A [disaster] is a very bad event that causes great damage, harm, or suffering.

examples.english: The heavy rain caused a terrible [disaster] in the village.
examples.chinese: 那场大雨给村庄带来了可怕的[灾难]。

examples.english: A big fire was a [disaster] for the forest animals.
examples.chinese: 一场大火对森林里的动物来说是一场[灾难]。

examples.english: The storm was a [disaster] that knocked down many trees.
examples.chinese: 那场风暴是一场[灾难]，刮倒了很多树。

meanings.explanation: If you say something is a [disaster], you mean it is a complete failure or goes very badly wrong.

examples.english: The school party was a [disaster] because the music didn't work.
examples.chinese: 学校派对成了一场[灾难]，因为音响坏了。

examples.english: My sister's first try to make dumplings was a [disaster].
examples.chinese: 姐姐第一次包饺子简直是一场[灾难]。

examples.english: The camping trip turned into a [disaster] when we forgot the tent.
examples.chinese: 那次露营变成了一场[灾难]，因为我们忘了带帐篷。

meanings.explanation: Something that is [discontinuous] happens in separate parts with gaps or breaks between them, rather than happening all the time without stopping.

examples.english: The rain was [discontinuous] yesterday, stopping and starting all day long.
examples.chinese: 昨天雨下得[断断续续]的，一会儿停一会儿下。

examples.english: We had [discontinuous] sleep because the baby cried many times at night.
examples.chinese: 我们的睡眠[断断续续]的，因为宝宝夜里哭了好多次。

examples.english: The old radio had a [discontinuous] signal, so the music kept cutting out.
examples.chinese: 这台旧收音机的信号[断断续续]的，所以音乐老是中断。

meanings.explanation: [Discordant] sounds are harsh and unpleasant because they do not combine well with other sounds.

examples.english: The [discordant] notes made the song sound terrible.
examples.chinese: 这些[不和谐的]音符让这首歌听起来糟透了。

examples.english: When two singers sing different notes at the same time, it sounds [discordant].
examples.chinese: 当两个歌手同时唱出不同音调时，听起来十分[不和谐]。

examples.english: The [discordant] crash of the cymbals hurt my ears.
examples.chinese: 这阵[刺耳的]钹声震得我耳朵疼。

meanings.explanation: [Discordant] people, groups, or opinions disagree strongly with each other and do not fit well together.

examples.english: The [discordant] opinions of my classmates made it hard to choose a game.
examples.chinese: 同学们[不一致的]意见让我们很难选出要玩的游戏。

examples.english: The two [discordant] teams refused to work together on the project.
examples.chinese: 这两个[对立的]队伍拒绝在项目中合作。

examples.english: [Discordant] views within the family led to a big argument.
examples.chinese: 家里[不一致的]看法引发了一场大争吵。

meanings.explanation: If you are [disappointed], you are unhappy because something that you hoped for or expected did not happen or is not as good as you expected it to be.

examples.english: I was [disappointed] that I couldn't go to the amusement park.
examples.chinese: 没能去游乐园，我很[失望]。

examples.english: My little brother felt [disappointed] when his ice cream fell on the ground.
examples.chinese: 小弟弟的冰淇淋掉在地上，他感到[失望]。

examples.english: My dad was [disappointed] with the new car he bought.
examples.chinese: 爸爸对他新买的车感到[失望]。

meanings.explanation: If you [disappointed] someone, you made them feel unhappy because something they hoped for did not happen.

examples.english: I [disappointed] my mom when I failed my math test.
examples.chinese: 我数学考试不及格，让妈妈[失望]了。

examples.english: The rainy day [disappointed] all the kids at the summer camp.
examples.chinese: 下雨天让夏令营里所有的孩子[失望]了。

examples.english: The new show [disappointed] many people who bought tickets.
examples.chinese: 这场新演出让很多买票的人[失望]了。

meanings.explanation: To [disguise] means to change your appearance or behavior so that people cannot recognize you.

examples.english: The boy wore a mask to [disguise] himself.
examples.chinese: 那个男孩戴口罩[伪装]自己。

examples.english: She tried to [disguise] her sadness with a big smile.
examples.chinese: 她试图用一个大大的微笑[掩饰]自己的悲伤。

examples.english: The spy [disguised] his voice on the phone.
examples.chinese: 那个间谍在电话里[伪装]了自己的声音。

meanings.explanation: A [disguise] is clothes, makeup, or other things that change your appearance so people cannot recognize you.

examples.english: The thief wore a hat and glasses as a [disguise].
examples.chinese: 小偷戴帽子和眼镜[伪装]自己。

examples.english: She took off her [disguise] and showed her real face.
examples.chinese: 她脱下[伪装]，露出了真实的面容。

examples.english: The detective was wearing a clever [disguise].
examples.chinese: 那个侦探戴着一个巧妙的[伪装]。

meanings.explanation: When a group of people [disperse], or when someone disperses them, the group splits up and the people go in different directions.

examples.english: When the bell rang, the kids [disperse]d and ran to the playground.
examples.chinese: 铃一响，孩子们就[散开]跑向了操场。

examples.english: The police asked the crowd to [disperse] and go home.
examples.chinese: 警察让人群[散开]，各自回家。

examples.english: After the meeting ended, everyone began to [disperse].
examples.chinese: 会议结束后，大家开始[散去]。

meanings.explanation: When something [disperse]s, or when something disperses it, it spreads over a wide area.

examples.english: The wind will [disperse] the dandelion seeds far away.
examples.chinese: 风会把蒲公英的种子[吹散]到很远的地方。

examples.english: The smell of the food [disperse]d quickly throughout the house.
examples.chinese: 食物的香味很快[弥漫]了整个屋子。

examples.english: She opened the window to [disperse] the smoke in the room.
examples.chinese: 她打开窗户把房间里的烟[散掉]。

meanings.explanation: If you [discard] something, you get rid of it because you no longer want or need it.

examples.english: I will [discard] these broken toys I don't play with anymore.
examples.chinese: 我要[扔掉]这些我不再玩的破玩具。

examples.english: Mom told me to [discard] the expired food in the fridge.
examples.chinese: 妈妈让我[扔掉]冰箱里过期的食物。

examples.english: We should [discard] bad habits that harm our health.
examples.chinese: 我们应该[摒弃]危害健康的坏习惯。

meanings.explanation: When you [discard] a card in a card game, you put down a card that you do not want to keep in your hand.

examples.english: I need to [discard] this unneeded card from my hand.
examples.chinese: 我需要从手里[丢出]这张没用的牌。

examples.english: He will [discard] his smallest card to keep the bigger ones.
examples.chinese: 他要[打出]最小的牌，好留着更大的牌。

examples.english: She forgot to [discard] a card after picking up a new one.
examples.chinese: 她抽了新牌之后忘记[丢出]一张牌了。

meanings.explanation: Something that is [disharmonic] lacks harmony or agreement; it describes things that do not go well together or sound unpleasant when combined.

examples.english: The [disharmonic] noises from the broken radio hurt my ears.
examples.chinese: 破收音机发出的[刺耳]噪音让我的耳朵很难受。

examples.english: The red and purple colors looked [disharmonic] in the painting.
examples.chinese: 画里的红色和紫色搭配起来[不协调]。

examples.english: Their [disharmonic] friendship ended because they always argued.
examples.chinese: 他们[不和谐的]友谊结束了，因为他们总是吵架。

meanings.explanation: If you [dip] something into a liquid, you put it into the liquid for a short time and then take it out.

examples.english: I like to [dip] my cookies in milk.
examples.chinese: 我喜欢把饼干[蘸]牛奶吃。

examples.english: We [dipped] our brushes in the blue paint.
examples.chinese: 我们把画笔在蓝色颜料里[蘸了蘸]。

examples.english: She [dipped] her bread in the warm soup.
examples.chinese: 她把面包在热汤里[蘸了蘸]。

meanings.explanation: A [dip] is a thick sauce that you eat with raw vegetables, biscuits, or chips.

examples.english: We had chips and [dip] at the party.
examples.chinese: 我们在派对上吃了薯片和[蘸酱]。

examples.english: My dad makes the best cheese [dip].
examples.chinese: 我爸爸做的奶酪[蘸酱]最好吃。

examples.english: Can you pass me the vegetable [dip]?
examples.chinese: 能把蔬菜[蘸酱]递给我吗？

meanings.explanation: Something that is [disputable] is open to question or is not certain, and people can argue about it because there may be more than one opinion or answer.

examples.english: Whether cats or dogs make better pets is a [disputable] question.
examples.chinese: 猫和狗哪个更适合当宠物，这是个[有争议的]问题。

examples.english: The test result was [disputable], so the teacher gave the student another chance.
examples.chinese: 那次测试结果[存疑]，所以老师让学生再考了一次。

examples.english: Some people say the story is true, but it is [disputable].
examples.chinese: 有些人说这个故事是真的，但这[有争议]。

meanings.explanation: A [disagreement] is a situation in which people have different opinions or ideas about something.

examples.english: My brother and I had a [disagreement] about which game to play.
examples.chinese: 我和弟弟在玩什么游戏上有[分歧]。

examples.english: The two friends had a [disagreement] about the best color for the picture.
examples.chinese: 两个朋友在画用什么颜色最好上有[分歧]。

examples.english: The students had a [disagreement] about the answer to the math problem.
examples.chinese: 学生们在数学题的答案上有[分歧]。

meanings.explanation: A [disagreement] is an argument or quarrel between people.

examples.english: The two friends had a [disagreement] and didn't talk for a whole day.
examples.chinese: 两个朋友发生了[争吵]，一整天没说话。

examples.english: Mom and Dad had a [disagreement] about where to go on vacation.
examples.chinese: 爸爸妈妈因为去哪里度假发生了[争执]。

examples.english: The loud [disagreement] between the children woke up the baby.
examples.chinese: 孩子们之间的[争吵声]把宝宝吵醒了。

meanings.explanation: If you [display] something, you show it to people so that they can see it.

examples.english: The museum [displays] many old paintings.
examples.chinese: 博物馆[展示]许多古老的画作。

examples.english: She [displayed] her homework on the board.
examples.chinese: 她在黑板上[展示]她的作业。

examples.english: The dog [displays] its toys to visitors.
examples.chinese: 这只狗向 visitors[展示]它的玩具。

meanings.explanation: A [display] is a screen or electronic device that shows information.

examples.english: Look at the [display] on your phone.
examples.chinese: 看看你手机上的[屏幕]。

examples.english: The store has a big [display] of toys.
examples.chinese: 那家商店有一个大大的玩具[陈列]。

examples.english: Her painting was on [display] at school.
examples.chinese: 她的画作在学校[展出]。

meanings.explanation: [Distrust] is a feeling of doubt or suspicion that you have towards someone or something, especially when you think they may be dishonest or unreliable.

examples.english: I have a deep [distrust] of strangers who knock on my door at night.
examples.chinese: 我对半夜敲门的陌生人有一种深深的[不信任]。

examples.english: Her [distrust] of online shopping comes from a bad experience last year.
examples.chinese: 她对网上购物的[不信任]源于去年的一次糟糕经历。

examples.english: There is a lot of [distrust] between the two neighbors after the argument.
examples.chinese: 那次争吵之后，两家人之间充满了[不信任]。

meanings.explanation: If you [distrust] someone or something, you do not trust them and you think that they may not be honest or reliable.

examples.english: I [distrust] people who promise too much.
examples.chinese: 我[不信任]那些承诺太多的人。

examples.english: Mom always taught me to [distrust] strangers.
examples.chinese: 妈妈总是教导我[不要信任]陌生人。

examples.english: She [distrusts] that website because it looks strange.
examples.chinese: 她[不信任]那个网站，因为它看起来很奇怪。

meanings.explanation: If you [dismiss] someone from their job, you officially tell them that they can no longer work there.

examples.english: The boss will [dismiss] any worker who steals things.
examples.chinese: 老板会[解雇]任何偷东西的员工。

examples.english: The company [dismissed] ten workers last month.
examples.chinese: 公司上个月[解雇]了十名工人。

examples.english: He was [dismissed] for always being late to work.
examples.chinese: 他因为上班总是迟到被[解雇]了。

meanings.explanation: If you [dismiss] an idea, suggestion, or warning, you decide it is not important and do not think about it seriously.

examples.english: Don't [dismiss] my suggestion just because I'm young.
examples.chinese: 别因为我年轻就[不理会]我的建议。

examples.english: She [dismissed] my warning and walked into the dark forest.
examples.chinese: 她[不理会]我的警告，走进了漆黑的森林。

examples.english: He [dismissed] the bad idea and focused on his homework.
examples.chinese: 他[打消]了那个坏主意，专心写作业去了。

meanings.explanation: If you [distribute] things, you hand them out or give them to several people or places.

examples.english: The teacher will [distribute] the test papers to the class.
examples.chinese: 老师将会把试卷[分发]给全班同学。

examples.english: They plan to [distribute] food and water to the families in need.
examples.chinese: 他们计划把食物和水[分发]给需要帮助的家庭。

examples.english: My brother helped [distribute] birthday gifts to all the children.
examples.chinese: 我哥哥帮忙把生日礼物[分发]给所有孩子。

meanings.explanation: If something [distributes] or is [distributed] over an area, it spreads or is spread across that area.

examples.english: The school decided to [distribute] the new computers equally among all classrooms.
examples.chinese: 学校决定把所有新电脑[分配]给各个教室，确保每个班都有。

examples.english: Rainfall [distributes] unevenly across different parts of the country.
examples.chinese: 降雨量在这个国家的各个地区[分布]不均衡。

examples.english: We should [distribute] the chairs evenly around the tables.
examples.chinese: 我们应该把椅子[均匀摆放]到桌子周围。

meanings.explanation: If you [disturb] someone, you interrupt what they are doing or make them feel worried.

examples.english: Please don't [disturb] your brother while he's doing homework.
examples.chinese: 请不要在你哥哥做作业的时候[打扰]他。

examples.english: I'm sorry to [disturb] you, but there's someone at the door.
examples.chinese: 抱歉[打扰]你一下，有人在敲门。

examples.english: The loud noise [disturbed] my sleep last night.
examples.chinese: 昨晚的噪音[打扰]了我的睡眠。

meanings.explanation: [Disgust] is a strong feeling of dislike or disapproval that you have when something is very unpleasant or offensive.

examples.english: He looked at the dirty dishes with [disgust].
examples.chinese: 他看着脏兮兮的碗碟，露出[厌恶]的表情。

examples.english: The smell of rotten eggs filled her with [disgust].
examples.chinese: 臭鸡蛋的味道让她充满[厌恶]。

examples.english: She walked away in [disgust] when she saw the mess on the floor.
examples.chinese: 看到地板上一片狼藉，她[厌恶]地走开了。

meanings.explanation: If something [disgusts] you, it makes you feel a strong sense of dislike or disapproval because it is very unpleasant or wrong.

examples.english: The dirty kitchen [disgusts] me.
examples.chinese: 脏兮兮的厨房[恶心]到我了。

examples.english: It [disgusts] me to see good food being wasted.
examples.chinese: 看到好好的食物被浪费[恶心]到我了。

examples.english: The bad smell [disgusts] everyone in the room.
examples.chinese: 难闻的气味[恶心]到了房间里的每个人。

common_collocations: a disconnect between A and B

meanings.explanation: If you [disconnect] something from something else, you separate it so that it is no longer attached or working.

examples.english: Please [disconnect] your tablet from the charger when it's fully charged.
examples.chinese: 充好后请[拔掉]平板的充电器。

examples.english: Can you help me [disconnect] these two toy train cars?
examples.chinese: 你能帮我把这两节玩具火车车厢[拆开]吗？

examples.english: Remember to [disconnect] the computer before you move it.
examples.chinese: 移动电脑前记得先[断开]电源。

meanings.explanation: A [disconnect] is a situation in which there is a lack of connection or agreement between two things.

examples.english: There is a [disconnect] between what my brother says and what he does.
examples.chinese: 我哥哥说的和做的之间有[脱节]。

examples.english: I feel a [disconnect] when I talk to my old friends on the phone.
examples.chinese: 和老朋友通电话时我感觉有[隔阂]。

examples.english: There is a big [disconnect] between the book and the movie.
examples.chinese: 书和电影之间有很大[差异]。

meanings.explanation: A [diverse] group or thing is made up of many different types, kinds, or people.

examples.english: Our class has a very [diverse] group of students.
examples.chinese: 我们班有一个非常[多元化]的学生群体。

examples.english: She loves reading books on [diverse] topics.
examples.chinese: 她喜欢阅读[各种各样]主题的书。

examples.english: The garden is full of [diverse] flowers and plants.
examples.chinese: 花园里长满了[形形色色]的花草。

meanings.explanation: When people or cultures are described as [diverse], it means they are very different from each other in background, race, or way of life.

examples.english: New York is a city with [diverse] cultures.
examples.chinese: 纽约是一个拥有[多元]文化的城市。

examples.english: We should respect [diverse] opinions from everyone.
examples.chinese: 我们应该尊重每个人的[不同]意见。

examples.english: The school welcomes children from [diverse] backgrounds.
examples.chinese: 学校欢迎来自[各种]背景的孩子。

meanings.explanation: A [disposable] product is designed to be thrown away after it has been used, instead of being washed and kept.

examples.english: We brought [disposable] plates to the picnic so we wouldn't have to wash dishes.
examples.chinese: 我们带了[一次性]盘子去野餐，这样就不用洗碗了。

examples.english: The nurse put on [disposable] gloves before giving me a shot.
examples.chinese: 护士在给我打针前戴上了[一次性]手套。

examples.english: These [disposable] cups are great for parties because you can just throw them away.
examples.chinese: 这些[一次性]杯子特别适合派对，用完直接扔掉就行。

meanings.explanation: [Disposables] are products that are designed to be used once and then thrown away.

examples.english: We use cloth napkins at home instead of [disposables] to reduce waste.
examples.chinese: 我们在家用布餐巾，而不是[一次性用品]，以减少垃圾。

examples.english: The restaurant switched from [disposables] to real plates and cups.
examples.chinese: 这家餐厅从[一次性用品]换成了真正的盘子和杯子。

examples.english: Many campers bring [disposables] because they are light and easy to clean up.
examples.chinese: 很多露营的人会带[一次性用品]，因为轻便又好收拾。

meanings.explanation: If you [divide] something, you split it into parts or groups.

examples.english: Let's [divide] the pizza among our friends.
examples.chinese: 让我们把披萨[分]给朋友们。

examples.english: The teacher asked us to [divide] into groups.
examples.chinese: 老师让我们[分组]。

examples.english: This river [divides] the city into two parts.
examples.chinese: 这条河把城市[分成]两部分。

meanings.explanation: A [divide] is a line or boundary that separates two areas or groups.

examples.english: There is a big [divide] between the rich and the poor.
examples.chinese: 贫富之间存在很大的[差距]。

examples.english: The mountain [divide] separates these two valleys.
examples.chinese: 这座山[分水岭]把这两个山谷分开。

examples.english: A deep [divide] opened in the ground after the earthquake.
examples.chinese: 地震后地面上[裂开]了一道大[裂缝]。

meanings.explanation: A [distribution] is the way in which things are arranged or spread out over a particular area, or the way in which something is shared out among a group of people.

examples.english: The [distribution] of candies in our class is very fair.
examples.chinese: 我们班的糖果[分配]非常公平。

examples.english: We studied the [distribution] of flowers on the hill.
examples.chinese: 我们研究了小山上花朵的[分布]。

examples.english: This chart shows the [distribution] of different animals in our country.
examples.chinese: 这张图表展示了我国不同动物的[分布]。

meanings.explanation: The [distribution] of goods is the process of moving them from producers to shops or businesses that sell them to the public.

examples.english: This company takes care of the [distribution] of snacks to all local shops.
examples.chinese: 这家公司负责本地所有商店的零食[配送]。

examples.english: A new [distribution] center was built near our town last year.
examples.chinese: 我们镇附近去年建了一个新的[配送]中心。

examples.english: The [distribution] of our school's new textbooks will start tomorrow.
examples.chinese: 我们学校新课本的[分发]工作明天开始。

meanings.explanation: A [dispute] is a serious disagreement or argument between people or groups.

examples.english: There was a small [dispute] between my two friends about where to play.
examples.chinese: 我的两个朋友因为去哪里玩发生了一点[争执]。

examples.english: My neighbors solved their [dispute] about the garden fence.
examples.chinese: 我的邻居解决了关于花园栅栏的[纠纷]。

examples.english: The teacher helped end the [dispute] between the two boys.
examples.chinese: 老师帮助结束了两个男孩之间的[争执]。

meanings.explanation: If you [dispute] something, you disagree with it and question whether it is true or correct.

examples.english: My little brother [disputes] my story about finding a big turtle.
examples.chinese: 我弟弟[质疑]我找到一只大乌龟的说法。

examples.english: She [disputes] the rule that says girls can't play football.
examples.chinese: 她[反对]女生不能踢足球的规则。

examples.english: The boy [disputed] his friend's answer to the math question.
examples.chinese: 这个男孩[不认同]他朋友给出的数学题答案。

meanings.explanation: If you are [disturbed], you feel worried, upset, or anxious about something.

examples.english: The baby was [disturbed] by the loud thunder.
examples.chinese: 宝宝被响雷吓得[不安]。

examples.english: My mother felt [disturbed] after hearing the bad news.
examples.chinese: 妈妈听到坏消息后感到很[心烦]。

examples.english: Please don't get [disturbed] by the noise outside.
examples.chinese: 别因为外面的噪音[烦心]。

meanings.explanation: A [disturbed] person has serious mental or emotional problems and cannot think or behave normally.

examples.english: The doctor helps [disturbed] children feel better.
examples.chinese: 这位医生帮助心理[有问题]的孩子们康复。

examples.english: He became mentally [disturbed] after the accident.
examples.chinese: 那次事故后他的精神[不正常]了。

examples.english: The [disturbed] man needs to see a doctor.
examples.chinese: 那个精神[失常]的男人需要看医生。

meanings.explanation: If you feel [dizzy], you feel that you are about to lose your balance or fall, and everything seems to be spinning around you.

examples.english: I felt [dizzy] after spinning around too many times.
examples.chinese: 我转太多圈后感到[头晕]。

examples.english: The hot weather made her feel [dizzy].
examples.chinese: 炎热的天气让她觉得[头晕]。

examples.english: He got [dizzy] when he stood up too quickly.
examples.chinese: 他站起来太快，感到[头晕]。

meanings.explanation: To [dizzy] someone means to make them feel dizzy or unsteady.

examples.english: The fast ride really [dizzied] me.
examples.chinese: 那个快速的过山车真的让我[头晕]。

examples.english: Standing in the sun for hours can [dizzy] anyone.
examples.chinese: 在太阳下站几个小时会让任何人[头晕]。

examples.english: The strong smell [dizzied] the little girl.
examples.chinese: 那股浓烈的气味让小女孩[头晕]了。

meanings.explanation: The [division] of something is the act of separating it into different parts or groups.

examples.english: The [division] of the cake into six equal pieces was easy.
examples.chinese: 把蛋糕[分成]六等份很简单。

examples.english: There is a [division] between the boys' lockers and the girls' lockers.
examples.chinese: 男生储物柜和女生储物柜之间有[分隔]。

examples.english: The teacher suggested the [division] of our class into four teams.
examples.chinese: 老师建议把我们班[分成]四个小组。

meanings.explanation: In mathematics, [division] is the process of calculating how many times one number is contained in another.

examples.english: We are learning [division] in our math class this week.
examples.chinese: 这周我们在数学课上学习[除法]。

examples.english: Ten divided by two equals five; that is simple [division].
examples.chinese: 十除以二等于五，这是简单的[除法]。

examples.english: Can you help me with this [division] homework?
examples.chinese: 你能帮我做这道[除法]作业吗？

meanings.explanation: A [donation] is something, especially money, that someone gives to a person, organization, or cause in order to help them.

examples.english: Our school got a big [donation] to build a new library.
examples.chinese: 我们学校收到了一笔大额[捐款]，用来建新图书馆。

examples.english: She made a [donation] to the animal shelter every month.
examples.chinese: 她每个月都给动物收容所[捐钱]。

examples.english: Thank you for your [donation]; it will help many children.
examples.chinese: 谢谢你的[捐赠]，它会帮助到很多孩子。

meanings.explanation: A [donation] is the act of giving your blood, organs, or other body parts to help someone who needs them.

examples.english: My dad gave a blood [donation] at the hospital last week.
examples.chinese: 我爸爸上周在医院[献血]了。

examples.english: Organ [donation] can save people's lives.
examples.chinese: 器官[捐献]可以拯救人们的生命。

examples.english: He signed up for a hair [donation] to help sick kids.
examples.chinese: 他报名参加了头发[捐献]，帮助生病的孩子。

meanings.explanation: The [derivation] of a word is its origin, or the story of where it comes from.

examples.english: The [derivation] of the word 'pizza' is from Italian.
examples.chinese: pizza这个单词的[来源]是意大利语。

examples.english: We learned about the [derivation] of the word 'robot' in class.
examples.chinese: 我们在课堂上学习了robot这个单词的[词源]。

examples.english: My teacher told us the [derivation] of the word 'sandwich'.
examples.chinese: 老师给我们讲了sandwich这个单词的[来源]。

meanings.explanation: A [derivation] is something that has been developed or made from another source.

examples.english: Yogurt is a [derivation] made from milk.
examples.chinese: 酸奶是一种用牛奶制成的[制品]。

examples.english: This new drink is a [derivation] of an old family recipe.
examples.chinese: 这种新饮料是古老家族配方的[衍生品]。

examples.english: Cheese is another tasty [derivation] made from milk.
examples.chinese: 奶酪是另一种用牛奶制成的美味[制品]。

meanings.explanation: If two roads, paths, or lines [diverge], they separate and go in different directions from a common starting point.

examples.english: The two roads [diverge] at the entrance of the park.
examples.chinese: 两条路在公园入口处[分叉]。

examples.english: Our hiking paths [diverge] here, so I'll go left and you go right.
examples.chinese: 我们的徒步路线在这里[分岔]，我走左边你走右边。

examples.english: The river [diverges] into two small streams after passing the hill.
examples.chinese: 河流经过小山后[分流]成两条小溪。

meanings.explanation: If opinions, plans, or interests [diverge], they become different from each other or depart from an original path or common view.

examples.english: Our discussion [diverges] from the topic we need to talk about.
examples.chinese: 我们的讨论[偏离]了我们要谈的话题。

examples.english: When writing my essay, my plan [diverges] from what I thought at first.
examples.chinese: 写作文时，我的计划[偏离]了我最初的想法。

examples.english: Many kids [diverge] from their parents' ideas about what toys to play with.
examples.chinese: 很多孩子在玩具选择上[偏离]了父母的想法。

meanings.explanation: [Dizziness] is a feeling that you are spinning around or that things around you are spinning, making it hard for you to stand or walk steadily.

examples.english: She felt a wave of [dizziness] after standing up too fast.
examples.chinese: 她猛地站起来后，感到一阵[头晕]。

examples.english: The [dizziness] made it hard for him to walk in a straight line.
examples.chinese: [头晕]让他很难走直线。

examples.english: If you experience [dizziness], you should sit down and rest right away.
examples.chinese: 如果你感到[头晕]，应该马上坐下来休息。

meanings.explanation: A [drawback] is a disadvantage or problem that makes something less attractive or useful.

examples.english: The only [drawback] of living near the school is that it's very noisy.
examples.chinese: 住学校附近唯一的[缺点]就是太吵了。

examples.english: One [drawback] of this phone is that the battery dies fast.
examples.chinese: 这部手机的一个[不足]是电池掉电太快。

examples.english: Going to bed late has one big [drawback] — you feel tired all day.
examples.chinese: 晚睡有一个很大的[弊端]——你会整天犯困。

meanings.explanation: A [drastic] action or change is extreme, severe, and often has a very strong and sudden effect.

examples.english: We need to take [drastic] action to protect the environment.
examples.chinese: 我们需要采取[坚决的]行动来保护环境。

examples.english: There has been a [drastic] change in temperature this week.
examples.chinese: 这周气温发生了[急剧的]变化。

examples.english: The doctor said he needs to make [drastic] changes to his lifestyle.
examples.chinese: 医生说他需要对生活方式做出[大幅度的]改变。

meanings.explanation: A [divorce] is the legal ending of a marriage between two people.

examples.english: Their [divorce] made their kids feel very sad.
examples.chinese: 他们的[离婚]让孩子们感到非常难过。

examples.english: My cousin's parents got a [divorce] last spring.
examples.chinese: 我表亲的父母去年春天办完了[离婚]。

examples.english: Everyone was surprised by their sudden [divorce].
examples.chinese: 所有人都对他们突然的[离婚]感到惊讶。

meanings.explanation: If two people [divorce], they legally end their marriage.

examples.english: My aunt [divorced] my uncle two years ago.
examples.chinese: 我姑姑两年前和我姑父[离婚]了。

examples.english: They decided to [divorce] after they stopped loving each other.
examples.chinese: 他们不再相爱之后，就决定[离婚]了。

examples.english: My neighbor's parents are going to [divorce].
examples.chinese: 我邻居的父母打算[离婚]。

meanings.explanation: A [domesticated] animal is one that is used to living with people and is not wild anymore.

examples.english: Dogs are [domesticated] animals that love living with families.
examples.chinese: 狗是[驯化了的]动物，喜欢和人们一起生活。

examples.english: This [domesticated] rabbit likes to be held and petted.
examples.chinese: 这只[驯化了的]兔子喜欢被人抱着抚摸。

examples.english: Cows are [domesticated] animals that farmers keep for milk.
examples.chinese: 牛是[驯化了的]动物，农民养它们来产奶。

meanings.explanation: If you describe a person as [domesticated], you mean they are good at cooking, cleaning, and doing other jobs at home.

examples.english: My grandmother is very [domesticated] and makes delicious meals every day.
examples.chinese: 我奶奶很[擅长持家]，每天做美味的饭菜。

examples.english: After getting married, he became more [domesticated] and learned to cook.
examples.chinese: 结婚后，他变得更[会照顾家了]，还学会了做饭。

examples.english: She was never very [domesticated] and preferred eating out to cooking.
examples.chinese: 她从来不太[擅长家务]，宁愿出去吃饭也不想做饭。

meanings.explanation: [domestic] means relating to the home, house, or family.

examples.english: I help my mom with [domestic] chores like washing dishes.
examples.chinese: 我帮妈妈做[家务]活，比如洗碗。

examples.english: Our dog is a [domestic] animal that lives in our house.
examples.chinese: 我们的狗是[家养]动物，住在我们家里。

examples.english: Everyone in our family shares the [domestic] duties.
examples.chinese: 我们家每个人都分担[家务]活儿。

meanings.explanation: [domestic] means relating to a particular country's own affairs, rather than foreign or international ones.

examples.english: This news is about [domestic] events in our country.
examples.chinese: 这条新闻说的是我们国家的[国内]事情。

examples.english: We should buy more [domestic] products made in our own country.
examples.chinese: 我们应该多买自己国家生产的[国产]产品。

examples.english: She took a [domestic] flight from Beijing to Shanghai.
examples.chinese: 她乘坐了从北京到上海的[国内]航班。

meanings.explanation: If a person or group [dominates] a situation or activity, they have more power or influence over it than anyone else.

examples.english: The big boy always [dominates] the game at recess.
examples.chinese: 那个大个子男孩总是[主导]课间的游戏。

examples.english: My big dog [dominates] all the other pets in our home.
examples.chinese: 我的大狗[控制]着家里所有其他宠物。

examples.english: That large shop [dominates] the toy business in our town.
examples.chinese: 那家大商店[掌控]着我们镇上的玩具生意。

meanings.explanation: If something [dominates] a place or area, it is the largest or most noticeable thing in it.

examples.english: The big apple tree [dominates] our front yard.
examples.chinese: 这棵大苹果树[占据]了我们前院的大部分空间。

examples.english: Dark clouds [dominate] the sky before it rains.
examples.chinese: 下雨前乌云[笼罩]着天空。

examples.english: That bright poster [dominates] the bedroom wall.
examples.chinese: 那张鲜艳的海报[占满]了卧室的整面墙。

meanings.explanation: If something is [divided], it is split or separated into different parts or groups.

examples.english: The cake was [divided] into eight pieces.
examples.chinese: 蛋糕被[分]成了八块。

examples.english: Our class is [divided] into four reading groups.
examples.chinese: 我们班[分成]了四个阅读小组。

examples.english: The playground is [divided] into a big kid area and a little kid area.
examples.chinese: 操场被[分为]大孩子区和小孩子区。

meanings.explanation: If a group of people is [divided], they have different opinions about something and cannot agree.

examples.english: My family is [divided] on where to go for the holiday.
examples.chinese: 我们家对去哪里度假意见[不统一]。

examples.english: The students were [divided] about which movie to watch.
examples.chinese: 学生们对看哪部电影[意见不一]。

examples.english: The neighbors are [divided] over the new fence.
examples.chinese: 邻居们对新围栏的看法[不一致]。

meanings.explanation: A [disturbance] is something that interrupts your peace, quiet, or normal activity, making it difficult for you to continue what you are doing.

examples.english: The TV next door was a [disturbance] while I did my homework.
