meanings.explanation: If something happens [indirectly], it does not happen in a direct or straightforward way, but through other means or in a roundabout manner.

examples.english: She [indirectly] hinted that she wanted a new bike for her birthday.
examples.chinese: 她[间接地]暗示自己想要一辆新自行车当生日礼物。

examples.english: The storm [indirectly] caused the power outage by breaking a tree branch.
examples.chinese: 暴风雨折断树枝，[间接地]导致了停电。

examples.english: He told me [indirectly] that he was upset, instead of saying it directly.
examples.chinese: 他[间接地]告诉我他不高兴，而不是直接说出来。

meanings.explanation: [Inappropriate] behavior, speech, or items are not suitable or proper for a particular situation or occasion.

examples.english: Wearing slippers to a wedding is [inappropriate].
examples.chinese: 穿拖鞋去参加婚礼是[不合适的]。

examples.english: The teacher stopped him from using [inappropriate] words in class.
examples.chinese: 老师制止了他在课堂上说[不当的]话。

examples.english: That silly joke was [inappropriate] at the serious funeral.
examples.chinese: 那个愚蠢的玩笑在严肃的葬礼上是[不妥当的]。

meanings.explanation: If you [indulge] in something, you allow yourself to enjoy it as a special pleasure, especially something you like but do not usually have or do.

examples.english: On Sundays, I like to [indulge] in a big plate of pancakes.
examples.chinese: 星期天我喜欢[尽情享用]一大盘煎饼。

examples.english: After a long week at school, she loves to [indulge] in a good movie.
examples.chinese: 在学校辛苦了一周后，她喜欢[好好享受]一部好电影。

examples.english: My dad sometimes [indulges] in a piece of dark chocolate after dinner.
examples.chinese: 我爸爸有时晚饭后会[犒劳自己]一块黑巧克力。

meanings.explanation: If you [indulge] someone, you let them have or do whatever they want, even if it is not good for them.

examples.english: My grandma always [indulges] me with extra candy when I visit her.
examples.chinese: 我去看望奶奶时，她总是[惯着]我，给我额外的糖果。

examples.english: Parents should not [indulge] their kids with too many toys.
examples.chinese: 父母不应该[溺爱]孩子，给他们买太多玩具。

examples.english: He likes to [indulge] his little sister by playing games with her all afternoon.
examples.chinese: 他喜欢一整个下午陪妹妹玩游戏来[迁就]她。

meanings.explanation: If a method, system, or activity is [incorporative], it tends to include or combine many different things, ideas, or people together into one whole.

examples.english: Our school has an [incorporative] way of teaching that uses songs, games, and stories together.
examples.chinese: 我们学校采用[融合性]的教学方式，把歌曲、游戏和故事结合在一起。

examples.english: The new park is [incorporative] of everyone, with playgrounds, gardens, and sports fields all in one place.
examples.chinese: 这个新公园[包罗万象]，游乐场、花园和运动场都集中在一个地方。

examples.english: Her [incorporative] personality helps her get along with all kinds of people.
examples.chinese: 她[包容]的性格让她能和各种各样的人相处融洽。

meanings.explanation: [Inexactitude] is the quality of being not completely accurate or precise; it means that something is slightly wrong or not exact.

examples.english: The [inexactitude] of my old watch makes me late sometimes.
examples.chinese: 我那块旧手表的[不精确]有时候会让我迟到。

examples.english: There is always some [inexactitude] when you measure things by hand.
examples.chinese: 手工测量东西时总会有一定的[误差]。

examples.english: He admitted the [inexactitude] of his answer in class.
examples.chinese: 他在课上承认了自己的回答有[不够准确]之处。

meanings.explanation: If something is [immemorial], it has existed or been happening for such a very long time that no one can remember when it began or first appeared.

examples.english: This old festival has been celebrated [from time immemorial].
examples.chinese: 这个古老的节日从[远古]时代起就在庆祝了。

examples.english: It is an [immemorial] custom to decorate the town with flowers in spring.
examples.chinese: 春天用鲜花装饰小镇是一项[古老的]习俗。

examples.english: Children have played this game [since time immemorial].
examples.chinese: 孩子们从[远古]时候起就玩这个游戏了。

meanings.explanation: If you describe something as [incredible], you mean it is extremely good, impressive, or enjoyable.

examples.english: We had an [incredible] day at the amusement park.
examples.chinese: 我们在游乐园度过了[超棒的]一天。

examples.english: My dad took me to see an [incredible] fireworks show last night.
examples.chinese: 我爸爸昨晚带我看了一场[震撼的]烟花秀。

examples.english: The ice cream at this shop has an [incredible] flavor.
examples.chinese: 这家店的冰淇淋有着[绝妙的]口味。

meanings.explanation: If you describe something as [incredible], you mean it is so unusual or surprising that it is hard to believe it is true.

examples.english: It's [incredible] that our team won the game in the last minute.
examples.chinese: 我们队在最后一分钟赢了比赛，这真是[不可思议的]。

examples.english: The [incredible] story he told us made everyone's eyes wide open.
examples.chinese: 他讲的这个[难以置信的]故事让每个人都瞪大了眼睛。

examples.english: The [incredible] news that our neighbor won the lottery spread quickly.
examples.chinese: 我们邻居中了彩票这个[惊人的]消息很快传开了。

meanings.explanation: If you describe something as [ineluctable], you mean that it cannot be stopped, avoided, or prevented; it is certain to happen.

examples.english: Mistakes are an [ineluctable] part of learning something new.
examples.chinese: 犯错是学习新东西时[不可避免]的一部分。

examples.english: The arrival of spring is an [ineluctable] fact of nature every year.
examples.chinese: 每年春天的到来是自然界[不可避免]的事实。

examples.english: As the sun rose higher, the midday heat became [ineluctable].
examples.chinese: 随着太阳升高，正午的炎热变得[不可避免]了。

meanings.explanation: If you describe a person, organization, or system as [inflexible], you mean they are not willing or able to change their ideas, plans, or methods, even when there is a good reason to do so.

examples.english: Our teacher is very [inflexible] about homework deadlines.
examples.chinese: 我们的老师对交作业的截止日期非常[严格]，一点都不肯通融。

examples.english: The school's rules are too [inflexible] for students who need extra help.
examples.chinese: 学校的规矩太[死板]了，对需要额外帮助的同学很不友好。

examples.english: My boss is [inflexible] and never listens to new ideas.
examples.chinese: 我老板很[固执]，从来不听新想法。

meanings.explanation: An [inflexible] material or object is stiff and hard, and does not bend easily.

examples.english: These new shoes are still [inflexible] and hurt my feet.
examples.chinese: 这双新鞋还很[硬]，穿着脚疼。

examples.english: The plastic pipe is very [inflexible] and hard to bend.
examples.chinese: 这根塑料管非常[硬]，很难弯折。

examples.english: Grandma's back has become [inflexible] as she gets older.
examples.chinese: 奶奶年纪大了，背变得很[僵硬]，弯不下来了。

meanings.explanation: If you [infer] that something is the case, you decide that it is true on the basis of information that you already have.

examples.english: I can [infer] from her smile that she is happy.
examples.chinese: 我能从她的笑容[推断出]她很开心。

examples.english: From his red eyes, I [inferred] that he had been crying.
examples.chinese: 从他红肿的眼睛，我[推断出]他刚哭过。

examples.english: What did you [infer] from the teacher's words?
examples.chinese: 你从老师的话里[推断出]了什么？

meanings.explanation: If you [illustrate] a book or story, you draw pictures for it.

examples.english: She loves to [illustrate] fairy tales for her little sister.
examples.chinese: 她喜欢给妹妹的童话故事[画插图]。

examples.english: The artist [illustrated] a new storybook.
examples.chinese: 这位艺术家给一本新故事书[画了插图]。

examples.english: My brother [illustrated] his favorite poem.
examples.chinese: 我哥哥给他最喜欢的诗[配了插图]。

meanings.explanation: If you [illustrate] something, you make it clear by giving examples.

examples.english: The teacher used a video to [illustrate] the science lesson.
examples.chinese: 老师用一段视频来[说明]科学课的内容。

examples.english: These photos [illustrate] how much our town has grown.
examples.chinese: 这些照片[展示]了我们小镇发展得有多快。

examples.english: Let me [illustrate] what I mean with a simple story.
examples.chinese: 让我用一个简单的故事来[说明]我的意思。

meanings.explanation: In physics, [inertia] is the tendency of an object to remain still or to continue moving in a straight line unless something pushes or pulls it.

examples.english: Because of [inertia], your books will stay on the desk even when the bus starts moving.
examples.chinese: 由于[惯性]，即使公交车开始行驶，你的书本也会留在桌子上。

examples.english: A rolling ball stops because friction fights against [inertia].
examples.chinese: 滚动的球会停下来，因为摩擦力在对抗[惯性]。

examples.english: The teacher showed how [inertia] makes the toy car keep moving on a smooth floor.
examples.chinese: 老师展示了[惯性]如何让玩具车在光滑的地板上继续滑行。

meanings.explanation: [Inertia] is also a feeling of not wanting to do anything or make any changes; a lack of energy or desire to move or act.

examples.english: After watching TV all day, I felt a sense of [inertia] and didn't want to clean my room.
examples.chinese: 看了一整天电视后，我感到一种[懒散]，不想打扫房间。

examples.english: The [inertia] of the old company made it slow to try new ideas.
examples.chinese: 那家老公司的[惰性]让它很难尝试新想法。

examples.english: She had to push through her morning [inertia] to get up and exercise.
examples.chinese: 她必须克服早上的[倦怠感]，起床去锻炼。

meanings.explanation: Something that is [infrequent] does not happen very often or only happens occasionally.

examples.english: We have [infrequent] visits from our cousins because they live far away.
examples.chinese: 我们和堂兄弟姐妹见面[不频繁]，因为他们住得很远。

examples.english: My dad takes [infrequent] breaks from work because he is very busy.
examples.chinese: 我爸爸工作[很少]休息，因为他太忙了。

examples.english: Rain is [infrequent] in the desert.
examples.chinese: 沙漠里下雨[很少见]。

meanings.explanation: If something is [infinite], it has no end, limit, or boundary and seems to go on forever.

examples.english: Some scientists believe the universe is [infinite].
examples.chinese: 一些科学家认为宇宙是[无限的]。

examples.english: My grandma has an [infinite] supply of cookies for us.
examples.chinese: 奶奶给我们准备了[吃不完的]饼干。

examples.english: The night sky looks like it has [infinite] stars.
examples.chinese: 夜空中看起来有[无数的]星星。

meanings.explanation: You use [infinite] to emphasize that something is extremely great in amount, degree, or extent.

examples.english: We need [infinite] care when holding baby rabbits.
examples.chinese: 抱小兔子幼崽时我们需要[极度的]小心。

examples.english: There is [infinite] joy in playing outside with friends.
examples.chinese: 和朋友在户外玩耍能获得[无穷的]快乐。

examples.english: My teacher shows [infinite] patience when explaining things to us.
examples.chinese: 老师给我们讲题时有着[极大的]耐心。

meanings.explanation: [Inexperience] is the state of not having done or seen something many times, so you lack knowledge and skill.

examples.english: My [inexperience] made it hard to ride a bike at first.
examples.chinese: 我的[缺乏经验]让刚学骑车时很吃力。

examples.english: Because of his [inexperience], he did not know how to cook.
examples.chinese: 因为[没经验]，他不知道怎么做饭。

examples.english: Her [inexperience] with computers meant she couldn't send emails.
examples.chinese: 她对电脑[不熟悉]，所以不会发邮件。

meanings.explanation: An [individual] is a single person, considered separately from a larger group or society.

examples.english: Each [individual] in our class gets one red apple.
examples.chinese: 我们班的每个[个人]都能分到一个红苹果。

examples.english: Every [individual] should help keep our classroom clean.
examples.chinese: 每个[个人]都应该帮忙保持教室干净。

examples.english: The teacher talks to each [individual] about their homework.
examples.chinese: 老师会和每个[个体]谈谈他们的作业情况。

meanings.explanation: [Individual] describes something that belongs to or is intended for a single person, rather than shared by a whole group.

examples.english: Each student has an [individual] desk in our new classroom.
examples.chinese: 在我们的新教室里，每个学生都有一张[个人的]书桌。

examples.english: Mom cut the big candy into [individual] pieces for us.
examples.chinese: 妈妈把一大块糖切成了[单独的]小块分给我们。

examples.english: Every child gets [individual] attention from the teacher in this small class.
examples.chinese: 在这个小班里，每个孩子都能得到老师[单独的]关注。

meanings.explanation: [Inhumanity] is cruel behavior or a cruel act that shows no kindness or pity towards others.

examples.english: The [inhumanity] of the bad king made everyone in the village sad.
examples.chinese: 坏国王的[残暴]让村子里所有人都很难过。

examples.english: We should show love, not [inhumanity], to all animals.
examples.chinese: 我们应该爱护所有动物，而不是表现出[残忍]。

examples.english: The old soldier could never forget the [inhumanity] he saw in the war.
examples.chinese: 那位老兵永远忘不了他在战争中目睹的[残酷景象]。

meanings.explanation: An [indication] is a sign or piece of information that shows something is true or likely to happen.

examples.english: Dark clouds are an [indication] that it might rain soon.
examples.chinese: 乌云是快要下雨的[迹象]。

examples.english: A high fever is often an [indication] of being sick.
examples.chinese: 发高烧通常是生病的[征兆]。

examples.english: Her smile was an [indication] that she enjoyed the party.
examples.chinese: 她的微笑是她喜欢这个派对的[表现]。

meanings.explanation: An [indication] is a signal or action that communicates something, often telling someone what to do or what is happening.

examples.english: A nod is an [indication] that you agree.
examples.chinese: 点头是表示同意的[信号]。

examples.english: The red light is an [indication] to stop.
examples.chinese: 红灯是停车的[信号]。

examples.english: A yawn can be an [indication] that you feel tired.
examples.chinese: 打哈欠是感到疲倦的[信号]。

meanings.explanation: To [initiate] something means to start it or make it begin.

examples.english: The teacher will [initiate] the game by counting to ten.
examples.chinese: 老师会数到十来[开始]这个游戏。

examples.english: Please [initiate] the robot by pressing the green button.
examples.chinese: 请按绿色按钮[启动]机器人。

examples.english: We need to [initiate] the plan before lunchtime.
examples.chinese: 我们需要在午饭前[开始]执行这个计划。

meanings.explanation: If you [initiate] someone into something, you introduce them to an activity or group that they did not know about before.

examples.english: My dad [initiated] me into the art of fishing.
examples.chinese: 爸爸[领我入门]钓鱼这门手艺。

examples.english: The club will [initiate] new members tomorrow.
examples.chinese: 俱乐部明天会[接纳]新成员入会。

examples.english: She [initiated] her little brother into the secrets of chess.
examples.chinese: 她[引导]弟弟初探国际象棋的奥秘。

meanings.explanation: An [innocent] person is someone who has not done anything wrong, especially not committed a crime.

examples.english: The police found that the man was [innocent] and let him go.
examples.chinese: 警察发现那个男人是[无辜的]，就把他放了。

examples.english: Do you think he is guilty or [innocent]?
examples.chinese: 你觉得他是有罪的还是[无辜的]？

examples.english: The judge said she was [innocent] of the crime.
examples.chinese: 法官说她在这桩罪行上是[无罪的]。

meanings.explanation: An [innocent] person, especially a child, is simple and pure, and does not know about the bad or dishonest things in the world.

examples.english: The little girl has an [innocent] smile.
examples.chinese: 小女孩的笑容很[天真]。

examples.english: He was just an [innocent] boy who knew nothing about the fight.
examples.chinese: 他只是个对打架一无所知的[天真]男孩。

examples.english: Children ask the funniest questions because they are so [innocent].
examples.chinese: 小孩子问出的问题最好笑，因为他们太[天真无邪]了。

meanings.explanation: If you [inherit] money, property, or titles from someone who has died, you receive it from them after they die.

examples.english: My grandma [inherited] a big house from her father.
examples.chinese: 我奶奶从她父亲那里[继承]了一栋大房子。

examples.english: He [inherited] his uncle's farm after the uncle passed away.
examples.chinese: 叔叔去世后，他[继承]了叔叔的农场。

examples.english: She [inherited] a lot of money from her rich aunt.
examples.chinese: 她从有钱的阿姨那里[继承]了一大笔钱。

meanings.explanation: If you [inherit] a characteristic, quality, or physical feature from your parents or ancestors, you have it because it was passed to you through genes.

examples.english: I [inherited] my mom's big brown eyes.
examples.chinese: 我[遗传]了妈妈棕色的大眼睛。

examples.english: She [inherited] her dad's curly hair.
examples.chinese: 她[遗传]了爸爸的卷发。

examples.english: Children often [inherit] some personality traits from their parents.
examples.chinese: 孩子通常会从父母那里[遗传]一些性格特征。

meanings.explanation: Someone or something that is [inoffensive] is not annoying or unpleasant, and will not hurt or upset anyone.

examples.english: My grandmother is a very [inoffensive] lady who never says angry words.
examples.chinese: 我奶奶是个非常[温和的]老太太，从来不发火。

examples.english: He told an [inoffensive] joke that made everyone laugh happily.
examples.chinese: 他讲了个[无伤大雅的]笑话，把大家都逗乐了。

examples.english: The movie is [inoffensive] and safe for small children to watch.
examples.chinese: 这部电影很[温和适宜]，小孩子看也没问题。

meanings.explanation: Something that is [inoffensive] does not have a strong smell or taste that people might dislike.

examples.english: This soap has a very [inoffensive] smell that most people like.
examples.chinese: 这款香皂的[气味清新宜人]，大多数人都很喜欢。

examples.english: The soup was [inoffensive] but not very exciting to eat.
examples.chinese: 这碗汤[清淡可口]，但吃起来没什么特别的。

examples.english: I prefer [inoffensive] perfumes that are not too strong.
examples.chinese: 我喜欢[清淡不刺鼻]的香水，不要太浓烈。

meanings.explanation: An [initial] action or event happens at the very beginning, before anything else.

examples.english: My [initial] reaction was surprise.
examples.chinese: 我的[最初]反应是惊讶。

examples.english: The [initial] meeting starts at nine o'clock.
examples.chinese: [第一次]会议九点开始。

examples.english: She passed all her [initial] tests.
examples.chinese: 她通过了所有的[初始]测试。

meanings.explanation: Your [initials] are the first letters of your first and last names, used to identify you.

examples.english: Please write your [initials] on the paper.
examples.chinese: 请在这张纸上写你的[姓名首字母]。

examples.english: His [initials] are J.L.
examples.chinese: 他的[名字首字母]是J.L。

examples.english: She signed the letter with her [initials].
examples.chinese: 她用[首字母签名]的方式签署了这封信。

meanings.explanation: If something is [informal], it is relaxed and not official or strict; you do not have to follow many rules.

examples.english: We wore [informal] clothes to the picnic.
examples.chinese: 我们去野餐时穿了[休闲]的衣服。

examples.english: The party was very [informal], so everyone felt relaxed.
examples.chinese: 派对很[随意]，所以大家都很放松。

examples.english: Dad had an [informal] chat with my teacher after school.
examples.chinese: 爸爸放学后和老师[随意]聊了聊。

meanings.explanation: Language or words that are [informal] are used in everyday conversation with friends and family, rather than in official writing or serious situations.

examples.english: We use [informal] words like 'gonna' when talking to friends.
examples.chinese: 和朋友聊天时，我们会用像"gonna"这样[口语化]的词。

examples.english: The storybook uses [informal] language that kids can easily understand.
examples.chinese: 这本故事书用了[通俗]的语言，孩子们很容易就能看懂。

examples.english: My email to my cousin was [informal] and full of jokes.
examples.chinese: 我给表弟写的邮件很[随意]，里面全是玩笑话。

meanings.explanation: If someone is [insane], they have a very serious mental illness that makes them unable to think or behave in a normal way.

examples.english: The man in that movie was completely [insane].
examples.chinese: 那部电影里的那个男人完全[疯了]。

examples.english: People thought he was [insane] because he talked to himself.
examples.chinese: 人们觉得他[疯了]，因为他总是自言自语。

examples.english: The doctor said the patient was not [insane], just very sad.
examples.chinese: 医生说这个病人不是[精神失常]，只是非常难过。

meanings.explanation: If you describe something as [insane], you mean it is very extreme, unreasonable, or completely beyond what is normal or expected.

examples.english: The line at the amusement park was [insane]!
examples.chinese: 游乐园的队伍[长得离谱]！

examples.english: That roller coaster ride was [insane].
examples.chinese: 那次过山车[太刺激了]。

examples.english: She pays an [insane] amount of money for those shoes.
examples.chinese: 她买那双鞋花的钱[多得离谱]。

meanings.explanation: If a fact, situation, or feeling is [inescapable], you cannot avoid it or ignore it.

examples.english: Getting older is an [inescapable] part of life.
examples.chinese: 变老是生活中[无法避免的]一部分。

examples.english: It is an [inescapable] fact that we all need water to live.
examples.chinese: 我们都需要水才能生存，这是一个[无法逃避的]事实。

examples.english: The [inescapable] truth is that it gets cold in winter.
examples.chinese: 冬天总会变冷，这是一个[无法回避的]事实。

meanings.explanation: If a place, cage, or trap is [inescapable], it is impossible to escape from it.

examples.english: The hunter set an [inescapable] trap for the wild pig.
examples.chinese: 猎人给野猪设了一个[无法逃脱的]陷阱。

examples.english: The bad man locked the puppy in an [inescapable] cage.
examples.chinese: 坏人把小狗锁在了一个[无法逃脱的]笼子里。

examples.english: In the story, the princess was stuck in an [inescapable] tower.
examples.chinese: 在故事里，公主被困在了一座[无法逃脱的]塔里。

meanings.explanation: [Innocuous] means not harmful or offensive; it describes something that is gentle, safe, and unlikely to hurt or upset anyone.

examples.english: It was just an [innocuous] comment about her haircut.
examples.chinese: 那只是一句关于她发型的[无害的]评价。

examples.english: The game has some [innocuous] challenges that are easy to solve.
examples.chinese: 这个游戏有一些[无害的]挑战，很容易解决。

examples.english: He made an [innocuous] remark about the weather.
examples.chinese: 他只是说了一句关于天气的[无害的]话。

meanings.explanation: Something that is [insignificant] is very small or not important, so it is not worth worrying about.

examples.english: The scratch on my bike is [insignificant] - you can barely see it.
examples.chinese: 我自行车上的划痕[微不足道]——你几乎看不出来。

examples.english: Don't worry about such [insignificant] problems.
examples.chinese: 别为这种[不重要的]小事操心。

examples.english: The extra cost was [insignificant], so we didn't mind paying it.
examples.chinese: 额外的费用[很少]，所以我们不介意付这笔钱。

meanings.explanation: An [instructor] is a person whose job is to teach people a practical skill or sport.

examples.english: My [instructor] taught me how to swim last summer.
examples.chinese: 去年夏天[教练]教会了我游泳。

examples.english: The dance [instructor] showed us some new moves.
examples.chinese: 舞蹈[老师]给我们演示了一些新动作。

examples.english: Our driving [instructor] is very kind and patient.
examples.chinese: 我们的驾驶[教练]非常友善和有耐心。

meanings.explanation: If someone or something [inspires] you, they give you a strong feeling of wanting to do something, often by making you feel excited or enthusiastic about it.

examples.english: My teacher's story [inspired] me to read more books.
examples.chinese: 老师的故事[激励]我读更多的书。

examples.english: My mom always [inspires] me to be a kind person.
examples.chinese: 妈妈总是[鼓励]我做一个善良的人。

examples.english: The movie about space [inspired] many children to become scientists.
examples.chinese: 那部关于太空的电影[激发]了很多孩子成为科学家的梦想。

meanings.explanation: If someone or something [inspires] a particular feeling or emotion in a person, they make that person feel it strongly.

examples.english: Her kind words [inspired] hope in everyone.
examples.chinese: 她温暖的话语让大家心中充满了[希望]。

examples.english: The beautiful song [inspired] a feeling of peace in me.
examples.chinese: 这首动听的歌让我感到一种[宁静]。

examples.english: His bravery [inspired] confidence in the whole team.
examples.chinese: 他的勇敢[唤起]了整个团队的信心。

meanings.explanation: If something is [integral] to a system, plan, or situation, it is an essential part of it and the whole thing cannot work properly without it.

examples.english: Reading is an [integral] part of learning a language.
examples.chinese: 阅读是学习语言的[不可或缺的]一部分。

examples.english: Teamwork is [integral] to the success of this project.
examples.chinese: 团队合作对这个项目的成功来说[至关重要]。

examples.english: Fruits and vegetables are an [integral] part of a healthy diet.
examples.chinese: 水果和蔬菜是健康饮食的[必不可少的部分]。

meanings.explanation: In mathematics, an [integral] is a way of calculating the area under a curve or the total value when something changes continuously.

examples.english: We learned how to calculate an [integral] in math class today.
examples.chinese: 今天数学课上我们学了怎么算[积分]。

examples.english: Finding the [integral] of this function is not easy.
examples.chinese: 求这个函数的[积分]不太容易。

examples.english: The teacher said the [integral] helps us find the total area.
examples.chinese: 老师说[积分]能帮我们求出总面积。

meanings.explanation: An [insolent] person is extremely rude and does not show any respect to someone who is older or in a position of authority.

examples.english: The [insolent] boy talked back to his teacher.
examples.chinese: 这个[无礼的]男孩跟老师顶嘴了。

examples.english: The [insolent] customer yelled at the waiter.
examples.chinese: 那个[蛮横的]顾客对服务员大喊大叫。

examples.english: My cousin apologized for his [insolent] remark yesterday.
examples.chinese: 我表弟为他昨天[无礼的]言论道歉了。

meanings.explanation: Something that is [intelligible] is clear enough to be understood.

examples.english: The teacher's explanation was [intelligible], so everyone understood it.
examples.chinese: 老师的解释[清楚易懂]，所以大家都听懂了。

examples.english: His speech was not [intelligible] because he spoke too fast.
examples.chinese: 他的讲话[让人听不清]，因为他说得太快了。

examples.english: This textbook uses simple words to make the ideas [intelligible].
examples.chinese: 这本教科书使用简单的词语，让概念[容易理解]。

meanings.explanation: If someone or an animal is [injured], they have suffered physical harm to part of their body, usually because of an accident.

examples.english: The [injured] dog was taken to the animal hospital.
examples.chinese: 这只[受伤的]狗狗被送去了动物医院。

examples.english: The little boy helped the [injured] man stand up.
examples.chinese: 小男孩扶起了[受伤的]男士。

examples.english: She wrapped a bandage around the [injured] finger.
examples.chinese: 她给[受伤的]手指缠上了绷带。

meanings.explanation: If your feelings, heart, or emotions are [injured], you feel upset because of something unkind someone has said or done to you.

examples.english: Her [injured] feelings made her sad all day.
examples.chinese: 她[受伤的]情绪让她伤心了一整天。

examples.english: He tried to cheer up her [injured] heart.
examples.chinese: 他努力让她[受伤的]心重新开心起来。

examples.english: A warm hug can fix [injured] feelings.
examples.chinese: 一个温暖的拥抱就能抚慰[受伤的]感情。

meanings.explanation: If you [inquire] about something or someone, you ask for information about them.

examples.english: I went to the school office to [inquire] about my missing schoolbag.
examples.chinese: 我去学校办公室[询问]我丢失书包的事情。

examples.english: My mom called to [inquire] after my teacher's recent illness.
examples.chinese: 我妈妈打电话来[询问]我老师最近的病情。

examples.english: Can I [inquire] whether this shop sells fresh bread?
examples.chinese: 我可以[询问]这家店有没有卖新鲜面包吗？

meanings.explanation: If you [inquire] into a matter or event, you investigate it to find out the truth.

examples.english: The police will [inquire] into the cause of the traffic accident.
examples.chinese: 警察会[调查]这起交通事故的原因。

examples.english: The teacher promised to [inquire] into who broke the classroom window.
examples.chinese: 老师答应会[调查]是谁打碎了教室的窗户。

examples.english: They set up a special team to [inquire] into the unexpected event.
examples.chinese: 他们成立了一个专门小组来[调查]这起突发事件。

meanings.explanation: [Intense] means having a very strong effect or felt very strongly.

examples.english: The summer sun gave off [intense] heat.
examples.chinese: 夏日的太阳散发着[强烈的]热量。

examples.english: She felt an [intense] pain in her finger.
examples.chinese: 她感到手指一阵[剧烈的]疼痛。

examples.english: The fire gave off [intense] heat.
examples.chinese: 火发出[强烈的]热气。

meanings.explanation: An [intense] person is someone who shows strong feelings or opinions; extremely serious about something.

examples.english: He gave me an [intense] look before the test.
examples.chinese: 考试前他给了我一个[专注的]眼神。

examples.english: My teacher is [intense] about keeping the classroom clean.
examples.chinese: 我的老师[十分重视]保持教室干净整洁。

examples.english: She is very [intense] when she plays the piano.
examples.chinese: 她弹钢琴时非常[投入]。

common_collocations: have no intention of doing something

meanings.explanation: An [intention] is a plan or desire that you have in your mind to do something.

examples.english: I have no [intention] of going out in the rain.
examples.chinese: 我没[打算]冒雨出门。

examples.english: She went to the store with the [intention] of buying a birthday gift.
examples.chinese: 她去商店，[打算]买一份生日礼物。

examples.english: His [intention] was to finish his homework before dinner.
examples.chinese: 他[打算]在晚饭前把作业写完。

meanings.explanation: If you do something with good [intention]s, you mean well, even if the result is not perfect.

examples.english: He helped the old lady across the street with good [intentions].
examples.chinese: 他出于[好意]，扶那位老奶奶过了马路。

examples.english: Mom made soup for me with the best [intentions], but it tasted terrible.
examples.chinese: 妈妈出于一片[好意]给我炖了汤，但味道实在太差了。

examples.english: Don't be angry at him — his [intentions] were good.
examples.chinese: 别生他的气——他的[出发点]是好的。

meanings.explanation: An [innovation] is a new idea, method, or invention that is introduced for the first time.

examples.english: The smartphone was a great [innovation] that changed how we talk to each other.
examples.chinese: 智能手机是一项伟大的[创新]，改变了我们互相交流的方式。

examples.english: This new pencil has a clever [innovation] — an eraser on both ends.
examples.chinese: 这支新铅笔有一个巧妙的[创新]——两头都有橡皮。

examples.english: Our school's latest [innovation] is a garden where students grow vegetables.
examples.chinese: 我们学校最新的[创新]是一个学生种菜的花园。

meanings.explanation: [Innovation] is the activity or process of introducing new ideas, methods, or products.

examples.english: [Innovation] helps make our daily lives better and easier.
examples.chinese: [创新]让我们的日常生活更美好、更便捷。

examples.english: Their [innovation] impressed the judges at the science fair.
examples.chinese: 他们的[创新]给科学展的评委留下了深刻印象。

examples.english: Many companies believe [innovation] is the key to success.
examples.chinese: 很多公司认为[创新]是成功的关键。

meanings.explanation: An [installation] is the act of putting equipment or furniture in place so that it can be used, or the process of setting up software on a computer.

examples.english: The [installation] of the new air conditioner took two hours.
examples.chinese: 新空调的[安装]花了两小时。

examples.english: We watched the [installation] of the new window in our living room.
examples.chinese: 我们看着工人[安装]客厅里的新窗户。

examples.english: The [installation] was done by a very friendly technician.
examples.chinese: [安装]是由一位非常友好的技术员完成的。

meanings.explanation: An [installation] is also a piece of equipment or a system that has been put in place, especially a military or industrial one.

examples.english: Our school has a new computer [installation] in the lab.
examples.chinese: 我们学校的实验室里有一套新的电脑[设备]。

examples.english: The army [installation] is located far from the city.
examples.chinese: 那个军事[设施]位于远离城市的地方。

examples.english: This is a beautiful art [installation] in the museum.
examples.chinese: 这是博物馆里一个很美的艺术[装置]。

meanings.explanation: When something exists or occurs [intangibly], it cannot be touched or physically grasped by the senses.

examples.english: The warm air [intangibly] surrounds us on a sunny day.
examples.chinese: 晴天里，暖空气[无形地]环绕着我们。

examples.english: The sweet scent of roses [intangibly] fills the whole house.
examples.chinese: 玫瑰的甜香[无形地]填满了整座房子。

examples.english: Wind moves [intangibly] but we can feel it on our skin.
examples.chinese: 风[无形地]流动着，但我们能在皮肤上感觉到它。

meanings.explanation: When something affects or changes people [intangibly], it cannot be easily defined or clearly understood by the mind because it is vague or abstract.

examples.english: Mom's love [intangibly] makes me feel safe and happy every day.
examples.chinese: 妈妈的爱[无形地]让我每天都感到安全和快乐。

examples.english: The friendship between us [intangibly] grows stronger every year.
examples.chinese: 我们之间的友谊每年都[无形地]变得更深厚。

examples.english: Small acts of kindness can [intangibly] make the world a better place.
examples.chinese: 小小的善举能[无形地]让世界变得更美好。

meanings.explanation: An [infection] is a disease or illness that is caused by very small germs, such as bacteria or viruses, getting into your body.

examples.english: Wash your hands to prevent [infection].
examples.chinese: 洗手可以预防[感染]。

examples.english: The doctor said the [infection] will go away after a few days.
examples.chinese: 医生说过几天[感染]就会好。

examples.english: The [infection] was so bad that she had to see the doctor.
examples.chinese: [感染]太严重了，她只好去看医生。

meanings.explanation: A computer [infection] is a problem caused by a harmful program, such as a virus, that gets into a computer and causes damage.

examples.english: A computer [infection] can damage your files.
examples.chinese: 电脑[感染]可能会损坏你的文件。

examples.english: The [infection] spread quickly to all the office computers.
examples.chinese: 这次[感染]迅速扩散到了办公室里所有的电脑。

examples.english: This software can protect your computer from [infection].
examples.chinese: 这款软件可以保护你的电脑免受[感染]。

meanings.explanation: If you [interfere], you try to influence or involve yourself in a situation where you have no right to, especially in order to change what someone else is doing.

examples.english: Don't [interfere] in other people's business.
examples.chinese: 不要[干涉]别人的事情。

examples.english: The noise from outside [interfered] with my study.
examples.chinese: 外面的噪音[干扰]了我的学习。

examples.english: Parents shouldn't [interfere] too much in their children's lives.
examples.chinese: 父母不应该太[干涉]孩子的生活。

meanings.explanation: If you [interrupt] someone, you say or do something that stops them from continuing what they are saying or doing.

examples.english: Please don't [interrupt] when someone is talking.
examples.chinese: 别人说话的时候请不要[打断]。

examples.english: He [interrupted] me in the middle of my story.
examples.chinese: 他在我讲故事讲到一半的时候[打断]了我。

examples.english: It's rude to [interrupt] others when they are speaking.
examples.chinese: 别人说话时[打断]别人是不礼貌的。

meanings.explanation: If something [interrupts] an activity, event, or process, it stops it for a short time.

examples.english: The rain [interrupted] our picnic.
examples.chinese: 下雨[打断了]我们的野餐。

examples.english: A phone call [interrupted] my homework.
examples.chinese: 一个电话[打断了]我做作业。

examples.english: A loud noise [interrupted] the quiet class.
examples.chinese: 一声巨响[打断了]安静的课堂。

meanings.explanation: If you [intend] to do something, you have decided or planned to do it.

examples.english: I [intend] to finish my homework before dinner.
examples.chinese: 我[打算]在晚饭前完成作业。

examples.english: She [intends] to become a doctor when she grows up.
examples.chinese: 她[打算]长大后当一名医生。

examples.english: We [intend] to visit our grandparents this weekend.
examples.chinese: 我们[打算]这个周末去看爷爷奶奶。

meanings.explanation: If something is [intended] for a particular purpose or person, it is made or designed for that purpose or person.

examples.english: This picture book is [intended] for young children.
examples.chinese: 这本绘本是[专为]小孩子创作的。

examples.english: The small chairs are [intended] for the kids to sit on.
examples.chinese: 这些小椅子是[留给]孩子们坐的。

examples.english: This simple map is [intended] to help you find the way.
examples.chinese: 这张简单的地图是[为了]帮你认路的。

meanings.explanation: If something is [instant], it happens or is done immediately, with no delay at all.

examples.english: I want an [instant] answer to my question.
examples.chinese: 我想要一个[即时]的回答。

examples.english: This is [instant] coffee — just add hot water and it's ready.
examples.chinese: 这是[速溶]咖啡——加热水就可以喝了。

examples.english: Dad pressed the button and got an [instant] reply on his phone.
examples.chinese: 爸爸按下按钮，手机上就收到了[即时]回复。

meanings.explanation: An [instant] is a very short period of time, almost too quick to measure.

examples.english: For one [instant], I saw a shooting star in the sky.
examples.chinese: [一瞬间]，我看到天空中有一颗流星。

examples.english: She stopped for an [instant] before crossing the street.
examples.chinese: 过马路前她停了[片刻]。

examples.english: In that [instant], the puppy jumped into my arms.
examples.chinese: 就在那一[瞬间]，小狗跳进了我的怀里。

meanings.explanation: An [international] activity, event, or situation involves two or more countries or happens between countries.

examples.english: Our school has an [international] day where students share food from different countries.
examples.chinese: 我们学校有一个[国际]日，学生们会分享来自不同国家的食物。

examples.english: My dad goes on [international] trips for his work.
examples.chinese: 我爸爸因为工作需要经常进行[国际]旅行。

examples.english: The airport has an [international] terminal for flights to other countries.
examples.chinese: 机场有一个[国际]航站楼，用于飞往其他国家的航班。

meanings.explanation: An [international] is a person who takes part in matches between teams from different countries.

examples.english: He is an [international] who plays football for his country.
examples.chinese: 他是一名[国脚]，代表他的国家踢足球。

examples.english: The team has three [internationals] who played in the World Cup.
examples.chinese: 这支球队有三名参加过世界杯的[国际球员]。

examples.english: She became an [international] at the age of eighteen.
examples.chinese: 她十八岁时就成为了[国家队选手]。

meanings.explanation: If someone or something [interrupted] an activity, they stopped it for a period of time by causing a noise or disturbance.

examples.english: The teacher [interrupted] the class to announce a fire drill.
examples.chinese: 老师[打断]了课堂，宣布要进行消防演习。

examples.english: Sorry to [interrupted] you, but there's an urgent phone call.
examples.chinese: 抱歉[打扰]一下，有紧急电话找您。

examples.english: The game was [interrupted] by heavy rain for an hour.
examples.chinese: 比赛因大雨[中断]了一个小时。

meanings.explanation: Something that is [interrupted] has been stopped or broken, and does not continue in a smooth or continuous way.

examples.english: The TV show had an [interrupted] broadcast due to technical problems.
examples.chinese: 电视节目因为技术问题[中断]播出了。

examples.english: She spoke in an [interrupted] voice because she kept crying.
examples.chinese: 她说话[断断续续]，因为一直哭。

examples.english: His [interrupted] sleep made him feel tired the next day.
examples.chinese: 他[被打断的]睡眠让他第二天感到很累。

meanings.explanation: An [interpreter] is a person who translates spoken words from one language to another, helping people who speak different languages communicate with each other.

examples.english: The [interpreter] helped the foreign tourist talk to our local guide.
examples.chinese: 这位[口译员]帮外国游客和我们的当地导游沟通。

examples.english: My aunt works as an [interpreter] at an international organization.
examples.chinese: 我阿姨在一家国际组织当[口译员]。

examples.english: We need an [interpreter] to understand what the French guest is saying.
examples.chinese: 我们需要一名[口译员]来听懂这位法国客人在说什么。

meanings.explanation: An [interpreter] is a person who explains or clarifies the meaning of something such as art, poetry, or confusing ideas.

examples.english: He is an [interpreter] of ancient Chinese poetry for young readers.
examples.chinese: 他是给年轻读者解读中国古诗的[诠释者]。

examples.english: The painter acted as his own [interpreter] when people asked about his work.
examples.chinese: 当人们问起他的作品时，这位画家当起了自己的[诠释者]。

examples.english: She is a thoughtful [interpreter] of children's inner thoughts.
examples.chinese: 她是一位能深刻理解孩子内心想法的[诠释者]。

meanings.explanation: You use [initially] to describe something that happens at the beginning of a process or situation, especially when it is not what happens later.

examples.english: I was [initially] too shy to speak in class, but now I love answering questions.
examples.chinese: [一开始]我太害羞不敢在班上发言，但现在我很喜欢回答问题。

examples.english: The weather was [initially] rainy, but later the sun came out.
examples.chinese: 天气[起初]下着雨，不过后来太阳出来了。

examples.english: My mom [initially] said no to getting a dog, but then she changed her mind.
examples.chinese: 我妈妈[最初]不同意养狗，但后来她改主意了。

meanings.explanation: If you do something [intensively], you do it with a great deal of effort, concentration, or activity over a period of time.

examples.english: I trained [intensively] for the 100-meter race last month.
examples.chinese: 上个月我为百米赛跑[刻苦地]训练。

examples.english: My sister practiced [intensively] to pass her piano test.
examples.chinese: 我姐姐为了通过钢琴考试[集中精力地]练习。

examples.english: We worked [intensively] to finish our class project before the holiday.
examples.chinese: 我们[集中全力地]工作，赶在假期前完成了班级项目。

meanings.explanation: If land or animals are farmed [intensively], they are managed in a way that produces as much food as possible, often using chemicals or artificial methods.

examples.english: This big farm grows vegetables [intensively] to feed more people.
examples.chinese: 这个大农场[集约化地]种植蔬菜，来养活更多人。

examples.english: Many chickens are raised [intensively] on this modern farm.
examples.chinese: 这个现代化农场[集中化地]饲养了很多鸡。

examples.english: Farmers grow corn [intensively] to get more harvest every year.
examples.chinese: 农民们[集约化地]种植玉米，每年都能获得更多收成。

meanings.explanation: If you [invent] something such as a machine or a new way of doing things, you are the first person to think of it or make it.

examples.english: Who [invented] the telephone?
examples.chinese: 是谁[发明]了电话？

examples.english: My brother likes to [invent] new games to play with me.
examples.chinese: 我哥哥喜欢[发明]新游戏跟我一起玩。

examples.english: The teacher asked us to [invent] a useful tool for the classroom.
examples.chinese: 老师让我们为教室[发明]一种有用的工具。

meanings.explanation: If you [invent] a story, excuse, or reason, you make it up in order to deceive someone.

examples.english: He [invented] a story about why he was late.
examples.chinese: 他[编造]了一个迟到的理由。

examples.english: Don't [invent] excuses for not doing your homework.
examples.chinese: 别[编造]不做作业的借口。

examples.english: She [invented] an imaginary friend to talk to.
examples.chinese: 她[编造]了一个想象中的朋友来聊天。

meanings.explanation: If you describe someone or their behavior as [insensitive], you mean that they do not notice or care about other people's feelings, and they often say or do things that upset or offend others.

examples.english: He made an [insensitive] joke and his friend felt hurt.
examples.chinese: 他开了个[不体贴]的玩笑，朋友感到受伤了。

examples.english: Mom said it was [insensitive] to eat all the cake without sharing.
examples.chinese: 妈妈说一个人把蛋糕全吃了不分享是[不体贴]的。

examples.english: The [insensitive] boy kept talking loudly while others were sleeping.
examples.chinese: 那个[不体贴]的男孩在别人睡觉时还大声说话。

meanings.explanation: If you are [insensitive] to a physical sensation or condition, you are not affected by it or do not feel it easily.

examples.english: After playing in the snow, his fingers became [insensitive] to the cold.
examples.chinese: 在雪地里玩完后，他的手指对寒冷变得[没感觉]了。

examples.english: Some people are [insensitive] to the pain of a small cut.
examples.chinese: 有些人对小伤口的疼痛[没感觉]。

examples.english: The dentist gave him a shot so his mouth would be [insensitive] to pain.
examples.chinese: 牙医给他打了一针，这样他的嘴就对疼痛[没感觉]了。

meanings.explanation: An [introverted] person is quiet, shy, and prefers to spend time alone rather than with others.

examples.english: My sister is [introverted] and enjoys reading books alone in her room.
examples.chinese: 我姐姐很[内向]，喜欢一个人待在房间里看书。

examples.english: Tom is too [introverted] to speak in front of the whole class.
examples.chinese: 汤姆太[内向]了，不敢在全班同学面前讲话。

examples.english: Although he is [introverted], he has many close friends.
examples.chinese: 虽然他很[内向]，但他有很多好朋友。

meanings.explanation: Something that is [irregular] does not happen at the same time, in the same way, or in the same pattern as usual.

examples.english: He works [irregular] hours, so he sometimes comes home very late.
examples.chinese: 他的工作时间[不规律]，所以有时候很晚才回家。

examples.english: My grandma's heartbeat is [irregular], so the doctor wants to check it.
examples.chinese: 我奶奶的心跳[不规律]，所以医生想给她检查一下。

examples.english: She goes to the swimming pool at [irregular] times.
examples.chinese: 她去游泳池的时间[没什么规律]。

meanings.explanation: Something that is [irregular] does not follow the usual rules, patterns, or shapes.

examples.english: "Go" and "went" are [irregular] verbs in English.
examples.chinese: "go" 和 "went" 是英语中的[不规则]动词。

examples.english: This stone has an [irregular] shape, not round at all.
examples.chinese: 这块石头的形状[不规则的]，一点都不圆。

examples.english: The garden has an [irregular] shape like a big letter L.
examples.chinese: 这个花园的形状是[不规则的]，像一个大写字母 L。

meanings.explanation: [Internal] describes something that exists or happens inside a place, object, or organization.

examples.english: The doctor used a machine to check my [internal] organs.
examples.chinese: 医生用机器检查了我的[内部]器官。

examples.english: Our school had an [internal] meeting for teachers only.
examples.chinese: 我们学校开了一个只限老师参加的[内部]会议。

examples.english: The toy has many [internal] parts that you cannot see.
examples.chinese: 这个玩具有很多你看不到的[内部]零件。

meanings.explanation: [Internal] describes feelings, thoughts, or experiences that happen inside your mind or heart, rather than on the outside.

examples.english: She felt an [internal] happiness that no one could see.
examples.chinese: 她感受到一种别人看不到的[内心]快乐。

examples.english: He had an [internal] struggle about telling the truth.
examples.chinese: 要不要说实话，他[内心]很挣扎。

examples.english: My [internal] voice told me to keep trying.
examples.chinese: 我[内心]的声音告诉我继续努力。

meanings.explanation: An [invader] is a person or armed force that enters another country or region by force to take control of it.

examples.english: The [invader] tried to take control of the small village.
examples.chinese: 这名[入侵者]试图占领这个小村庄。

examples.english: Local people fought bravely against the [invader].
examples.chinese: 当地人民勇敢地抗击这名[入侵者]。

examples.english: The old castle was built to keep out [invader]s.
examples.chinese: 这座古老的城堡是为了抵御[入侵者]而修建的。

meanings.explanation: An [invader] is a plant, animal, or thing that enters a place where it is not wanted and causes damage or harm.

examples.english: This foreign [invader] is killing all our local plants.
examples.chinese: 这种外来[入侵者]正在杀死所有本地植物。

examples.english: Ants can be an unwelcome [invader] in your kitchen.
examples.chinese: 蚂蚁可能是厨房里不受欢迎的[入侵者]。

examples.english: We must work together to stop this [invader] from spreading.
examples.chinese: 我们必须一起阻止这种[入侵者]扩散。

common_collocations: don't judge a book by its cover

meanings.explanation: A [judge] is a person who is in charge of a court of law and decides how the law should be applied. It can also refer to someone who decides the winner of a contest or competition.

examples.english: The [judge] asked the man to tell the truth in court.
examples.chinese: [法官]在法庭上要求那个男人说实话。

examples.english: The [judge] said the winner of the singing contest is Lily.
examples.chinese: [评委]宣布歌唱比赛的冠军是莉莉。

examples.english: My mom is the [judge] of our family talent show.
examples.chinese: 我妈妈是我们家庭才艺表演的[评委]。

meanings.explanation: If you [judge] someone or something, you form an opinion about them based on what you see or know. It can also mean to decide the winner of a competition.

examples.english: Don't [judge] people by how they look.
examples.chinese: 不要以貌[取人]。

examples.english: You shouldn't [judge] a book by its cover.
examples.chinese: 你不应该凭封面来[评判]一本书。

examples.english: The teacher will [judge] the students' drawings and pick the best one.
examples.chinese: 老师会[评选]学生们的画，选出最好的那一幅。

meanings.explanation: A [junior] person is younger in age or has a lower rank or position than someone else.

examples.english: My sister is [junior] to me, so she is younger.
examples.chinese: 我妹妹比我[年龄小]，所以她年龄更小。

examples.english: He is the [junior] member of the basketball team.
examples.chinese: 他是篮球队里[最年轻的]队员。

examples.english: In swimming class, the [junior] kids use the small pool.
examples.chinese: 在游泳课里，[年龄小的]孩子们用小泳池。

meanings.explanation: A [junior] is a young person who takes part in sports or activities for younger age groups.

examples.english: My brother plays on the [junior] soccer team.
examples.chinese: 我哥哥在[少年]足球队踢球。

examples.english: She joined the [junior] chess club after school.
examples.chinese: 放学后她加入了[少年]象棋俱乐部。

examples.english: The [junior] swimmers practice every Saturday.
examples.chinese: [少年]游泳队员每周六训练。

meanings.explanation: If a situation, activity, or plan [involves] something, that thing is a necessary part or result of it.

examples.english: The game [involves] running and catching a ball.
examples.chinese: 这个游戏[需要]跑和接球。

examples.english: Making cookies [involves] mixing flour and sugar.
examples.chinese: 做饼干[需要]把面粉和糖混合在一起。

examples.english: This job [involves] talking to many people every day.
examples.chinese: 这份工作[需要]每天和很多人交谈。

meanings.explanation: If you [involve] someone in something, you ask or allow them to take part in it or to help with it.

examples.english: Please [involve] me in your team game.
examples.chinese: 请[让]我[加入]你们的团队游戏。

examples.english: Mom always [involves] us in cooking dinner.
examples.chinese: 妈妈总是[叫]我们[一起]做晚饭。

examples.english: The teacher wants to [involve] every student in the class discussion.
examples.chinese: 老师想让每个学生都[参与]课堂讨论。

meanings.explanation: Something that is [invisible] cannot be seen.

examples.english: The wind is [invisible] but we can feel it.
examples.chinese: 风是[看不见的]，但我们能感觉到它。

examples.english: Some tiny germs are [invisible] to the naked eye.
examples.chinese: 有些小细菌是肉眼[看不见的]。

examples.english: The magic trick made the rabbit become [invisible].
examples.chinese: 魔术让兔子[隐形]了。

meanings.explanation: An [issue] is an important subject or problem that people are talking about or trying to deal with.

examples.english: We need to talk about this [issue] with our teacher.
examples.chinese: 我们需要和老师谈谈这个[问题]。

examples.english: Pollution is a big [issue] in our city.
examples.chinese: 污染是我们城市的一个大[问题]。

examples.english: She has a health [issue] and needs to see a doctor.
examples.chinese: 她有一个健康[问题]，需要去看医生。

meanings.explanation: If you [issue] something, you officially produce it, give it out, or make it known.

examples.english: The school will [issue] new student ID cards next week.
examples.chinese: 学校下周将[发放]新的学生证。

examples.english: The library [issued] a notice about the new opening hours.
examples.chinese: 图书馆[发布了]关于新开放时间的通知。

examples.english: The government plans to [issue] a report on air quality.
examples.chinese: 政府计划[发布]一份关于空气质量的报告。

meanings.explanation: A [kangaroo] is a large Australian animal with a long, thick tail and strong back legs that it uses for jumping.

examples.english: The [kangaroo] jumped across the field with its baby in its pouch.
examples.chinese: 那只[袋鼠]带着育儿袋里的宝宝跳过了田野。

examples.english: We saw a big grey [kangaroo] at the zoo yesterday.
examples.chinese: 我们昨天在动物园看到一只大灰[袋鼠]。

examples.english: A [kangaroo] can jump higher than a tall fence.
examples.chinese: [袋鼠]能跳得比高高的栅栏还高。

meanings.explanation: [Kindness] is the quality of being friendly, generous, and caring towards other people. If someone shows [kindness], they behave in a warm and thoughtful way.

examples.english: My grandma always treats everyone with [kindness].
examples.chinese: 我奶奶总是用[善良]对待每一个人。

examples.english: She thanked the teacher for her [kindness] and help.
examples.chinese: 她感谢老师的[善意]和帮助。

examples.english: His [kindness] made the new student feel welcome.
examples.chinese: 他的[友善]让新同学感到很受欢迎。

meanings.explanation: A [kindness] is a kind, helpful, or considerate act that you do for someone else. When you do someone a [kindness], you help them or do something nice for them.

examples.english: It was very kind of you to do me such a [kindness].
examples.chinese: 你帮了我这么大的忙，真是太好了，这份[善举]我很感激。

examples.english: She did me a great [kindness] by carrying my heavy bag.
examples.chinese: 她帮我拎了很重的包，真是帮了我一个大[忙]。

examples.english: He helps old people cross the road as a small [kindness].
examples.chinese: 他扶老人过马路，算是一点小小的[善举]。

derived_forms: knock out (phrasal v.) - 击倒；淘汰
knocked-out (adj.) - 被击倒的；筋疲力尽的

meanings.explanation: A [knockout] is a punch that makes someone fall unconscious, especially in boxing. It is also used to describe something or someone that is very attractive or impressive.

examples.english: The boxer won the match with a powerful [knockout].
examples.chinese: 那名拳击手一记重拳[击倒]对手，赢得了比赛。

examples.english: She is a total [knockout] in that red dress.
examples.chinese: 她穿那条红色连衣裙，真是[美极了]。

examples.english: The new phone design was a [knockout] at the tech show.
examples.chinese: 那款新手机设计在科技展上[惊艳全场]。

meanings.explanation: If you describe someone or something as [knockout], you mean they are extremely attractive or impressive.

examples.english: That's a [knockout] idea!
examples.chinese: 这主意[太棒了]！

examples.english: He showed a [knockout] performance on stage.
examples.chinese: 他在舞台上的表演[令人叫绝]。

examples.english: She gave a [knockout] smile that everyone loved.
examples.chinese: 她露出一个[迷人至极]的笑容人人都喜欢。

meanings.explanation: An [interval] is a period of time between two events or activities.

examples.english: There is a ten-minute [interval] between each class at school.
examples.chinese: 学校里每节课之间有十分钟的[间隔]。

examples.english: After a short [interval], the show started again.
examples.chinese: 短暂的[休息]之后，演出又开始了。

examples.english: We played outside for two hours without an [interval].
examples.chinese: 我们在外面连续玩了两个小时，没有[休息]。

meanings.explanation: An [interval] is a space or gap between two things or points.

examples.english: There is an [interval] of three meters between each tree.
examples.chinese: 每棵树之间有三米的[间隔]。

examples.english: Please leave an [interval] between the desks so we can walk through.
examples.chinese: 请在课桌之间留出[空隙]，方便我们走过去。

examples.english: The houses along the road are built at wide [intervals].
examples.chinese: 沿路的房屋建得[间隔]很宽。

meanings.explanation: If someone is [irresponsible], they do things without thinking about the results or fail to do what they should do.

examples.english: It's [irresponsible] to leave your toys all over the floor.
examples.chinese: [不负责任地]把玩具扔得满地都是可不好。

examples.english: Leaving the window open was [irresponsible] of you.
examples.chinese: 你[不负责任地]没关窗户。

examples.english: He was [irresponsible] for breaking the window and not telling anyone.
examples.chinese: 他打破了窗户却不说出来，真是[不负责任]。

meanings.explanation: You use [least] to indicate that something is smaller in amount, degree, or number than anything else, or the smallest possible amount of something.

examples.english: She ate the [least] amount of food among all the kids.
examples.chinese: 她吃了所有孩子里[最少]的食物。

examples.english: This shirt costs the [least] of all the clothes in the store.
examples.chinese: 这件衬衫是店里所有衣服中[最便宜]的。

examples.english: He does the [least] homework in the whole class.
examples.chinese: 他是全班做作业[最少]的人。

meanings.explanation: You use [least] in phrases like 'at least' to say that something is true or will happen, even if nothing else is true or happens. It is also used to mean 'to the smallest degree'.

examples.english: You should at [least] say sorry to your little sister.
examples.chinese: 你[至少]应该跟妹妹道个歉。

examples.english: This is the game I like the [least].
examples.chinese: 这是我最[不]喜欢的一款游戏。

examples.english: We can visit the park tomorrow, or at [least] this weekend.
examples.chinese: 我们明天可以去公园，[最起码]这个周末能去。

meanings.explanation: A [journal] is a regular written record of your personal experiences, thoughts, and daily activities.

examples.english: I write down my happy things in my [journal] every day.
examples.chinese: 我每天都会把开心的事写在我的[日记]里。

examples.english: Lily keeps a [journal] to remember her trip to the zoo.
examples.chinese: 莉莉写[日记]来记住她去动物园的旅行。

examples.english: My mom bought me a beautiful new [journal] for my birthday.
examples.chinese: 妈妈给我买了一本漂亮的新[日记本]作为生日礼物。

meanings.explanation: A [journal] is a regularly published magazine that contains articles about a specific subject or professional field.

examples.english: My dad reads a science [journal] every month.
examples.chinese: 爸爸每个月都会读一本科学[期刊]。

examples.english: This [journal] has many interesting stories about wild animals.
examples.chinese: 这本[期刊]有很多关于野生动物的有趣故事。

examples.english: The doctor wrote a research paper for a medical [journal].
examples.chinese: 这位医生给一本医学[期刊]写了一篇研究论文。

meanings.explanation: If you [invite] someone to a social event such as a party, a meal, or a special occasion, you ask them to come to it.

examples.english: I want to [invite] my friend to my birthday party.
examples.chinese: 我想[邀请]我的朋友参加我的生日派对。

examples.english: Mom will [invite] the neighbors for dinner tonight.
examples.chinese: 妈妈今晚要[邀请]邻居来吃晚饭。

examples.english: Did you [invite] Lisa to the movie?
examples.chinese: 你[邀请]丽莎去看电影了吗？

meanings.explanation: An [invite] is a spoken or written request asking someone to go to a social event or to take part in something.

examples.english: Tom sent me an [invite] to his birthday party.
examples.chinese: 汤姆给我发了生日派对的[邀请]。

examples.english: Did you get the [invite] from the school?
examples.chinese: 你收到学校的[邀请]了吗？

examples.english: Please reply to the [invite] before Friday.
examples.chinese: 请在周五前回复[邀请]。

meanings.explanation: If you [lend] something that you own, you allow someone else to have it or use it for a period of time, after which they must give it back to you.

examples.english: Can you [lend] me your pencil? I forgot mine at home.
examples.chinese: 你能把铅笔[借]给我吗？我把自己的忘在家里了。

examples.english: My friend will [lend] me his bike for the weekend.
examples.chinese: 我的朋友会把自行车[借]给我周末骑。

examples.english: My mom doesn't like to [lend] books to other people.
examples.chinese: 我妈妈不喜欢把书[借]给别人。

meanings.explanation: If you [lend] a hand, you help someone do something.

examples.english: Everyone, please [lend] a hand and help clean the classroom.
examples.chinese: 请大家[搭把手]，帮忙打扫教室。

examples.english: My brother will [lend] a hand with moving the boxes.
examples.chinese: 我哥哥会[搭把手]，帮忙搬箱子。

examples.english: Can you [lend] a hand carrying these heavy bags?
examples.chinese: 你能[搭把手]提这些重袋子吗？

meanings.explanation: If you [join] an organization, club, or group, you become a member of it.

examples.english: I want to [join] the school art club.
examples.chinese: 我想[加入]学校美术社团。

examples.english: She will [join] the music group next week.
examples.chinese: 她下周要[加入]音乐小组。

examples.english: Did you [join] the football team?
examples.chinese: 你[加入]足球队了吗？

meanings.explanation: If you [join] two things together, you connect them or fasten them together.

examples.english: Use glue to [join] the two pieces of paper.
examples.chinese: 用胶水把这两张纸[粘在一起]。

examples.english: Let's [join] hands and make a circle.
examples.chinese: 咱们[拉起手来]围成一个圈吧。

examples.english: This road [joins] the two towns.
examples.chinese: 这条路把两个镇子[连在一块]。

meanings.explanation: The [last] thing or person is the one that comes after all the others.

examples.english: Monday is the [last] day of our vacation.
examples.chinese: 周一是我们假期的[最后]一天。

examples.english: Please eat the [last] cookie on the plate.
examples.chinese: 请吃掉盘子里[最后]一块饼干。

examples.english: December is the [last] month of the year.
examples.chinese: 十二月是一年[当中最后]的一个月份。

meanings.explanation: If something [lasts], it continues to exist or happen for a particular period of time.

examples.english: The movie will [last] for two hours.
examples.chinese: 这部电影会[持续]两个小时。

examples.english: This big box of crayons can [last] all year.
examples.chinese: 这盒大蜡笔可以[用上一整]年。

examples.english: Good friendships [last] a long time.
examples.chinese: 好的友谊可以[维持]很长时间。

meanings.explanation: When you [leave] a place, you go away from it. It can also mean to allow something to stay in a particular place or condition.

examples.english: I have to [leave] home early tomorrow morning.
examples.chinese: 明天早上我得早早[离开]家。

examples.english: Please [leave] your shoes at the door.
examples.chinese: 请把鞋子[放在]门口。

examples.english: Don't [leave] the lights on when you go out.
examples.chinese: 出门的时候别[让]灯[开着]。

meanings.explanation: To [leave] something to someone means to give it to them after you die, or to pass something on to them.

examples.english: She [left] all her money to her children.
examples.chinese: 她把所有的钱都[留给]了孩子们。

examples.english: The old man [left] his house to the church.
examples.chinese: 那位老人把他的房子[捐赠给]了教堂。

meanings.explanation: [Leave] is time off from work or school that you are allowed to take.

examples.english: I'm taking a week's [leave] to visit my grandmother.
examples.chinese: 我请了一周[假]去看望奶奶。

examples.english: Workers get 20 days of [leave] each year.
examples.chinese: 员工每年有20天[假期]。

examples.english: He asked for [leave] to attend his brother's wedding.
examples.chinese: 他请[假]去参加哥哥的婚礼。

meanings.explanation: To [liberate] someone or something means to set them free from imprisonment, captivity, or any kind of restriction.

examples.english: The rescue team worked hard to [liberate] the dog trapped under the tree.
examples.chinese: 救援队努力[解救]被困在树下的那只狗。

examples.english: Please open the cage and [liberate] the little bird.
examples.chinese: 请打开笼子，[放飞]那只小鸟。

examples.english: Reading books can [liberate] your imagination.
examples.chinese: 读书能[解放]你的想象力。

meanings.explanation: To [liberate] a place, country, or group of people means to free them from the control of an enemy or an oppressive government.

examples.english: The soldiers fought bravely to [liberate] the town.
examples.chinese: 战士们英勇作战，[解放]了那座小镇。

examples.english: Everyone cheered when the city was [liberated].
examples.chinese: 城市被[解放]时，所有人都欢呼起来。

examples.english: The army moved forward to [liberate] the village from enemy control.
examples.chinese: 军队向前推进，[解放]了被敌人控制的村庄。

meanings.explanation: A [load] is an amount of something that is being carried, or the total amount that something can hold or carry. It can also mean a large amount of something.

examples.english: The [load] on my back is too heavy, I need to take a rest.
examples.chinese: 我背上的[东西]太重了，我得休息一下。

examples.english: Mom asked me to take a [load] of clothes out of the washing machine.
examples.chinese: 妈妈让我把洗衣机里的[一桶衣服]拿出来。

examples.english: The truck is full, it has reached its maximum [load].
examples.chinese: 卡车已经满了，达到了最大[载重量]。

meanings.explanation: If you [load] something, you put a large amount of it into or onto something, such as putting things into a vehicle or container.

examples.english: Can you help me [load] these boxes into the car?
examples.chinese: 你能帮我把这些箱子[装]进车里吗？

examples.english: Dad is [loading] the dishwasher after dinner.
examples.chinese: 吃完饭后爸爸正在往洗碗机里[装]碗碟。

examples.english: We need to [load] the van before we leave for the trip.
examples.chinese: 出发旅行之前，我们需要先把[装满]面包车。

meanings.explanation: A [limit] is the greatest amount, number, or level of something that is allowed or possible.

examples.english: There is a speed [limit] of 30 miles per hour on this road.
examples.chinese: 这条路上的[限速]是每小时30英里。

examples.english: I have reached my [limit] and cannot eat any more.
examples.chinese: 我已经到[极限]了，再也吃不下了。

examples.english: The teacher set a time [limit] for the test.
examples.chinese: 老师给考试定了[时间限制]。

meanings.explanation: If you [limit] something, you keep it within a particular size, amount, or area and do not let it go beyond that.

examples.english: Please [limit] your screen time to one hour a day.
examples.chinese: 请把每天看屏幕的时间[限制]在一小时内。

examples.english: We should [limit] how much candy we eat.
examples.chinese: 我们应该[控制]吃糖的量。

examples.english: The school [limits] the number of students in each class.
examples.chinese: 学校把每个班的学生人数[限制]在一定范围内。

meanings.explanation: If you [let slip] a secret or piece of information, you accidentally tell it to someone when you did not mean to.

examples.english: I almost [let slip] that we are planning a surprise party for Mom.
examples.chinese: 我差点[说漏嘴]我们正在给妈妈准备惊喜派对。

examples.english: My brother [let slip] the secret about my new bike.
examples.chinese: 我哥哥[说漏]了关于我新自行车的秘密。

examples.english: She didn't mean to [let slip] the truth.
examples.chinese: 她不是故意[走漏]真相的。

meanings.explanation: If you [let slip] an opportunity or chance, you fail to take it when you have the chance to do so.

examples.english: I [let slip] my chance to go to the zoo last week.
examples.chinese: 我上周[错过]了去动物园的机会。

examples.english: Don't [let slip] this great opportunity to learn swimming.
examples.chinese: 不要[放过]这个学习游泳的好机会。

examples.english: She [let slip] the chance to meet her favorite singer.
examples.chinese: 她[错失]了见到她最喜欢歌手的机会。

meanings.explanation: If you are [keen] to do something or [keen] on something, you are very enthusiastic and eager to do it.

examples.english: I am [keen] on playing badminton with my dad.
examples.chinese: 我很[热衷]于和爸爸打羽毛球。

examples.english: She is [keen] to learn how to bake cookies.
examples.chinese: 她对学习烤饼干很[渴望]。

examples.english: All the children are [keen] to open their Christmas presents.
examples.chinese: 所有孩子都[急切]想要打开圣诞礼物。

meanings.explanation: A [keen] sense, mind, or body part is very sensitive and good at noticing small or clear details.

examples.english: Dogs have a very [keen] sense of smell.
examples.chinese: 狗有着非常[敏锐]的嗅觉。

examples.english: Her [keen] hearing caught the sound of a bird outside.
examples.chinese: 她[敏锐]的听觉捕捉到了外面小鸟的声音。

examples.english: This bird has [keen] eyesight to find small food on the ground.
examples.chinese: 这种鸟有着[锐利]的视力，能找到地面上的细小食物。

meanings.explanation: [Likely] describes something that is expected to happen or be true, but not certain.

examples.english: It is [likely] to rain this afternoon.
examples.chinese: 今天下午[可能]会下雨。

examples.english: She is [likely] to win the game.
examples.chinese: 她[可能]会赢得这场比赛。

examples.english: This is the [likely] answer.
examples.chinese: 这[可能]就是正确答案。

meanings.explanation: [Likely] means probably; in a way that is expected but not certain.

examples.english: I will [likely] go to the park tomorrow.
examples.chinese: 我明天[可能]会去公园。

examples.english: Most [likely], he is already at home.
examples.chinese: [很可能]他已经到家了。

examples.english: She will [likely] finish her homework tonight.
examples.chinese: 她今晚[大概]会完成作业。

meanings.explanation: A [loss] is the fact of no longer having something or of having less of it than before.

examples.english: The [loss] of his favorite toy made the little boy cry.
examples.chinese: 小男孩因为[丢失]了最爱的玩具而哭了。

examples.english: There was a [loss] of power during the storm last night.
examples.chinese: 昨晚暴风雨期间发生了电力[中断]。

examples.english: The [loss] of heat through the window made the room cold.
examples.chinese: 窗户的热量[流失]让房间变冷了。

meanings.explanation: A [loss] is a feeling of sadness when someone you love dies or goes away.

examples.english: She felt a deep [loss] when her grandmother passed away.
examples.chinese: 奶奶去世时，她感到深深的[失落]。

examples.english: The whole family shared their [loss] together.
examples.chinese: 全家人一起分担[悲伤]。

examples.english: Time helps us deal with the [loss] of someone we love.
examples.chinese: 时间帮助我们面对所爱之人的[离世]。

meanings.explanation: Something that is [limited] is restricted in amount, size, or extent and is therefore not very great in quantity or scope.

examples.english: We have a [limited] supply of cookies for the party.
examples.chinese: 我们为派对准备的饼干[数量有限]。

examples.english: The store has a [limited] number of toys on sale.
examples.chinese: 这家商店打折的玩具[数量不多]。

examples.english: My free time is very [limited] during the school week.
examples.chinese: 上学期间我的空闲时间非常[有限]。

meanings.explanation: Something that is [local] relates to a particular area or community, especially the area where you are.

examples.english: We bought fresh vegetables from the [local] market.
examples.chinese: 我们从当地的[菜市场]买了新鲜蔬菜。

examples.english: My mom prefers shopping at [local] stores.
examples.chinese: 我妈妈喜欢在[本地]商店买东西。

examples.english: The [local] school is just a short walk from our house.
examples.chinese: [本地]学校离我们家步行就到了。

meanings.explanation: A [local] is a person who lives in a particular area or place, especially where you are visiting.

examples.english: The [locals] are very friendly to tourists here.
examples.chinese: 这里的[当地人]对游客很友好。

examples.english: As a [local], she knows all the best restaurants.
examples.chinese: 作为[本地人]，她知道所有最好的餐馆。

examples.english: Ask a [local] for directions if you get lost.
examples.chinese: 如果你迷路了，就问问[当地人]路线。

meanings.explanation: [Lunar] means relating to the moon.

examples.english: We looked up at the sky and saw a bright [lunar] glow.
examples.chinese: 我们抬头看天，看到了明亮的[月亮的]光。

examples.english: The astronaut walked on the [lunar] surface for the first time.
examples.chinese: 宇航员第一次在[月球的]表面上行走。

examples.english: People came outside to watch the [lunar] eclipse last night.
examples.chinese: 人们昨晚来到外面观看[月食]。

meanings.explanation: [Lunar] also describes a period of time or a calendar that is based on the cycles of the moon.

examples.english: Chinese New Year follows the [lunar] calendar.
examples.chinese: 中国新年是按照[农历]来定的。

examples.english: The [lunar] month has about twenty-nine or thirty days.
examples.chinese: 一个[太阴月]大约有二十九或三十天。

examples.english: The Mid-Autumn Festival falls on the fifteenth day of the eighth [lunar] month.
examples.chinese: 中秋节在八月[农历]十五。

meanings.explanation: A [leisurely] action is done in a relaxed and unhurried way.

examples.english: We had a [leisurely] breakfast and then went for a walk.
examples.chinese: 我们吃了一顿[悠闲的]早餐，然后出去散了步。

examples.english: They spent a [leisurely] afternoon in the park.
examples.chinese: 他们在公园里度过了[悠闲的]一个下午。

examples.english: He took a [leisurely] bike ride through the countryside.
examples.chinese: 他在乡间进行了一次[悠闲的]骑行。

meanings.explanation: If you do something [leisurely], you do it in a relaxed way without hurrying.

examples.english: He walked [leisurely] down the street, looking at the shops.
examples.chinese: 他[悠闲地]走在街上，看看路边的商店。

examples.english: She ate her lunch [leisurely] while reading a book.
examples.chinese: 她一边看书一边[悠闲地]吃午饭。

examples.english: They sat [leisurely] in the garden, chatting and laughing.
examples.chinese: 他们[悠闲地]坐在花园里，聊着天，笑着。

meanings.explanation: If someone is [involved] in an activity or situation, they take part in it or are closely connected to it.

examples.english: All [involved] students need to go to the auditorium after class.
examples.chinese: 所有[相关]同学下课后都要去礼堂。

examples.english: Many [involved] parents helped decorate the school for Children's Day.
examples.chinese: 许多[相关]家长帮忙装饰学校迎接儿童节。

examples.english: My sister is an [involved] contestant in the city singing competition.
examples.chinese: 我姐姐是城市歌唱比赛的[相关]选手。

meanings.explanation: Something such as a story, problem, or process that is [involved] has many different parts and is difficult to understand or deal with.

examples.english: This puzzle has an [involved] pattern that I can't figure out.
examples.chinese: 这个拼图有一个[复杂]的图案，我拼不出来。

examples.english: The movie's plot is so [involved] that I got lost watching it.
examples.chinese: 这部电影的情节太[复杂]了，我看晕了。

examples.english: This new board game has [involved] rules that I don't understand.
examples.chinese: 这个新桌游有[复杂]的规则，我看不懂。

meanings.explanation: If you [lay] something somewhere, you put it there carefully or neatly.

examples.english: Please [lay] your sweater on the bed.
examples.chinese: 请把你的毛衣[放]在床上。

examples.english: Can you help me [lay] the cups on the table?
examples.chinese: 你能帮我把杯子[摆]在桌子上吗？

examples.english: We need to [lay] the map flat on the floor.
examples.chinese: 我们得把地图[铺]在地板上。

meanings.explanation: [Lay] is the past tense of lie, meaning to rest or be in a flat horizontal position on a surface.

examples.english: I [lay] on the sofa and watched TV yesterday afternoon.
examples.chinese: 昨天下午我[躺]在沙发上看电视。

examples.english: After running, she [lay] under the tree to cool down.
examples.chinese: 跑步结束后，她[躺]在树下乘凉。

examples.english: The lazy cat [lay] still on the warm windowsill.
examples.chinese: 那只懒猫一动不动[躺]在温暖的窗台上。

meanings.explanation: If there is a [lack] of something, there is not enough of it or it does not exist at all.

examples.english: The plants died because of a [lack] of water.
examples.chinese: 这些植物因为[缺水]而枯死了。

examples.english: There is a [lack] of food in some poor countries.
examples.chinese: 一些贫困国家[缺少]食物。

examples.english: She showed a [lack] of interest in the game.
examples.chinese: 她对那个游戏表现出[缺乏]兴趣。

meanings.explanation: If you [lack] something, you do not have enough of it or you do not have it at all.

examples.english: He [lacks] confidence when speaking in front of the class.
examples.chinese: 他在全班同学面前发言时[缺乏]自信。

examples.english: The soup [lacks] salt.
examples.chinese: 这汤[缺]盐。

examples.english: She [lacks] experience but works very hard.
examples.chinese: 她虽然[缺乏]经验，但工作很努力。

meanings.explanation: Used to describe the most important or largest thing of a group.

examples.english: The [main] reason I came here is to see you.
examples.chinese: 我来这里[主要]是因为想见你。

examples.english: What is the [main] dish for dinner today?
examples.chinese: 今天晚餐的[主]菜是什么？

examples.english: The [main] door is closed, let's use the side door.
examples.chinese: [正]门关着，我们走侧门吧。

meanings.explanation: A large pipe or cable that carries water, gas, or electricity to a building.

examples.english: The water [main] burst yesterday.
examples.chinese: 昨天水管（[主管]）爆了。

examples.english: They are fixing the gas [main] now.
examples.chinese: 他们现在在修煤气[主管道]。

examples.english: Turn off the water at the [main] before you fix anything.
examples.chinese: 修东西之前先把水[总阀]关掉。

meanings.explanation: If you [manage] to do something difficult, you succeed in doing it.

examples.english: I can [manage] to tie my shoes by myself.
examples.chinese: 我自己[会]系鞋带了。

examples.english: She [managed] to finish her homework before dinner.
examples.chinese: 她[成功做]完作业才吃晚饭。

examples.english: We [managed] to find the lost puppy.
examples.chinese: 我们[终于]找到了走失的小狗。

meanings.explanation: To [manage] a business or a group of people means to be in charge of them.

examples.english: My mom [manages] the school store.
examples.chinese: 我妈妈[管理]学校的小卖部。

examples.english: Our coach knows how to [manage] the team well.
examples.chinese: 我们的教练很会[管理]球队。

examples.english: Who [manages] this computer lab?
examples.chinese: 谁[负责管理]这间电脑教室？

meanings.explanation: [Mamma] is an informal and affectionate word for 'mother.' Children often use [mamma] to call or talk about their mom, especially in a warm and loving way.

examples.english: I drew this picture for my [mamma].
examples.chinese: 我给我[妈妈]画了这幅画。

examples.english: [Mamma], can you read me a bedtime story?
examples.chinese: [妈妈]，你能给我念一个睡前故事吗？

examples.english: My [mamma] always packs a snack for me before school.
examples.chinese: 我[妈妈]上学前总会给我装一份小零食。

meanings.explanation: If you [maintain] something, you keep it in good condition or working order by taking care of it regularly.

examples.english: My dad [maintains] our family car every month.
examples.chinese: 我爸爸每个月都[保养]我们家的车。

examples.english: You must [maintain] your bicycle to ride it safely.
examples.chinese: 你必须[保养]你的自行车才能安全骑行。

examples.english: The park worker [maintains] the playground every week.
examples.chinese: park工作人员每周都[维护]游乐场。

meanings.explanation: If you [maintain] something at a particular level or rate, you keep it at that level or rate and do not let it change.

examples.english: Please [maintain] silence in the library.
examples.chinese: 请在图书馆[保持]安静。

examples.english: I try to [maintain] a healthy diet every day.
examples.chinese: 我每天都努力[保持]健康的饮食。

examples.english: It is hard to [maintain] good grades.
examples.chinese: [保持]好成绩很难。

meanings.explanation: You use [literally] to indicate that a word or phrase is being used in its exact, original sense, rather than a figurative or exaggerated one.

examples.english: When I said I "died laughing", I wasn't speaking [literally].
examples.chinese: 当我说我“笑死了”的时候，我不是[按字面]说的。

examples.english: You need to read this rule [literally] to follow it correctly.
examples.chinese: 你必须[按字面]理解这条规则才能正确遵守。

examples.english: The word "apple" [literally] means a kind of fruit, not a technology company.
examples.chinese: "苹果"这个词[字面上]指的是一种水果，不是一家科技公司。

meanings.explanation: You use [literally] to emphasize an exaggerated or vivid statement, even though you know it is not true in the exact literal sense.

examples.english: I've [literally] told you a hundred times to clean your room.
examples.chinese: 我[简直]已经告诉你一百遍要打扫你的房间了。

examples.english: I was [literally] dying of laughter when I heard that joke.
examples.chinese: 听到那个笑话时，我[简直]要笑死了。

examples.english: This backpack is [literally] a ton heavy—I can't carry it.
examples.chinese: 这个背包[简直]有一吨重——我拎不动。

meanings.explanation: You use [mainly] to say that something is true for the most part, or to emphasize the most important reason, fact, or feature of something.

examples.english: I [mainly] eat fruit for breakfast.
examples.chinese: 我早餐[主要]吃水果。

examples.english: This book is [mainly] about animals.
examples.chinese: 这本书[主要]是关于动物的。

examples.english: The playground is [mainly] for little kids.
examples.chinese: 这个游乐场[主要]是给小孩子玩的。

meanings.explanation: A [location] is a particular place or position where someone or something is situated.

examples.english: My school is in a very quiet [location].
examples.chinese: 我的学校在一个非常安静的[位置]。

examples.english: We found a good [location] for our picnic.
examples.chinese: 我们找到了一个野餐的好[地方]。

examples.english: Can you tell me the [location] of the library?
examples.chinese: 你能告诉我图书馆的[位置]吗？

meanings.explanation: A [location] is a place away from a studio where a film or television programme is made.

examples.english: The movie was filmed on [location] in a small town.
examples.chinese: 这部电影是在一个小镇[外景地]拍摄的。

examples.english: The actors worked on [location] for three weeks.
examples.chinese: 演员们在[外景地]拍摄了三周。

examples.english: The director chose a beach as the [location] for the scene.
examples.chinese: 导演选了一个海滩作为这个场景的[拍摄地]。

meanings.explanation: To [manufacture] something means to make it in a factory, usually in large quantities.

examples.english: This factory [manufactures] toy cars for children.
examples.chinese: 这家工厂[生产]儿童玩具车。

examples.english: The company [manufactures] shoes in many different colors.
examples.chinese: 这家公司[生产]多种颜色的鞋子。

examples.english: These chairs are [manufactured] from recycled wood.
examples.chinese: 这些椅子是用回收木材[制造]的。

meanings.explanation: The [manufacture] of something is the process of making it in a factory.

examples.english: The [manufacture] of paper requires many trees.
examples.chinese: 纸张的[生产]需要很多树木。

examples.english: This country is famous for the [manufacture] of electronics.
examples.chinese: 这个国家以电子产品[制造]闻名。

examples.english: Robots help in the [manufacture] of cars.
examples.chinese: 机器人帮助进行汽车[制造]。

meanings.explanation: [Justice] is the quality of treating people fairly and equally.

examples.english: A good teacher always treats all students with [justice].
examples.chinese: 好老师总是[公平]地对待所有学生。

examples.english: The referee showed [justice] by being fair to both teams.
examples.chinese: 裁判很[公正]，对两队都一样。

examples.english: My parents taught me the importance of [justice].
examples.chinese: 我父母教我[公平]待人很重要。

meanings.explanation: [Justice] is the system of laws and courts that decides what happens when someone breaks the law.

examples.english: The police caught the thief and brought him to [justice].
examples.chinese: 警察抓住了小偷，把他绳之以[法]。

examples.english: The bad man had to face [justice] for what he did.
examples.chinese: 那个坏人因自己的行为受到了[法律制裁]。

examples.english: Judges and lawyers work in the [justice] system.
examples.chinese: 法官和律师都在[司法]系统工作。

meanings.explanation: If something is [marginal], it is very small in amount or effect, and not large enough to be important.

examples.english: There was only a [marginal] increase in sales this year.
examples.chinese: 今年的销售额只有[微小的]增长。

examples.english: The difference between the two pictures is [marginal].
examples.chinese: 这两张图之间的差别[微乎其微]。

examples.english: She made a [marginal] improvement in her math test.
examples.chinese: 她的数学成绩有一点[微小的]提高。

meanings.explanation: If something is [marginal], it is at the edge or border of something, rather than in the center or main part.

examples.english: He sat in a [marginal] seat at the back of the room.
examples.chinese: 他坐在教室后面的一个[边缘]座位上。

examples.english: I always write [marginal] notes in my textbook to help me remember key points.
examples.chinese: 我总是在课本的[页边]写笔记，帮我记住重点。

examples.english: These wild flowers can grow on [marginal] land near the road.
examples.chinese: 这些野花能在路边[边缘的]土地上生长。

meanings.explanation: [Maturity] is the state of being fully grown or fully developed. It is often used to describe when a person, animal, or plant has finished growing and reached its full size or age.

examples.english: These apples will be sweet when they reach [maturity].
examples.chinese: 这些苹果到了[成熟]的时候就会很甜。

examples.english: Cats usually reach [maturity] at about one year old.
examples.chinese: 猫一般在一年左右就达到[成熟]。
